_comment: THE MANAGER'S CHECKLIST. Every work item in the CURRENT manager session's
scope, and the state of each.
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-01, verbatim in intent: 'every manager session
keeps a detailed checklist of work items in its scope (this may be updated
as work progresses and the workplan is adapted, eg an unforeseen blocker
that needs to be resolved to release the rest of the items) - and every
status update should start with the checklist, then summary of what has
been done (recently) and what's next.'
SO THE REPORTING CONTRACT IS FIXED: checklist -> recently done -> next.
In that order, every time. A status update that opens with a narrative is
not following this.
WHY IT LIVES IN THE REPO AND NOT IN A SESSION'S CONTEXT. Same reason as
MANAGER-LEASE.json and SESSIONS.json: it must survive its holder's DEATH
and be readable by a manager arriving COLD. A checklist held only in
context is lost exactly when a successor most needs it, and re-deriving it
costs the successor the hours that produced it.
IT IS ADAPTIVE, NOT A FROZEN PLAN. The directive is explicit that it
changes as work progresses -- an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved
to release the rest is a first-class edit, not a failure of planning. Add
the blocker as its own item, point the blocked items at it, and say so.
STATES ARE NEVER COLLAPSED. 'delegated' is not 'in progress' and neither is
'done'; 'blocked' names WHAT it waits on. Most importantly 'done' means
MERGED AND OBSERVED, while 'landed_unproven' means the code is in and its
effect has NOT been seen on the fleet -- the distinction this whole system
keeps paying for when it is skipped.
THE MANAGER DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE ITEMS. Operator-directed the same day:
'the manager session only manages and does not take even small items,
because that means they're not focused on what they're actually supposed
to be doing.' An item with owner 'manager' is a MANAGEMENT act (a merge, a
deploy, a lease heartbeat, a spawn), never a build.

states.landed_unproven: merged; effect NOT yet observed on the fleet
states.in_flight: a session is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on a named thing; see blocked_on
states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it

items.title: The ping duplicate IS real and measured; I archived the session fixing it and told the board it was not
items.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY READ `dropped` WITH 'THE DEFECT WAS NEVER DEMONSTRATED'. THAT WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. The session had already measured it from the live journals: 22:10:19.934 bridge drain tick STARTS, 22:10:21 trader-bot tick reads the SAME file and delivers it, 22:10:23.212 bridge POST returns and unlinks. Both drainers do read -> send -> unlink, so the file survives the whole POST; the bridge's POST took 3.28s against ~1ms on every other tick that day. The copies went to different BOTS because ict-telegram-bot started at 21:37:37Z, before the secret was set at 22:08:26Z, and _resolve_claude_bot() caches once per process. === WHERE MY REASONING FAILED: I read the operator's later 'nothing showed up in both feeds' as REFUTING the earlier 'sent to both channels'. It does not. The mechanism is INTERMITTENT BY CONSTRUCTION — a duplicate needs the winning drainer's POST to exceed the ~2s phase gap between two 5s ticks. Absence on later pings is what the mechanism PREDICTS. === AND THE DUPLICATE IS THE LESS SERIOUS HALF: when the race is won outright one copy is sent, but WHICH CHAT it lands in is decided by scheduler phase, and an operator cannot learn where to look for a channel picked at random. === #10695 reached the same mechanism independently and called it correctly ('predicts intermittent duplication rather than reliable doubling'). Two sessions, same finding, while I had told the board it was not real. === STATUS: #10694 is Tier-2 and stays DRAFT — it changes a live service's drain behaviour and needs ict-telegram-bot.service restarted after merge, which is an operator OK I do not have overnight. Three send-ping actions dispatched inside 15s and the MIDDLE run was cancelled: issue left open, zero comments, nothing anywhere saying the action never ran. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects a RUNNING job, but GitHub keeps only one PENDING run per concurrency group, so a third queued run cancels the second. ⚠️ THE ISSUE COMMENT IS THE ONLY RESULT SURFACE A PM-SIDE SESSION HAS, so 'silently dropped' is indistinguishable from 'still queued' — a session can wait forever on a run that is already dead. The test session's workaround was to dispatch strictly one at a time, which is exactly the sort of unwritten discipline that decays. Filed as BL-20260901-SYSTEM-ACTIONS-CANCELS-A-SUPERSEDED-PENDING-RUN-AND-COMMENTS-NOTHING-BACK-SO-A-DISPATCHED-ACTION-IS-SILENTLY-LOST.

items.title: Nine merges in three hours left four PRs conflicted on the same append-mostly register files
items.note: Resolved in practice by the manager-only PR pattern, now confirmed a SECOND time under live test: a PR touching only MANAGER-LEASE.json / MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json / SESSIONS.json has an empty conflict surface (all three are manager-written), so it never serializes against a sibling. #10728 merged mid-queue with #10679 open and #10679 stayed clean; verified again by diffing every open train branch. It is also nearly free to verify — 5/5 green in 76s. landed_unproven, not done: this holds only while I am the sole writer of those three files. A second concurrent manager would break the premise, which is exactly what the lease exists to prevent. ⚠️ ITS PREMISE WAS REFUTED 2026-09-03T12:4xZ, AND THAT IS THE MORE USEFUL RESULT. The row claims a manager-only PR has an EMPTY conflict surface because the manager is the sole writer of MANAGER-LEASE / MANAGER-CHECKLIST / SESSIONS.json. Measured on the real merge of origin/main into the manager branch: MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json CONFLICTED — MI-96, MI-97 and MI-98 were added on BOTH sides with different content, and the merge driver correctly REFUSED to auto-resolve them. SESSIONS.json also diverged (main had minted the -2/-3 registry_keys my branch lacked). THE CAUSE IS NOT A SECOND MANAGER — the lease held all day and there was exactly one. It is that SUB-SESSIONS WRITE THE CHECKLIST TOO: #10918, #10923 and #10916 each carried checklist edits for their own rows. So the sole-writer premise was never true, and the row's stated risk ('a second concurrent manager would break it') names the wrong mechanism. The pattern's PRACTICAL value survives — the conflicts were row-level and the driver plus one hand-merge cleared them — but it must not be described as an empty conflict surface. Stays landed_unproven with the premise corrected rather than being marked done on a claim that has now failed.

items.title: The Data Explorer serves the live journal to anyone on the public Caddy host
items.note: ⚠️ TOP ITEM FOR THE MORNING REPORT, ABOVE THE RETIREMENT DECISIONS. Surfaced by session_01LvzsinECH8HP in #10687 and then MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MANAGER rather than taken on report — plain curl, no Authorization header, from outside the VM against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org : /api/bot/db/table/trades -> HTTP 200, total 5,318 · order_packages -> 200, 4,275 · balance_snapshots -> 200, 29,892. NEGATIVE CONTROL: device_tokens -> HTTP 404, so #10682's exclusion genuinely holds and the probe can distinguish a refusal from a serve. The filing session counted `signals` at 2,301,022 rows. === WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A CODING ERROR: CLAUDE.md justifies the Data Explorer as Tier-1 on the premise 'no secrets in either DB' — a claim about CREDENTIALS, not about the CONFIDENTIALITY of the trading record. That judgement was made while the API sat on a firewalled IP reachable only server-side by Streamlit. Caddy was then added (2026-08-13) so the browser-direct Svelte SPA could reach the API over HTTPS, and NOBODY RE-DERIVED THE TIER DECISION AFTER THE TRANSPORT CHANGED. The route did not become less safe; the world became able to reach it. === HONEST SEVERITY, in the direction that does not overstate: this is a CONFIDENTIALITY exposure, NOT a control path. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound values and schema-validated identifiers; nothing writes, no order can be placed, and no credential is reachable now that device_tokens is excluded. Nobody's money can be moved with it. What is exposed is the operator's complete trading record — every trade, order package and balance snapshot. === ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED TONIGHT, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Gating a live public read route is Tier-2, and the Data Explorer tab of the Svelte SPA reaches this route BROWSER-DIRECT, so adding a bearer would break a working operator surface. Doing that unannounced at 02:00 while the operator sleeps trades a three-week-old read exposure for a broken dashboard they wake up to. The options worth putting to them: leave it (the record is not secret), gate it behind DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN and teach the SPA to send one, or put Caddy basic-auth in front of /api/bot/db/* only. === ⚠️ THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOW BOUNDED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REASONING — the manager probed the same public host unauthenticated for anything WRITEABLE or PRIVILEGED and every gate refused: POST /api/bot/prop/report (the one route that writes the journal) -> HTTP 401 'missing authorization', confirming its documented FAIL-CLOSED behaviour; GET /api/pnl -> 401 and GET /api/status -> 401, so require_session is genuinely enforced on both session-gated routes; GET /api/diag/version -> 401 without a bearer. SO: NO UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE EXISTS ANYWHERE on the public surface, and no privileged read. The exposure is exactly and only the Tier-1 READ surface. That is what makes 'confidentiality, not control' a measured statement rather than a hedge, and it is why this can wait for the operator rather than being fixed unilaterally overnight. === Incidental confirmation worth keeping: this independently verifies CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-13 correction that require_session enforcement IS live on /api/pnl and /api/status — an earlier version of that row said 'issuance only', which was stale in the dangerous direction. Field now matches comment.

items.title: The standing 'scheduled workflows here never fire' assumption is FALSE, and the truth is worse-shaped
items.note: ⚠️ THIS CONTRADICTS A STANDING ASSUMPTION THAT IS QUOTED IN AT LEAST THREE PLACES — OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON, the header comment of .github/workflows/work-digest.yml, and MI-03's own note — all of which tell a session that a correct cron here is not evidence it will run. MEASURED BY THE MANAGER 2026-09-02T01:50Z, repo-wide, event=schedule, n=30 completed runs: FIFTEEN DISTINCT WORKFLOWS FIRED ON CRON, 29 of 30 successful. Among them are probes AND due-list — the exact two the OI row says have never fired. === THE OI ROW'S OWN CLEARING CRITERION IS MET, and I ran the precise probe it specifies rather than a proxy: `actions_list` on probes.yml filtered to event=schedule returns total_count=1 — run #34, event `schedule` (NOT workflow_dispatch, which that row explicitly says does not count), conclusion success, created 2026-09-01T10:12:17Z on main. === ⚠️ BUT DO NOT SIMPLY CLEAR IT AND MOVE ON, BECAUSE THE REAL FINDING IS THE TIMING AND IT IS THE PART THAT AFFECTS THE OPERATOR. probes.yml declares `20 5 * * *` and fired at 10:12 — FOUR HOURS FIFTY-TWO MINUTES LATE. work-digest declares `20 2,6,10,14,18,22` (raised from `20 6`) and fired at 00:19, matching no slot. So the honest statement is NOT 'cron never fires' and NOT 'cron works' — it is CRON FIRES, HOURS LATE AND AT AN UNPREDICTABLE OFFSET. That is a THIRD state both existing claims collapse, and it is the one that matters for the 06:20 morning digest: the operator may get it mid-morning rather than on waking. === n=2 offsets is not a delay distribution and must not be quoted as one; what is established is that the offset is large and nonzero, not its size. ROUTE TO: session_01TASYv35o6XciFnMC9wmnHi, which is already investigating exactly this question and should own both the OI clearing and the corrected wording — clearing a monitoring row is an observation its clearer must have made, and that session will have the fuller picture including the 02:20Z slot.

items.title: A better explanation for the never-traded legs than 'long-horizon'
items.blocked_on: operator — the remedy is a Tier-3 disposition or a netted-symbol arbitration policy
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. Found by backlog drain #3 (session_01JXBmVC) and it LANDS ON A NUMBER PHASE G MEASURED HOURS EARLIER AND COULD NOT EXPLAIN. Phase G: 12 of 52 enabled legs have never closed a trade, only 11 of 52 would EVER be gradeable at the n>=20 floor; its candidate explanation was 'retire them, or accept they are long-horizon'. Drain #3 supplies a third and better one. === MEASURED, population stated: over a 30.9-day overlap window (2026-08-02T02:27:21Z -> 2026-09-02T00:40:22Z, 805 order packages / 508 closed trades — the window where BOTH diag tables are complete under their 1000-row cap), there were 352 unfilled decisions, ALL attributed, ZERO residual. 163 were `all_accounts_noop`, of which 106 `flip_suppressed_hold_policy` and 56 `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` — both DELIBERATE POLICY. Then the deciding test: 141 of 163 (86.5%) were raised while a position in that (account_id, symbol) was ALREADY OPEN, and in every named pairing THE HOLDER IS A DIFFERENT STRATEGY LEG. So a low fill rate on these legs is not lost opportunity — it is a second leg correctly denied a symbol another leg already owns. === THE SHARPEST CASE, filed as PB-20260902-MGC-TREND-1H-IS-LIVE-AND-STRUCTURALLY-CANNOT-TRADE: `mgc_trend_1h` is execution:live and enabled:true with 95 decisions, ZERO fills, ZERO closed trades since 2026-07-26. 55 of 55 of its suppressions were raised while MGC was already open on ib_paper, held ALWAYS by a sibling (ict_scalp_mgc_15m 48, mgc_pullback_1d 7) and NEVER by itself, because it has never held a position. Union-of-intervals occupancy of (ib_paper, MGC) is 73.3%. Three legs share one netted position on one account WITH NO ARBITRATION BEYOND FIRST-COME — which leg trades MGC is decided by arrival order rather than any policy anyone chose. === WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A DEAD LEG: a leg cannot accrue the evidence its own kill-gate demands if a sibling owns the symbol 73% of the time. The M7 gate is therefore not merely under-powered (MI-06) — it is grading legs that were never given the chance to trade. === ⚠️ TWO LIMITS I AM NOT CROSSING. (a) This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE, which arbitrates one symbol across ACCOUNTS; this is contention among legs on the SAME account and symbol. Do not conflate them when fixing. (b) 'Structurally cannot trade' is established for mgc_trend_1h on 95 decisions with zero residual; whether it GENERALISES to the other 11 never-closed legs is UNMEASURED and must not be carried as if it were.

items.title: 17.2% of closed rows store a stop on the wrong side of entry; expectancyR reaches +206.9
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. PB-20260821-R-AND-DOLLARS-DISAGREE-IN-SIGN was REFUSED by drain #3 rather than closed, and the refusal is the right call — its criteria split, the real-money limb PASSES (n=28, +$18.40, +44.840R, rCoverage 1.000) and the plausible-bound limb FAILS HARD. Closing on the limb that passed would be exactly the sign-flip-by-choice-of-population failure this repo has already paid for. === THE ROW GOT WORSE, and its mechanism is now proven rather than inferred: it reasoned from ONE trade (4824) that trades.stop_loss holds the CURRENT TRAILED stop rather than the initial one. Direct test over closed rows with pnl NOT NULL (n=477): 82 carry a stored stop on the WRONG SIDE OF ENTRY — impossible for an initial stop — i.e. 17.2%, against the row's n=1. items.title: The trainer relay is issue-driven, and a sub-session's issue_write is 403
items.note: MERGED as 7b95451c (#10736) — .github/workflows/trainer-diag-relay.yml, the third push-triggered relay beside pr-opener and board-post. I reviewed the WORKFLOW rather than its description, since it opens an SSH path. Findings: the SSH target is vars.TRAINER_VM_IP defaulting to the trainer's hardcoded IP and is NOT caller-controlled (the request file is the SCRIPT, not the host); permissions are contents:write only; push does not fire from forks so it is gated to accounts that could already edit any workflow and use any secret. It REJECTS the `cmd:` parser shape by citing FIVE documented truncation bugs in the existing issue relay — including one where the truncated prefix STILL RAN and returned plausible output at exit 0 — and a file has no ambient YAML, so that whole class is unreachable. Concurrency is keyed on github.sha so no request is ever dropped, citing the bug where a coarser key silently discarded a burst; that is MI-19's shape avoided by construction. ⚠️ And it describes its own scope tripwire HONESTLY as an accident guard and NOT a security boundary — 'anyone who can trigger this workflow can push, and push access already permits editing this file' — which is the framing that made me willing to merge it. ⚠️ landed_unproven: the relay has never been exercised end to end. items.title: A sub-session's 'I'll stay available' is a hand-off nothing can act on
items.note: MEASURED TWICE TONIGHT, and the second time it cost a real hand-off. The merge-train sub-session (session_01CKcZFm) ended its turn IDLE at 01:46:45Z with post_turn_summary 'staying available to re-resolve as manager merges' — an explicit offer to be re-invoked. When two of its PRs needed exactly that re-resolve, the manager tried `SendMessage` to it and got: **'No agent named session_01CKcZFm... is reachable. Use ListAgents to see everyone you can message.'** `ListAgents` lists only in-process agents and local sessions; a CCR cloud sub-session appears in NEITHER direction. === SO 'STAYING AVAILABLE' IS A DEAD END THAT READS AS A HAND-OFF. That session was holding full context on two conflicted PRs — which files, which resolution rule, what it had already tried — and NONE of it was reachable. The manager had to spawn a fresh session (session_015oCrkh) and re-supply everything it already knew. It worked, but the duplicated context is the cost, and the operator has said that cost is acceptable — which is not the same as it being invisible. === ⚠️ THIS IS THE COORDINATION LIMIT THE OPERATING-MODEL DESIGN ALREADY NAMES, observed live: 'a session that dies cannot run its own close-out', so state must be written to the WORK OBJECT as work happens rather than held in a session that expects to be woken. An IDLE session is the same case as a dead one for this purpose — the design's three mechanisms (incremental progress, a lease per session, a reaper) are the answer, and none of them is 'message it again'. === TWO THINGS A FUTURE MANAGER SHOULD DO DIFFERENTLY: (1) never write a spawn prompt that invites a session to idle and await follow-up — tell it to finish, write its state down, and stop; (2) do not read `post_turn_summary: staying available` as an owner. It is not one. The row is `queued` rather than filed to a backlog because the fix is a change to how sessions are SPAWNED and how hand-off state is RECORDED, which is operating-model work, not a bug in a file. === RE-TESTED 2026-09-02T04:15Z AND IT HOLDS, with a sharper statement. Every running sub-session's CCR record advertises `cross_session_inbound: "available"`, which reads as a capability. ListAgents from this manager returns 'No reachable agents — no other Claude session is running on this machine right now'. So the field describes a CCR-side inbound path, not this session's peer graph, and a manager reading it would conclude it can message a sub-session when it cannot. That is the same unprovenanced-output shape MI-27 and MI-36 are about, one layer up in the tooling. Practical consequence, hit tonight: #10739 needed a fix, its author was ALIVE and self-reported review_ready, and I could not tell it — I had to post a PR comment and hope it reads it.
items.correction: 2026-09-02: MI-32'S CONCLUSION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It recorded that an idle cloud sub-session is unreachable, and that was true of the mechanisms it TESTED (SendMessage / ListAgents, which do not enumerate or address cloud sessions from this manager). It generalised from those two to 'unreachable', and that generalisation cost a full archive-and-respawn cycle on MI-37 and nearly cost another here. A SESSION-BOUND ROUTINE IS A WORKING CHANNEL. create_trigger with persistent_session_id (no cron, no run_once_at -- a poke-only Routine) followed by fire_trigger delivers a prompt into a specific existing session. MEASURED 2026-09-02T05:35Z on session_01PcirVtpMXJGiKm2548nkrR (the MI-39 fix session, which had gone idle mid-task without pushing): immediately before the fire it read session_status=SESSION_STATUS_IDLE / connection_status=disconnected; immediately after, SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING / connected, same session id, context intact. Trigger trig_01NcP7PmwUeFPCbRN4G61VQX. ⚠️ ONE REAL LIMIT, DO NOT OMIT IT WHEN USING THIS: the tool warns that a Routine created this way stores no MCP connectors, so THE FIRED TURN RUNS WITHOUT mcp__* TOOLS. A poked session keeps Bash/git/file tools and therefore keeps the pr-opener and board-post relays, but loses mcp__github__* outright. That is fine for a sub-session that already 403s on GitHub writes and works through the relays; it is NOT fine for one that needs the GitHub MCP to finish. ⚠️ AND THIS IS NOT A REPLY CHANNEL: the poked session cannot answer back. It is a one-way wake, so the manager still learns the outcome from the branch, the PR, or get_session -- never from a message. THE MANAGER LESSON: an idle sub-session is a RESUMABLE session, not a dead one. Poke it before archiving; a respawn duplicates context and loses whatever the idle session already worked out.

items.title: The merge-ordering protocol, learned by getting it wrong three times in one night
items.note: Written into #10728 and then PROVEN under live test the same hour. The rule: resolve one → merge it → resolve the next against the NEW main. Batch-resolve-then-batch-merge cannot converge, because each merge invalidates every sibling resolve not yet landed — measured cost tonight was two wasted resolves on #10679. Under the protocol, four PRs merged in sequence with zero re-conflicts. TWO refinements learned in the doing and worth keeping: (1) a manager-only PR is the standing EXCEPTION — its conflict surface is empty, so it merges at any point in the queue without disturbing an in-flight sibling (#10728 merged while #10679 was open and #10679 stayed clean). (2) GitHub returns mergeable_state:'unknown' for up to a minute after each merge; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/<branch>` answers immediately and authoritatively, so do not idle on the API. ⚠️ landed_unproven rather than done: it has survived one queue. It has not yet been tested against a queue containing two PRs that genuinely touch the same file. ⚠️ THE TEST IT ASKS FOR IS NOW SET UP AND HAS NOT YET RUN — do not read this as verified. The row wants 'a queue containing two PRs that genuinely touch the same file'. As of 13:0xZ that exists: #10920 and the manager branch BOTH modify docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, both have merged main in, and both are clean locally. The evidence this row needs is the SEQUENTIAL MERGE — whether the second one re-conflicts after the first lands. Until both are on main this is a setup, not a result, and claiming otherwise would be exactly the 'a merge is not a deploy' error the register is full of. ⚠️ ONE THING ALREADY LEARNED FROM THE SETUP: the protocol's 'only position 1 rebases' rule is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT here, because GitHub cannot merge a register conflict at all — see MI-94's client-side finding — so the queue also needs someone with an armed clone at each step, which the written protocol does not currently say. ✅ THE TEST RAN 2026-09-03T13:28Z AND IT ANSWERED BOTH WAYS — which is worth more than a pass. #10920 merged to main (631bad18) at 13:28Z. The manager branch is the second PR and BOTH modify docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, so this is the 'two PRs that genuinely touch the same file' case the row was waiting for. Measured immediately after, on the same commit pair, twice: WITH the merge driver (this clone is armed) `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` returns CLEAN — the second PR did NOT re-conflict once the first landed, which is the protocol's claim, verified. WITHOUT the driver (`-c merge.jsonregister.driver=false`, i.e. what GitHub's servers see) the SAME pair CONFLICTS on that file, three stages listed. ⚠️ SO THE PROTOCOL IS CONFIRMED AND ITS WRITTEN FORM IS INCOMPLETE. 'Only position 1 rebases' is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: it prevents siblings invalidating each other's resolves, and it does nothing about the fact that GitHub cannot merge a register conflict AT ALL. The queue therefore also needs SOMEONE WITH AN ARMED CLONE at each step, and the written protocol does not say so. That is not a theoretical gap — it is exactly why #10920 sat dirty with its author idle, and why the 7 reconcile-open-prs PRs of MI-103 cannot self-heal. ⚠️ AND IT RETROSPECTIVELY EXPLAINS MI-20: the manager-only pattern never worked because the conflict surface was empty (it is not — sub-sessions write the checklist). It worked because the DRIVER resolves row-level register conflicts. Same mechanism, different and correct explanation.

items.why_not_spawned_yet: Two sub-sessions cannot share one git working tree: they would fight over checkouts and `git add -A` from either can sweep the other's uncommitted files into the wrong branch — a hazard that already nearly bit this session, whose `git status` surfaced the AVAX agent's in-progress test file on an unrelated workflow branch. Agent worktree isolation was ATTEMPTED and REFUSED here: 'Cannot create agent worktree: not in a git repository' — the session's cwd is /home/user while the repo is /home/user/Metis-Insights. So this waits for the AVAX sub-session to finish, or goes to a cloud session with its own container (create_session), which must be REGISTERED IN SESSIONS.json in the same action.
items.risk_is_real_but_not_imminent: Firing requires the VM-local gitignored ledger to be LOST (re-provision / re-clone / fresh data dir). It is not on a timer. So deferring is defensible; leaving a false owner on it was not.

items.title: The docs/skills/workflow restructure was diagnosed, never put in a plan, and quietly did not happen
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02. The operating-model design diagnosed a 403k-token instruction surface as a root cause and the eight-phase build plan (A-H) contained NO phase for reducing it. So it was never scheduled and never happened. Re-measured today it is WORSE, not better: CLAUDE.md 430,453 bytes (~119k tok, was ~105k -- +13% in ONE DAY), ROADMAP.md 648,407 (~180k), ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL 168,495 (~46k), CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 99,222 (~27k), OPEN-ITEMS.json 191,955 (~53k, was ~42k, +26%). Total mandatory ~425k tokens against ~403k at diagnosis. The API + env-var + diag reference tables are 330,333 of CLAUDE.md's 430,453 bytes -- 77% -- and are lookup material, not boot reading. 32 skills, none split or retired; nothing owns DISPOSE, which is the MEASURED CONSTRAINT. 129 workflows, 21 with a schedule. OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-02, verbatim intent: 'our work plan needs to include completely implementing the plan that we made for the workflows. This is exactly how things are falling through the cracks unacceptable... We shouldn't have gotten to backlog [drain] before we did this much more basic part of implementing the plan.' AND the clarification that corrects a misreading of mine: the ask is NOT for actions that INVOKE Claude -- it is for ACTIONS CLAUDE CAN INVOKE TO SAVE TOKENS, e.g. pulling data. I answered the wrong question by measuring 'does any workflow invoke claude-code-action' (zero, true but irrelevant).
sub_items: A. TOKEN-SAVING ACTIONS CLAUDE INVOKES (the operator's actual ask, highest value) -- enumerate the recurring things a session does by hand that a workflow could return in one call, and build them. Known concrete cost measured THIS session: PR-CI polling. api.github.com is 403 from the sandbox so a session cannot write a bash poller, and this manager spent dozens of MCP pull_request_read calls waiting on suites. Others to enumerate, not assume: batched diag pulls, one-call PR state (mergeable_state + checks + threads), journal/DB reads that currently cost several relay round trips.

B. SPLIT THE INSTRUCTION SURFACE -- move the 330KB of API/env/diag reference out of CLAUDE.md behind an index a session reads on demand. CLAUDE.md is the ONLY surface that reaches a session before it acts (hooks do not run on Claude Code on the web), so what stays must be what changes behaviour, not what answers a lookup.

C. SKILLS vs THE FIVE SESSION TYPES -- map the 32 skills onto CYCLE/PRODUCE/DISPOSE/BUILD/OPERATE. Nothing owns DISPOSE today and that is the measured constraint; PRODUCE-without-DISPOSE is the 256-of-370-unread defect.
D. WORKFLOW INVENTORY -- 129 workflows: which are retained, retired, or created. Includes the dead-Routine cleanup (routines that look armed and are not).
items.note: SEQUENCING, per the operator: this goes AHEAD of backlog drain. The one drain already dispatched (session_012Nk5tVpHfSHvYfRyN7BC5S, exit-head class) is allowed to FINISH -- a half-landed change is worse than either state -- but NO further drain is spawned until A-D are dispatched.
items.adjudicated_2026_09_06: BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION, not a verdict on the work. State read `in_flight` with owner `None`, which a LIVE list_sessions read on 2026-09-06T08:0xZ graded NO_OWNER (population: 180 sessions enumerated back to 2026-08-02; exactly ONE was RUNNING and it was the manager). So the register asserted this was being worked while no worker existed. items.title: A manager spawns its own handoff manager, which pings the operator that it has taken over, with a link to itself
items.operator_ask: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'the possibility of the manager spawning its own handoff manager session at its own discretion - this requires that we be certain about continuity robustness, and the new session needs to send a ping that it has taken over with a link to itself.'
verified_today: SELF-IDENTIFICATION WORKS. get_session with session_id OMITTED returns the CALLING session's own record, id included (verified 2026-09-02T06:21Z from this manager: returned session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ). So a successor can build https://claude.ai/code/<its own id> without being told what it is -- which the spawning manager CANNOT pass in the prompt anyway, since the id does not exist until create_session returns.

THE PING CAN CARRY THE LINK TODAY. Read on main 2026-09-02: notify_on_pull._render_ping_message emits `title`, `summary` and `chat_url` from its recognised-key list. A takeover ping using those keys renders with its link. ⚠️ BUT `message` IS NOT IN THAT LIST -- a ping built with it renders as a BARE EVENT LABEL, which is exactly the empty 03:24 digest the operator screenshotted. The takeover ping MUST use recognised keys, or it announces nothing.
SPAWNING WORKS: 11 sub-sessions created this session via create_session with explicit source_url + source_revision.

THE LEASE ALREADY HAS THE HANDOVER PRIMITIVES: manager_lease.py has release + claim, and CLAIMABLE = {expired, released, absent}. A HELD lease REFUSES a claim, so the successor cannot simply take it -- the outgoing manager must release first, or the successor must --force with a reason.
proposed_protocol: 1. Outgoing SPAWNS the successor (create_session, explicit source_url+revision) and REGISTERS it in SESSIONS.json in the same action.
2. Outgoing RELEASES the lease and PUSHES it. An unpushed release protects nothing -- the successor reads origin.
3. Successor CLAIMS the lease, pushes, and PINGS with `title`+`summary`+`chat_url` naming itself.

4. ⚠️ OUTGOING DOES NOT EXIT YET. It polls the LEASE FROM ORIGIN -- the lease is the only shared state both sides can see, and there is NO back-channel (a woken session cannot reply; cross-session inbound does not reach back). When holder == successor, the handover is CONFIRMED and the outgoing stands down.

5. If nobody has claimed within a bounded window, the outgoing RE-CLAIMS (released is claimable by anyone, including the original) and reports a FAILED handoff. This step is the robustness the operator asked for: the outgoing must not disappear on the ASSUMPTION its successor is alive.
risks_named: ⚠️ THE GAP WINDOW IS THE REAL HAZARD. Between release and claim, NOBODY holds the lease while sub-sessions keep running -- the lease's own doc is explicit that sub-sessions do not depend on it and what pauses is SUPERVISION. If the successor dies at spawn (which happened TWICE tonight on MI-37, both times on repo provisioning), the system is left with running sub-sessions, no manager, and nobody aware. Step 5 exists for exactly this and is the part that must be proven, not assumed.

⚠️ A SUCCESSOR THAT CLAIMS AND THEN DIES IS WORSE THAN ONE THAT NEVER CLAIMED: the lease reads `held` for its full 90-minute TTL, so the time-based takeover that protects against death is precisely what delays discovery.

⚠️ CONTINUITY IS NOT PROVEN UNTIL MI-43 LANDS. 'Certain about continuity robustness' is the operator's own precondition, and today both handoff records (SESSIONS.json, OPEN-PRS.json) are maintained by REMEMBERING -- the mechanism that failed twice tonight at 3-of-6 and 6-of-9.

COST, as an independent argument FOR bounded manager sessions: this manager session has cost $885.84 with 1.31 BILLION cache-read tokens (read from its own get_session record, 2026-09-02T06:21Z). A manager that never hands over accumulates this indefinitely.

blocked_on.note: Still ordered behind MI-43 -- the readiness check should gate the handoff it is being tested with. If MI-43 is not landed when the handoff is due, run the handoff anyway and record WHICH criteria went unverified rather than claiming a clean pass.

items.note: QUEUED, NOT STARTED, and deliberately blocked behind MI-43. Building self-handoff before the readiness check exists would let a manager hand over a state nothing has verified -- which is the failure mode the operator's own precondition names.
items.operator_decision: 2026-09-02: THIS HANDOFF IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. Operator: 'we'll obviously test it on this handoff, so we can verify before closing here.' So MI-44 is no longer a deferred design -- it is exercised at THIS session's close, and the outgoing manager stays alive to observe it. That is the only way the protocol gets proven rather than asserted, and it matches the repo's own standard that a deploy is not an observation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The successor CLAIMS the lease: docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json on ORIGIN reads state=held with holder=<successor id>. Read from origin, never from a local tree.

2. The operator RECEIVES a takeover ping that RENDERS -- carrying a link to the successor. ⚠️ A ping that arrives as a bare event label is a FAILURE of this criterion, not a partial pass: that is the exact defect #10747 exists to fix, and `message` is not a recognised renderer key.

3. The successor demonstrates it can READ the handoff state it inherited -- naming the live sub-sessions from SESSIONS.json and the open PRs with their CONDITIONS from OPEN-PRS.json. ⚠️ Inheriting the files is not the test; USING them is. A successor that claims the lease and cannot say what #10746's staging condition is has failed, because that is the case where a half-informed manager is more dangerous than an ignorant one.
4. Only after 1-3 are OBSERVED does the outgoing manager stand down. If any fails, it RE-CLAIMS and reports the failed handoff rather than leaving the system unmanaged.
items.criterion_2_PROVEN:
VERIFIED 2026-09-02T06:24Z, ahead of the test rather than during it. Ran the REAL renderer (scripts/notify_on_pull.py::_render_event_body, on main) over two candidate takeover payloads:
  • title+summary+chat_url -> 3 lines, link PRESENT:
      'manager_takeover — Manager handover complete\n<summary>\nhttps://claude.ai/code/session_XXXX'
  • the same information under `message` -> 1 line, link ABSENT: 'manager_takeover'
CONCLUSION: the takeover ping WORKS TODAY on unfixed main and is NOT blocked on #10747 -- PROVIDED it is built with the recognised keys. Built with `message` it announces nothing, which would look like a successful silent handoff. This is a HARD REQUIREMENT for the successor's spawn prompt.
⚠️ METHOD NOTE, because the first attempt nearly produced a false finding: I initially guarded the call on a function name that does not exist, so BOTH arms returned None and read as 'the ping path is broken'. That is the `curl || echo '{}'` shape this repo files against its own diagnostics -- a probe that cannot find a positive reporting a confident negative. Caught only because both arms failing identically is implausible. A negative needs a positive control.
items.⚠️_state_corrected: Read `in_flight` with owner: null, which is a FALSE state -- nothing was working it. Corrected to `queued` on 2026-09-02. ⚠️ AND ITS SCOPE IS NOW PARTLY SUPERSEDED: the operator decided the same day that BOTH hops are MANUAL -- the manager sets off the night session itself (create_session, proven), and the operator sets off the morning one because they want to be there at the beginning. What survives of this item is NOT the spawn machinery but the BRIEF the successor is handed. See MI-74.

items.title: system-actions run 33604747877 failed at SSH — ~/.ssh/id_rsa absent on the runner
items.finding: Run 33604747877 (send-ping, target=claude) concluded FAILURE. Log: 'Identity file /home/runner/.ssh/id_rsa not accessible: No such file or directory' then 'ubuntu@141.145.193.91: Permission denied (publickey)' then 'notify_run.sh failed; transparency ping not delivered'. The post-action diag fetch failed the same way. EXIT_CODE and NOTIFY_EXIT_CODE were both EMPTY, which the workflow's own comment says means the action step never produced an exit code (pre-flight failure).
ruled_out: The SSH-key step is UNCHANGED: git log -L on lines 1082-1096 shows no edit since it was written.
VM_SSH_KEY is not obviously unset: the step exits 1 with an explicit ::error:: when it is, and that error is absent from the log.
Not input injection: DISPATCH_MESSAGE rides through `env`, not inline ${{ }} interpolation, so backticks/newlines in the body are safe.
Not a workflow regression from overnight: only #10683 touched system-actions.yml since the last good run, and it only added the ping classes.
items.still_unknown: WHICH earlier step failed. Only the last 200 of 674 log lines were read; the failing step is in the unread head. This is 'we did not look', NOT 'there was no cause'.
items.blast_radius: If SSH from Actions to the live VM is broken generally, EVERY VM-touching system-action is down: send-ping, set-env, get-env, pull-and-deploy, restart-bot-service, and sync-vm-secrets.yml.
items.note: I reported the first ping as 'queued'. Queued is not delivered, and it was not delivered. Re-dispatched with a short single-line body as the discriminating test.
items.PROVEN_2026_09_02T09_34Z: ⚠️ PROVEN BY OBSERVATION, not by test — and it is the FIRST thing today to earn that word. Run 33614797065, event=workflow_dispatch, head de3f0a19, conclusion=SUCCESS. AND the operator CONFIRMED RECEIPT of the ping it sent, with a screenshot. Both halves matter and neither alone would do: a `success` conclusion proves the workflow ran, and only the operator seeing the message proves it DELIVERED.
items.why_no_test_could_have_established_this: CI never dispatches this workflow, so the defect is unreachable from every required check. #10768 was GREEN on all four, reproduced its failure and its fix in both directions, and was still wrong. That is the whole lesson: a green suite over a path the suite does not exercise is not evidence about that path.
items.the_transferable_error: I read the failing step's TAIL, saw the lines around it already using ${x:-}, and fixed the one site the log pointed at. Sampling the visible evidence and treating it as the POPULATION. Seven bare refs sat in one contiguous block and each would have aborted the step IN TURN — fixing them one failure at a time would have cost seven dispatch cycles. ⚠️ It took a FAILED PROOF RUN to make me enumerate. The first fix's own verification (reproduced both directions, exact error matched) is precisely what made it convincing.

items.⚠️_what_PROVES_ITSELF_must_mean: The operator did not define it and a vague criterion is how a demo-only approval leaks to real money. I will NOT widen on any of: time elapsed, a quiet soak, or a green test suite. If they do not, the honest report is 'unproven, not proven-good', and widening to real money on an unexercised gate is NOT what the operator approved. Put that back to them rather than letting a quiet soak read as a pass.

Do not leave it stated that way.

(b) FLIP AND BREAK STREAMLIT — consistent with 'no work on it': if nobody is developing it, nobody is hurt by it breaking. But the operator said it 'can stay alive', which reads as wanting it usable, so this needs their explicit word.

(c) GATE ONLY WHAT STREAMLIT DOES NOT CALL — the middle path, and the only one that needs no further operator input to START. Cost: it is a measurement job (establish Streamlit's actual call set) and it leaves the job half-done by construction.

It is the only route that reduces the unauthenticated surface without needing the operator to choose between two things they have already implied they want (Streamlit usable AND the gate closed). ⚠️ But it is NOT free and not silent: establishing Streamlit's call set is real work on a codebase the operator just said not to work on — so the measurement is READ-ONLY (grep the SPA and streamlit_app.py for endpoint strings), never a change to it.

items.title: I asked seven decisions today as in-session popups and sent zero pings
items.operator_observation: 2026-09-02: 'I'm supposed to get a ping when there's a decision waiting for me, and I didn't get any pings about decisions waiting for me.' Correct.
items.measured: SEVEN decisions were put to the operator via in-session popups across this session (bybit arming · widening order · Phase-H route · handoff timing · #10694 restart · drain unblock · build the wiring). ZERO pings were sent announcing any of them.
items.why_it_matters_more_than_politeness: F6 — 'the operator is told, by Telegram, whenever something is done without them' — is the CONDITION ON WHICH THE AUTONOMY GRANT WAS MADE. A decision waiting is a checkpoint, and a checkpoint that only exists inside a session the operator is not looking at is not a checkpoint. ⚠️ It also compounds: the operator cannot answer what they cannot see, so an unpinged decision silently becomes a BLOCKED work item that looks like it is merely pending.
items.⚠️_the_channel_was_also_broken_but_that_: Both ping paths were down for part of today (renderer dropping bodies until #10747; workflow_dispatch dead until #10772, still unmerged). But the ISSUE-driven path worked THROUGHOUT and I used it for status pings — so I could have pinged the decisions and did not. Do not let the channel outage absorb this.
remedy: IMMEDIATE, behavioural: every AskUserQuestion is followed by a ping naming the decisions and carrying the session link. Done for today's seven (issue #10774).
DURABLE: the mechanism belongs with MI-55 — a decision in the work store should ping on its own, not depend on the manager remembering.
items.note: ⚠️ RECURRED TODAY AND THE OPERATOR CAUGHT IT, not me — they asked directly 'why aren't those decisions being sent to the bot?' MEASURED IMMEDIATELY AFTER, and the answer is NOT that the channel is broken: GET /api/bot/work/decisions returns HTTP 200 with one real request, the ClaudeBot poller is heartbeating (pid 440663, prefix wdec), and the operator's own screenshots show /status rendering as ONE message with expandable sections and /decisions pulling the full question body with its options. THE CHANNEL WORKS. I simply was not using it — every item I reported as 'waiting on you' was in a chat transcript and none was declared as a decision_requests[] block, so the sweep had nothing to send. That is this row's exact diagnosis, reproduced across a whole day. ⚠️ AND MY FIRST PROBE OF IT WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: I called the route through scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh, which prefixes /api/diag/, got a 404, and was one step from reporting 'the decision route is not deployed' — a false infrastructure finding that would have sent someone hunting a deploy problem that does not exist. The script's own error text said 'check the path form' and I read past it. Corrected with a plain curl before it left the session. ✅ END-TO-END CONFIRMED 14:1xZ, and this is the first time this row has had evidence rather than a diagnosis. #10941 merged 14:03:59Z; ict-git-sync carried it; and a plain curl of GET /api/bot/work/decisions on the LIVE VM now returns 8 requests including DEC-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITION-POLICY on WO-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS-OWED with answerState: not_submitted. So the path repo -> main -> git-sync -> route -> ClaudeBot is intact and the failure really was that I never wrote the question down. ⚠️ AND A STALE CLAIM ON AN OPEN MONITORING ROW IS CORRECTED BY THE SAME READ: `writeGate.state` reads **open**, not `closed_no_token`. OI-20260901-DECISION-ROUNDTRIP-SHIPPED-AND-NO-DECISION-HAS-EVER-MADE-THE-ROUND-TRIP asserts as its clause (b) that 'DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN is UNSET on the live web-api as far as this session could establish, so the write route would serve 503 and writeGate.state reads closed_no_token'. That is measurably false now — the token IS set and an answer submitted from the UI would be ACCEPTED. That row's own text says if the operator decides NOT to set the token the row CHANGES rather than clears; the opposite happened and it needs the same treatment. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT CLEAR THE ROW: the round-trip still requires an answer to be submitted AND then observed as `committed` in the object YAML on main, and no decision has done that. Six requests read `committed` today, but those were committed by sessions editing the repo directly, NOT by an answer travelling through the route — which is the distinction that row exists to hold. ⚠️ THE STANDING RULE FROM THIS, and it is the whole lesson: an item is only 'waiting on the operator' once it is a decision_requests[] block on a work object ON MAIN. Reporting it in chat reaches nobody, and an object on an unmerged branch reaches nobody either — the route reads main.

items.title: stop-hook-git-check pressures the manager to commit a running sub-agent's in-flight source changes
items.observed: 2026-09-02, FOUR times in ~20 minutes. `~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh` fires 'There are uncommitted changes ... Please commit and push' whenever the working tree is dirty. It has no notion of WHOSE changes those are. Every firing today was on a live sub-agent's work, not mine — my branch was in sync with origin each time.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: ⚠️ NOT a tidiness issue. The dirty paths were config/instruments.yaml, src/units/accounts/execute.py, src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py, precision.py, instrument_profile.py, profile_loader.py and two test files — a live, unreviewed, ORDER-PATH-ADJACENT change. Committing them would have (a) put unreviewed order-path code into a PR about recording operator decisions, and (b) taken the work out from under a running agent that had not finished or tested it.
items.root_cause: One git working tree, two writers. The hook assumes a single writer per checkout. It is correct for that case and actively harmful for this one. The manager's own `git checkout` compounds it: it does not move an agent's uncommitted files aside, it DRAGS them onto whatever branch the manager lands on.
what_actually_prevents_it: Sub-sessions in their OWN CONTAINER (create_session) rather than in-process agents — used for MI-53 today, and the reason it was used.

Agent worktree isolation — ATTEMPTED today and REFUSED: 'Cannot create agent worktree: not in a git repository', because the session cwd is /home/user while the repo is /home/user/Metis-Insights. Spawning with the repo as cwd would likely fix it; UNVERIFIED, do not assert it.
NEVER `git add -A` while any agent shares the tree. Explicit paths only. This is the discipline that saved it today after the first near-miss.
items.the_honest_residual: ⚠️ The hook is not wrong to fire — it cannot know. So this is not 'fix the hook to be quiet'; a hook that learned to ignore dirty trees would stop catching the case it exists for. The fix is on the SPAWN side: agents should not share a tree. Recorded so the next manager does not resolve four hook warnings by committing someone else's work.

items.title: The open-PR handoff record can never read clean, because the PR that maintains it is itself an open PR
items.observed: handoff_check's open_prs check FAILS in both directions by construction. Every open PR must have a row (recorded - observed_open -> stale_row; observed_open - recorded -> unrecorded). The PR that maintains the rows is itself an open PR, so it needs a row, and merging it makes that row stale. MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-02: #10775 merged (d08cac48) about NINETY SECONDS after a branch recorded a row for it -- the row was correct when written and stale before the PR carrying it could open. The manager then pruned it and opened #10777, whose own row went stale on merge (cd8554fa). Two full iterations of the loop, observed, not argued.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing. There is no compliant sequence: the gate cannot read `ready` on the merge that closes it. Restating the regress in each PR body -- which is what happened twice -- documents the trap without removing it, and the operator correctly named that as the failure: a structural fix was needed, not a better description.
items.root_cause: TWO, and only the second is the terminator. (1) TWO POPULATIONS CONFLATED UNDER ONE KEY: open_prs[] holds both an in-flight CLAIM (this PR is open, here is its owner and blocker) and the durable DECISION RECORD (what the operator actually said, verbatim). Only the first should be graded against the live open list; the second is HISTORY and is MORE load-bearing after the merge than before -- #10746's conditional Tier-2 approval (bybit_1 demo only, real-money bybit_2 accepted as exposed) is precisely what a successor must not lose. So 'pruning a stale row' DELETES decision knowledge in order to satisfy a freshness rule: the same shape as the OPEN-ITEMS cap that instructed a session to EVICT a valid row, which CLAUDE.md already records as a failure. (2) A COMMIT CANNOT RECORD ITS OWN MERGE. Whatever writes a row's terminal state must run OUTSIDE the commit being merged, and nothing did.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Four parts, spawned as MI-57. (A) SPLIT THE FILE: open_prs[] graded against live, settled_prs[] never compared -- pruning becomes a MOVE, so knowledge is preserved and the freshness check keeps its teeth. (B) A POST-MERGE RECONCILER on push:main that moves a row whose PR is no longer open into settled_prs[] stamped with terminal/merge_sha/observed_at. Running outside the merging commit is what terminates the regress. (C) grade_completeness reads only open_prs[]; a NEW finding fails a settled_prs[] row with terminal=closed_unmerged and no disposition, because an abandoned PR with no stated reason IS real lost knowledge. (D) A DEAD RECONCILER MUST BE VISIBLE: if a stale row exists AND last_reconciled_sha != current main sha, the message says the RECONCILER has not run -- a different finding from a session forgetting, never collapsed into stale_row. (E) MEASURED CONSTRAINT ON (B), recorded here AND relayed. ⚠️ THIS ROW SAID 'a manager CANNOT message a running sub-session' AND THAT WAS WRONG -- do not re-quote it. The true statement is narrower: SendMessage/ListAgents do not ADDRESS cloud sessions from a manager container (measured -- SendMessage to the session id returned 'No agent named ... is reachable'), and the manager generalised from those two tools to the capability. A session-bound Routine DOES reach it: create_trigger with persistent_session_id set and BOTH cron_expression and run_once_at omitted, then fire_trigger. Two limits travel with it -- the fired turn runs WITHOUT mcp__* tools (so never tell it to pull a job log; quote the log INTO the prompt), and it is ONE-WAY, so the outcome is read from the branch/PR/get_session and never as a reply. The constraint below is therefore BOTH a relayed instruction and a review criterion on the draft PR: `main` is branch-protected and a direct push is REJECTED -- I tried one for this very commit and got `GH006 ... 3 of 3 required status checks are expected`. The repo already solved this: `.github/actions/commit-to-main` lands a change via a PAT-authored auto-merge PR with `verify-merged: true`, whose own comment records BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE (a direct push rejected, rows SILENTLY dropped, the $10 spend gate defeated). ⚠️ THAT CREATES THE REGRESS FROM THE OTHER SIDE: the reconciler's own landing PR is an open PR and would itself need a row. The resolution is a TYPED exclusion -- bot author AND `automation/` head-branch prefix, BOTH, never either -- which is categorically different from the rejected exemption: an automation landing PR carries no owner session, no intent and no operator decision, i.e. none of the three things this record exists to carry, so its absence cannot hide a forgotten human decision. A bare 'skip bots' is WRONG and must fail a test: a Claude-opened PR is bot-authored in the API sense and must still require a row.
items.the_honest_residual: The fix depends on a workflow actually firing, and this repo has a documented history of machinery that looks armed and is not -- probes.yml and due-list.yml at zero scheduled runs, two Claude Routines enabled:true with next_run_at 0001-01-01. That is exactly why (D) exists: the failure mode is not 'the reconciler is wrong' but 'the reconciler silently stopped and stale rows read as a session's negligence'. Separately, the REJECTED fix must stay rejected: exempting the in-flight PR from the completeness check is byte-indistinguishable from the real failure the check exists to catch (a PR nobody recorded), and open_pr_record.py's own docstring says so. And the residual open_pr_record.py already names is untouched -- an author writing verdict:approved where conditions were in fact given is undetectable from inside the repo, because this file IS the record. AND the manager initially believed (E) could not be relayed at all, which was FALSE and is corrected above -- the wrong belief came from generalising two tools' addressing limits into a capability claim, which is the same unprovenanced-inference shape this repo keeps filing. It was relayed by a session-bound Routine. What remains genuinely one-way is the RETURN path: the sub-session cannot answer, so a relayed constraint is a broadcast and the manager still learns whether it landed only by reading the branch. A constraint that must be ACKNOWLEDGED still has no channel.
items.adjudicated_2026_09_06: BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION, not a verdict on the work. State read `in_flight` with owner `session_01T8iWSepqAuBU7sgbs8GPHu`, which a LIVE list_sessions read on 2026-09-06T08:0xZ graded IDLE (population: 180 sessions enumerated back to 2026-08-02; exactly ONE was RUNNING and it was the manager). So the register asserted this was being worked while no worker existed. items.title: Work-decision prompts are answerable only on the trader bot, because nothing polls the dedicated Claude bot
items.tier: 2 (a live service gains a polling loop; no order path)
items.observed: Operator direction 2026-09-02, on seeing the first live prompt: 'that's supposed to be showing up in Cloudbot. Right? Not on the trader one, the decisions.' Correct. #10778 (merged 133587f1) routes prompts to the TRADER bot via telegram_decisions.answerable_route(), deliberately NOT claude_route(). Measured in that PR: the trader token is polled by ict-telegram-bot.service with a CallbackQueryHandler; the prop token is polled by ict-claude-bridge.service despite its name; TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is polled by NOTHING. The operator DOES receive pings on ClaudeBot (an OPS deploy ping landed there at 10:11Z and they screenshotted it), which is exactly the distinction: sending needs only a token, a BUTTON needs a polling process to collect the callback_query.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated. The build's choice was correct given what exists -- pointing prompts at ClaudeBot today would have shipped DEAD BUTTONS THAT LOOK HEALTHY, which is strictly worse than the wrong-channel state, and the PR said so explicitly rather than picking claude_route() because the name matched. The gap is that only half the capability exists, not that the wrong half was built.
items.root_cause: DELIVERY AND ANSWERABILITY ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES and only the first was ever built for the Claude bot. OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN tracks the delivery half; nothing tracked the second, because until a button existed nobody needed the Claude bot to be polled. A channel that can be written to but not answered on reads as a working two-way channel from the operator's side right up until the first tap.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-58 builds BOTH halves in one PR, in order: (1) make the Claude bot genuinely polled with a CallbackQueryHandler wired to the SAME handle_decision_callback -- not a fork, one owner, so the route stays the single owner of every refusal; (2) only THEN point answerable_route() at it. Plus the state that makes a regression visible: a startup line naming which token is polled and whether a handler is attached, and a sweep HOLD with a WARNING when the answerable bot is not confirmed polled -- three states, never collapsed (polled_with_handler / token_only_not_polled / unknown), because 'the button rendered' and 'the button works' are otherwise indistinguishable from the operator's side.
items.the_honest_residual: A green harness cannot prove this: the done-condition is a real tap on ClaudeBot producing a work_decision_transit.jsonl row, which needs the operator. The trader-bot round-trip IS already proven end to end (2026-09-02T10:16:36Z, chosen=accept_ungated, submitted_by=telegram), so MI-58 changes WHERE it happens and must not be read as re-proving WHETHER it works. And if the VM's .env lacks TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET the build stops at a manager/operator action -- it must NOT be worked around, and must NOT reuse TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN, which drives the PROP bot.

items.note: ✅ LIVE READ 2026-09-03T13:19Z, and it moves this row — but read exactly what it proves. /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude returns present:true with a heartbeat at 13:19:07.321106Z, seconds old, carrying token_var=TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET, service=ict-claude-decision-bot, pid=440663, prefixes=['wdec']. /api/diag/services shows ict-claude-decision-bot.service ACTIVE. THREE THINGS FOLLOW, all measured rather than inferred: (1) TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET IS SET on the VM — a poller cannot resolve a token that is not there, so the Tier-2 set-env that OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION named as the one missing step has happened. (2) The dedicated bot is POLLED AND HANDLES `wdec`, which is the positive evidence telegram_poll_registry requires, so answerable_route() should now grade `polled_with_handler` and prefer ClaudeBot over the trader bot — the exact condition this row was filed against. (3) The heartbeat is a LIVE process claim that expires with the process, not a declaration, so it cannot be stale in the dangerous direction. ⚠️ WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, and this is the half that keeps the row open: no TAP has been observed. A poller that claims the prefix is not the same as a callback_query received and answered, and the last hop — WHICH CHAT the prompt appeared in — is observable only on the operator's phone, because in a DM the chat_id is the operator's own id for every bot by construction. So this clears the PLUMBING and not the DELIVERY. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO: the trader bot's own claim (telegram_poll_trader) lists prefixes ['propexp','wdec'], so BOTH bots handle wdec. That is the designed fallback, not a conflict — but it means a prompt landing on the trader bot would still be answerable, and therefore would NOT announce itself as mis-routed. Do not read a working tap as evidence of correct routing.

items.title: /status and /decisions — pull the status update and every waiting decision on demand, instead of only receiving them as they fire
items.tier: 2 (a live service gains command handlers; no order path)
items.observed: Operator ask 2026-09-02, immediately after the first decision round-trip closed: a /status command returning the status update 'with the checklist and everything', and a /decisions command so every still-unanswered decision 'can all pop up at once, in case I don't get them as they come in'. The second names a real gap the push channel cannot close by itself: a prompt that fires while the operator is away is not re-offered, and the periodic sweep deliberately asks ONCE per request (a per-process re-ask is BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART, which put 202 CRITICALs on the operator's channel). PULL is the correct complement to PUSH here, not a duplicate of it.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated; this is new capability. Worth recording is the SEQUENCING constraint the ask does not mention: a /command reaches only a bot some process is POLLING, exactly like a button, so on ClaudeBot these arrive WITH MI-58 and not before it. Building them against a hardcoded token would have created a second migration the moment MI-58 lands.
items.root_cause: n/a — a feature request. The dependency is structural: DELIVERY needs only a token, but a COMMAND and a BUTTON both need a polling process. MI-58 is what makes ClaudeBot satisfy that; MI-59 must not duplicate the decision.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Both commands register on telegram_decisions.answerable_route() -- the SAME resolver the prompts use -- so they work today on whatever bot is genuinely polled and follow MI-58 to ClaudeBot automatically, with no second migration and no operator decision required. /decisions reuses the sweep's own prompt/keyboard builder rather than a second copy, because two copies of the callback_data construction is how the 64-byte budget and the key-digest scheme drift apart. /status prints in the operator's required order (checklist -> recently done -> next) and STAMPS the sha it read plus whether the VM tree is behind main, three states never collapsed (synced / behind_main / unknown) -- measured today, the decisions route read `in_transit` for minutes after the answer was already committed to main, purely because the VM had not synced, so a confident status over a stale tree is a live failure mode and not a hypothetical. A truncated checklist must state how many items it omitted; a /decisions with nothing waiting must say so explicitly, because silence is indistinguishable from a broken command.
items.the_honest_residual: A green harness proves none of it: the done-condition is the operator typing each command and getting a correct reply, which needs them. Authorization is the sharper risk -- the repo is PUBLIC and the bot username is discoverable, so both commands expose internal state to anyone who finds the bot unless they answer only the operator's own chat; the spec requires reusing the existing handlers' auth notion rather than inventing a second one, and that is the thing to check hardest at review. And /status reads the MANAGER's checklist, which is only as honest as the manager keeping it -- a stale as_of will render as confidently as a fresh one, which the sha stamp mitigates but does not solve.

items.title: The decision round-trip ends in the repo and stops — the session that asked learns the answer only by polling
items.tier: 1 for the investigation; the build depends on what it touches. No order path either way.
items.observed: Operator ask on watching the first round-trip close: 'can we add a push on the end of that so that when the answer gets to the repo, it knows to push it to the session instead of waiting for the session to pull'. MEASURED against the machinery that shipped today: a decision request carries object_id, request_id, options, urgency and context -- and NOTHING identifying the session that asked. So there is currently no address to push to, whatever the transport turns out to be.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: n/a -- a feature request, and a well-aimed one. Phase H's own design says visibility is the enforcement mechanism this system has never had; a channel that carries a question outward and cannot carry the answer back to the asker is half of that.
items.root_cause: The round-trip was designed to make truth land in the REPO, which it does correctly. Delivery back to the ASKER was never in scope, so the asking session's identity was never recorded. That is a gap in the object schema before it is a gap in transport.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-60, and its FIRST deliverable is deliberately not code: a feasibility doc stating per claim what was TESTED versus READ FROM DOCUMENTATION. ⚠️ The manager made exactly this error today -- declared 'a manager cannot message a running sub-session' off ONE failed SendMessage, wrote it into a merged PR body and a checklist row, and it was FALSE. A session-bound Routine (create_trigger with persistent_session_id, no cron, no run_once_at, then fire_trigger) IS verified to wake a running session, observed 2026-09-02T10:12Z. The genuine unknown is whether an Actions runner can fire one -- it holds no mcp__* tools -- and the watch_url alternative has two limits that shape the design rather than decorate it: the watch dies with the session, and THIS REPO IS PUBLIC so a webhook URL committed to it is a published endpoint. Design constraints that hold whichever transport wins: record the asking session (smallest change, gates everything); the push must CARRY the answer because a fired turn cannot go fetch it; one-way, so nothing waits for an ack; three states never collapsed (pushed / session_gone / unknown); and PUSH ADDS TO PULL rather than replacing it.
items.the_honest_residual: session_gone is not an edge case -- a long question is exactly the kind whose asking session dies before the answer lands, so the fallback is the common path and the push is the optimisation. A push-only design would silently lose answers precisely when they matter most. And a green test proves nothing here: the done-condition is an OBSERVED wake -- a session idle before and running after, doing something attributable to the push.
items.note: || OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-02, dispatched to the session and recorded here because a decision that lives only in a transcript is the failure this build exists to end. THE 30-DAY CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN IS RULED OUT -- operator verbatim: 'we definitely can't have a flow that relies on my minting new tokens every month - but we also need to the 2 way flow here.' The REQUIREMENT STANDS; only that mechanism is dead, and the objection is to a human re-minting anything on a schedule, so a longer-lived token or a PAT is the same answer and is also ruled out. APPROVED SHAPE: C as the design (a blocking question ENDS the session and a fresh one is re-fired when the answer lands, so nothing must reach into a live session and nothing needs a credential to do it) - B as the mechanism (a standing cron Routine, fresh session per fire, hourly, draining committed decisions off /api/bot/work/decisions) - A as the fast path (session-bound Routine wake, PROVEN, used four times today). [!] C IS RIGHT AND NOT YET EARNED: it depends on the work object being resumable, which is Phase E, whose exit condition is 'killing a session mid-work loses nothing, DEMONSTRATED by killing one' and nobody has killed one. B is therefore the floor. [!] B IS THE SHAPE THAT HAS GONE INERT TWICE ON THIS ACCOUNT (Health Check Routine and Sprint Continue Work: enabled true, next_run_at 0001-01-01, never fired, still naming the pre-July repo name), so B IS NOT DONE WHEN THE ROUTINE EXISTS -- it is done when something WATCHES that it fired, via list_triggers.last_run. RULED OUT ON MEASUREMENT, not inference: watch_url mints a per-session inbound webhook at api.anthropic.com with no standing secret -- exactly the right shape -- and an unsigned POST returns 401; its sealed_secret is encrypted to the artifact service, so no GitHub workflow can ever sign a delivery. Probe created, POSTed, 401, unwatched.

The gap is that no check compares automation output against main. `claude-run-failure-alert` covers run failures, and whether it fired here is unestablished -- that is part of MI-62's brief and must be answered with a POSITIVE CONTROL, since 'it did not fire' and 'we could not show it can fire' are different findings.

items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-62, and its first job is a DISPOSITION PER BRANCH -- `superseded` (the content is on main by another route) / `lost` (it is not, and nothing regenerates it) / `unknown` (could not establish) -- checked against CONTENT, never the branch name. items.title: Operator cap: at most 3 concurrent work sessions, scale up only on measured feasibility
items.observed: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'I think we need to limit ourselves to 3 concuurent work sessions - 8 seems like too much for to handle reliably, so lets start small and scale up based on what we actually know is feasible', followed by 'LEt all the opne sessions close, but don't spawn new ones until 1 of the 3 slots is open'. So: no forced stand-downs, a spawn gate, and the number is provisional pending evidence.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated -- this is a new constraint. What it corrects is a manager habit: this session spawned freely because the declared ceiling was 8, and the binding constraint was never the ceiling. It is the OPERATOR'S capacity to follow what is in flight, which no register measured.
items.root_cause: THE CAP IN THE DESIGN COUNTS A DIFFERENT THING FROM WHAT THE OPERATOR CAPPED, and conflating them would silently break CI. The operating model's WIP ceiling of 8 counts in_flight WORK OBJECTS (docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml) and is enforced by scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py. The operator capped concurrent WORK SESSIONS. These are different registers with different populations: measured 2026-09-02 there are 4 in_flight objects and 2 RUNNING sessions. Lowering the OBJECT ceiling to 3 would fail CI immediately on the 4 in_flight phase objects, which is not what was asked and would block the build. The session cap is therefore applied to SESSIONS, and the object ceiling is left at 8 pending an explicit operator call.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: The manager does not spawn while the count is at or above 3. [!] THE COUNT IS ASSIGNED-AND-UNFINISHED WORK, NOT `SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING`. An idle session that still owes a PR is a thing the operator is tracking, and counting only RUNNING would have read 2 today while four sessions held open work -- the permissive reading, and the one that reproduces the condition the cap exists to end. [!] AND A list_sessions PAGE IS NOT A POPULATION: the read that established today's number returned 40 rows with has_more true, so a count taken from one page must say so.
items.the_honest_residual: NOTHING ENFORCES THIS YET -- it is a manager discipline, and the register that would make it checkable (SESSIONS.json) is the same one measured INCOMPLETE twice: MI-15 found 3 of 6 absent, and a later census found 26 of 55 sessions unregistered with 17 carrying this manager's own id as parent. So a cap counted over that register would under-count exactly when it matters. Making it enforceable is real work and is not done here. [!] THE NUMBER IS PROVISIONAL BY THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDING -- 'scale up based on what we actually know is feasible' -- so raising it needs evidence about handling capacity, not a busy week.

items.title: Claimed TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was unset from a doc row, over the operator's own contrary observation
items.observed: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'I really can't believe we're going back to this again, we already established that the channel works!!!! JUST WIRE THE PR TO RIGHT BOT!!!' They were right. The manager told them TWICE that TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was unset, and gated the ClaudeBot work on it, having never measured it. The claim came from OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN (dated the PREVIOUS day) and from #10789's body saying its author could not read the VM. Neither is a measurement.
items.root_cause: FIELD BEATS COMMENT, INVERTED. The operator had ALREADY shown a ping arriving on ClaudeBot earlier the same day and said 'got this'. That is a direct observation of the channel working, and it was weighed BELOW a dated doc row. This repo's first rule is that a doc is a CLAIM about the field and the field wins; an operator's own sighting is field evidence, not opinion.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: The blocker was asserted, not measured, so it was never a blocker to remove -- it was a claim to check. The correct action is the one the operator gave: wire and merge, and let the DEPLOY be the measurement. The new unit exits EX_CONFIG into a visible `failed` state if the var really is missing, so one deploy settles it at less cost than two rounds of argument.
items.the_honest_residual: IT IS STILL NOT MEASURED. get-env's ALLOWED_KEYS admits a key only when its VALUE is safe to publish, so a bot token is not readable that way, and presence-vs-value is a distinction that path does not expose. The honest state is UNMEASURED -- not 'set', and not 'unset'. Do not close this row on the argument being over; close it on the deploy.

items.root_cause: THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, and the reason the operating layer keeps not being used: it shipped its OBJECT half on 2026-09-01 -- store, intents, WIP ceiling, constraint readout, lease, checklist, cycle priority, sunset pass -- and NOT ONE ROLE PACK was updated to know it exists. Measured across all 32 SKILL.md files, case-insensitively: docs/claude/work 0 hits, 'work object' 0, WIP 0, blocked_on 0, CYCLE-PRIORITY 0, READOUT 0, PRODUCE/DISPOSE 0, SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS 0. The model's anti-silo mechanism is context = work object + role pack, and its two halves are wired to DIFFERENT SYSTEMS. A session handed a work object opens a role pack describing the pre-2026-09-01 world of three backlogs and DUE.md.
items.scope: IN: (a) wire the handful of role packs that govern how a session SITUATES itself -- the audit's 4.2 names them -- to the work store, the readout and the caps. (b) The 4 REPAIR workflows the audit evidences: replay-pregate-nightly (5 of 5 most recent runs FAILED, and it is now correctly alarmed, so it is generating a nightly page nobody acts on -- a desensitized alarm forming in real time), probes + due-list (reliability, distinct from the already-cleared 'has it ever fired'), strategy-review-packets (20 lifetime runs, 0 on cron -- RE-READ before grading, a late fire is possible), ict-scalp-exit-sweep (red since 2026-08-10, 23 days). (c) The audit's single CREATE item, which it calls the highest-leverage in the document. [!] NOT IN SCOPE: editing all 32 skills. A 32-file sweep would be the wrong shape and would bury the handful that matter.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Nothing technical -- it is unowned, and it was queued behind a session cap rather than behind a blocker. That distinction matters: this is not waiting on evidence or a decision.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] 87 OF THE 129 WORKFLOWS CANNOT BE GRADED ON DORMANCY AT ALL, and the audit says so rather than guessing. They are issue-label-driven and their run history is dominated by skipped label evaluations whose most recent entry is always today; no cheap surface answers 'has this ever done work, and when last'. That is why the RETIRE list is short -- an honest audit cannot retire what it could not measure. Do not let an enacting session 'finish the job' by retiring on a dormancy signal that does not exist. [!] AND THE AUDIT ITSELF CORRECTED THE DESIGN DOCS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: 5 functions the derivation lists as MISSING have all since shipped, and A1's readout is declared Cadenced while having NO cadence and no freshness check -- stale in the dangerous direction. An enacting session must read the audit, not the derivation, and must not re-derive from build-plan text that the audit already superseded.
