items.title: No manager handoff until the requisite flows are built, implemented AND verified working
items.observed: Operator-directed 2026-09-02: "I don't want to handoff before we are at least 200% certain that the requisite flows and merchanisms are built, implmented, and verified working correctly". Also, earlier the same hour: "i don't want to hand off before we're ready - that's why I keep asking you instead of telling you." So handoff readiness is the OPERATOR'S call and handoff_check's readiness=ready is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.
items.root_cause: handoff_check grades whether a SUCCESSOR CAN SEE the state -- registry, lease, checklist, open-PR rows. It says nothing about whether the MECHANISMS WORK. Those are different questions and this repo's whole vocabulary exists to keep them apart: landed_unproven is not done, a merge is not a deploy, and a deploy is not an observation.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: THE BAR, STATED AS OBSERVATIONS SO IT IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN A FEELING. Each names what would settle it, and a green test settles NONE of them: (1) DECISION ROUND-TRIP ON CLAUDEBOT -- a tap on ClaudeBot producing a work_decision_transit row, then that same request grading `committed` on /api/bot/work/decisions with the answer block on main. Already PROVEN on the TRADER bot (10:11:42Z prompt, 10:16:36Z tap, submitted_by telegram); the ClaudeBot leg is not. [!] CORRECTED 2026-09-02 BY MI-58, AND THE MANAGER'S PREMISE WAS FALSE. The manager told MI-58 that 'once TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is set, the fallback can never fire' and used that to argue for KEEPING the trader-bot fallback rather than making it fail-closed. WRONG: answerable_route() requires a live HEARTBEAT, not merely a token, so if ict-claude-decision-bot.service dies or is masked, decisions land on the trader bot again WITH THE SECRET SET. The fallback is PERMANENT, not a pre-secret window. The decision to keep it may still be right on its own merits -- a wrong chat is a noise complaint, holding every prompt is an outage -- but the reason given for it was not. [!] SO SETTING THE SECRET IS NOT THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK. Read /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude and `destination` in the sweep stats. 'Decisions still arrive' is NOT evidence the move happened -- that is precisely what the fallback produces. (2) /status AND /decisions -- the operator types each and gets a correct reply, ON CLAUDEBOT. #10793 is held as a draft precisely so this cannot be satisfied on the wrong bot. (3) PUSH-BACK TO THE ASKING SESSION (MI-60, #10788) -- a committed decision reaching the session that asked, without a minted token. B is not done when the Routine EXISTS; it is done when something WATCHES that it FIRED (list_triggers.last_run), because two Routines on this account were enabled and never once fired. (4) THE WORK STORE -- a COLD session, not pointed there by its prompt, acting on the readout or the cycle priority and citing where it read it. (5) NO WORK IS LOST (Phase E) -- demonstrated BY KILLING A SESSION MID-WORK, not asserted from a test. Nobody has killed one. (6) THE DAILY DIGEST -- one run with event=schedule. A workflow_dispatch run is not a cron run.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] THE MANAGER IS THE WRONG JUDGE OF (4) AND CANNOT CLEAR IT. A cold observation is by definition made by a session that was not told, and this manager built or dispatched most of these. Record WHICH session made each observation. [!] AND DO NOT LET THIS ROW BECOME A REASON NEVER TO HAND OFF. It is a bar, not a veto: if a mechanism turns out to be unverifiable rather than merely unverified, that is a finding to report to the operator, not a condition to wait out forever.

items.title: The most privileged role in the system has no skill, so every manager re-derives the job from prose and repeats the same mistakes
items.spawn_when: After MI-66, or in the same session if scope allows. Both are enactment of the operating-layer inventory.
items.observed: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'how do we ensure that you future manager session don't make the same mistake?' MEASURED in answering it: 32 skills exist and NOT ONE is a manager role pack. The role that merges, deploys, spawns sessions, holds the lease and answers to the operator is the only significant role with no pack. Everything a manager knows arrives as prose -- CLAUDE.md, a sweep-trigger prompt, and whatever the previous manager wrote in a checklist note.
items.root_cause: DOCUMENTATION HAS ALREADY BEEN TRIED AND MEASURABLY FAILED, and that is the whole argument for this row. The CI-never-fired trap is stated VERBATIM in CLAUDE.md ('if such a commit lands last your PR shows ZERO checks and is blocked, not green -- push an ordinary commit after, to arm CI'). The manager session of 2026-09-02 had read that line and hit the trap THREE TIMES the same afternoon (#10793, #10795, #10789). Restating a rule that is known and still broken is not a fix; this repo's own F4 says a repeated mistake becomes an executable check or it is not a lesson.
items.scope: A `manager` skill carrying (a) the loop -- lease heartbeat, read the registers, merge one at a time re-verifying between, review before un-drafting, spawn through the registry -- and (b) an EXECUTABLE PREFLIGHT rather than a list of reminders. The preflight must include, at minimum, the four failures measured on 2026-09-02: 1. BEFORE trusting `total_count: 0`, read mergeable_state AND the head commit's AUTHOR -- a bot-authored head means CI never fired (BL-20260902-BOARD-POST-RELAY-SILENTLY-KILLS-CI-ON-THE-PR-OF-ANY-SESSION-THAT-FOLLOWS-THE-PROTOCOL...). 2. BEFORE landing a register-touching manager PR, check what sibling PRs it will re-conflict; the manager is the highest-frequency writer to those files (BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE...). 3. BEFORE blocking work on a claim about live state, PROBE it. The 2026-09-02 manager blocked the ClaudeBot work on 'TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is unset', asserted from a doc row dated the previous day, against the operator's own contrary sighting (MI-65). 4. BEFORE a read-append-write on any register, confirm the file round-trips; OPEN-ITEMS.json does not (BL-20260902-OPEN-ITEMS-IS-THE-ONE-REGISTER-NO-APPEND-HELPER-PROTECTS). 5. F6 -- REFUSE TO PROCEED when the count of unnotified autonomous actions since the last ping exceeds a stated threshold. This is the fifth item and arguably the first in importance: F6 is the CONDITION the autonomy grant rests on, and on 2026-09-02 a manager merged 5 PRs, dispatched 4 sessions, held a PR to block a deploy and made a fallback design call across ~8 hours while sending ZERO pings -- the operator noticed before the manager did. The class of action most worth reporting is exactly the class that is silent, because merge_pull_request / update_pull_request / create_session / fire_trigger are MCP calls with no notification hop, while the narrow VM system-actions DO carry one. BL-20260902-THE-MANAGERS-HIGH-IMPACT-ACTIONS-BYPASS-EVERY-PATH-THAT-NOTIFIES.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: An executable preflight the manager RUNS, not a section it reads -- the `handoff_check.py` shape, which already refuses `ready` rather than grading a soft pass, and which is the one manager mechanism that has worked reliably today. Every item above is checkable from a script.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] A SKILL IS STILL PROSE UNTIL THE CHECKS EXIST. Writing a `manager` SKILL.md and stopping there would reproduce exactly the failure this row documents -- and would be harder to see, because the role pack would LOOK like the fix. The deliverable is the checks; the skill is where they are invoked from. [!] AND IT INHERITS MI-66's FINDING: no role pack references the operating layer at all, so a new manager pack must point at the work store, the readout and the caps rather than the pre-2026-09-01 world of three backlogs and DUE.md. Writing it against the old world would add a 33rd skill with the same gap.
items.landed_unproven_because: #10808 MERGED 2026-09-02 (67cfb8be). ⚠️ TWO OF THE THREE MECHANISMS WORK AND THE THIRD CANNOT. The manager VERIFIED spawn_gate.py on both controls itself -- out-of-priority exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But queue_latency.py grades `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live list_sessions read and CI holds no mcp__* tools. Honest, and not yet a guard. MI-73 owns closing that.

items.title: A rebase or merge of main arms auto-merge on a claude/** branch, because the push diff includes everything main changed
items.observed: Found and filed by MI-58. claude-pr-automerge.yml still carries the LEGACY shared marker `.github/pr-automerge-request` in its paths: filter and that file is still in the tree, so any claude/** branch that merges or rebases main touches the path and is UN-DRAFTED AND ARMED having asked for nothing. [!] THIS EXPLAINS AN OBSERVATION THE MANAGER MADE AND COULD NOT ACCOUNT FOR: on #10795 the manager noted that github-actions[bot] un-drafted the PR and enabled auto-merge 'without a marker file in my diff' and flagged it as odd. This is the cause. The manager had the symptom; MI-58 had the mechanism.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Remove the legacy shared path from the workflow's paths: filter so ONLY the per-request .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt opt-in arms it. That per-request path is already the documented convention and its README records why the shared marker was wrong.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] DELETING A HOLD FILE IS NOT THE FIX. A test-file hold WAS deleted on 2026-09-02 (correctly, for an unrelated reason) and could be mistaken for remediation. The mechanism is untouched.
items.note: #10810 reviewed by the manager and ARMED 2026-09-02, not yet merged. Its central finding is that removing the legacy shared marker FIXES NOTHING ON ITS OWN -- measured across the three misfires, that path appears in ZERO of them; what matched is the GLOB, because any branch merging main drags other branches' request files into its push diff. The real fix is a REQUEST GATE proving THIS branch asked, plus never un-drafting a PR the workflow did not create.
items.adjudicated_2026_09_06: BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION, not a verdict on the work. State read `in_flight` with owner `session_01XrwTGRY819PCzBnppCTLbi`, which a LIVE list_sessions read on 2026-09-06T08:0xZ graded IDLE (population: 180 sessions enumerated back to 2026-08-02; exactly ONE was RUNNING and it was the manager). So the register asserted this was being worked while no worker existed. Re-graded in_flight -> queued, owner -> unassigned. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE WORK IS UNDONE, and NOT a claim that it is done — nobody looked at the artifact. Whether its code landed is UNVERIFIED and is exactly what the Phase-1 observation sweep must establish. The prior owner id is preserved here so the evidence trail is not lost.

items.title: Decision PRESENTATION on ClaudeBot: options as a readable list, and real multiple choice
items.tier: 2 (touches the Telegram bridge; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY not urgent: 'Also not urgent, but something that I do want us to have ... somewhere in our work plan.'
items.observed: Operator, on the live decision prompt: 'the point with the buttons is that it's very shortened, a little cut off ... maybe there's more of a list and I can click the options, maybe some would be multiple choice. I think that button is a good first step, but probably not the end of where this design needs to go.' So the ASK half of the decision round-trip works and its PRESENTATION is the limit.
items.⚠️_the_truncation_is_the_LABEL_not_the_c: DO NOT go looking for a callback_data size bug -- it is already solved and re-solving it would waste the session. `callback_data` is 26 bytes FIXED (`wdec:<12 hex>:<8 hex>`) against Telegram's 64-byte cap, and it carries a DIGEST of the option KEY, deliberately never a positional index. What the operator sees cut off is the BUTTON LABEL, which Telegram renders narrow and elides. Those are different layers.

the_shape_to_build.1_options_as_a_numbered_list_in_the_MESS: Put the full option text in the message body as a numbered list -- where there is room for it -- and reduce each button to its number. The body is not width-constrained the way a button is, so the option a person is choosing between becomes readable without touching the callback contract at all. This is the cheap half and it is probably most of the win.
the_shape_to_build.2_multiple_choice_is_NOT_one_press: [!] A single inline keyboard press submits ONE value, so multi-select is not a formatting change -- it needs a TOGGLE keyboard: each tap flips an option's mark and re-renders the keyboard, and an explicit Submit sends the set. That means holding PARTIAL, UNSUBMITTED state between taps, which the current design deliberately does not have. Decide where that state lives BEFORE building it; a half-submitted answer that looks submitted is the forward-failure the transit contract exists to refuse.
the_shape_to_build.3_free_text_is_still_a_separate_step: Unchanged and deliberately not half-built: inline buttons cannot carry arbitrary text. A request declaring no options is still SENT (so a blocking question is never invisible) and says plainly that it needs an answer on the SPA or in the repo.

items.what_must_not_regress: The four never-collapsed answer states (`not_submitted`/`in_transit`/`committed`/`unreadable`); the option token staying a KEY DIGEST rather than an index (an index silently records a different answer if the object is reordered between send and tap); the fail-closed write gate; and the confirmation continuing to read 'Submitted -- NOT yet decided'.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability and P2 is the overhaul implementation. This is a UX improvement to a channel that already works end-to-end -- the round-trip was observed complete on 2026-09-02. The operator said not urgent and this records that as a decision, not as an oversight.

items.title: The daily manager cadence: day session → declared wrap → night manager → morning brief
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, as the shape the handoff should take
items.⚠️_THIS_SUPERSEDES_THE_MANAGERS_OWN_FRAM: The manager reported that `open_prs` completeness is POINT-IN-TIME and concluded 'a handoff has to be taken in a QUIET WINDOW, or the check needs a bounded tolerance.' That framing is PASSIVE -- it waits for a quiet moment that a busy repo never reliably offers. The operator's answer is ACTIVE and is better: you do not wait for a quiet window, you CREATE one, by declaring per thread which PR is the LAST one before the manager moves on. Do not re-derive the tolerance idea from the old framing; the boundary is declared, not awaited.

the_cycle.1_morning: The day STARTS WITH A PING — a daily brief into a NEW manager session. ⚠️ The brief must carry WHAT WAS DONE OVERNIGHT and what was wrapped up after the operator went to bed. Operator: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, so that I know where I'm starting off from.' A brief that only describes the new day's plan fails its purpose.
the_cycle.3_wrap: The operator SAYS when they are going to bed. That is the trigger, not a clock. The manager then produces a RAPID WRAP PLAN: (a) the LAST PR for each thread; (b) confirmation that NO Tier-3 decision is left dangling -- and any that is gets LOGGED FOR THE NEXT DAY rather than carried in a session's head; (c) close everything down.
the_cycle.4_night: The manager SETS OFF THE NIGHT SESSION ITSELF, scoped by HOW MUCH TIME IT HAS until the morning brief. Night work is deliberately the low-operator-dependency kind: backlog items and UI, 'things that are less important and need less of me, and very easy to run without me.' ⚠️ NOTHING TIER-3 AND NOTHING NEEDING A DECISION goes to the night session -- it cannot get an answer.

items.the_last_PR_per_thread_rule: ⚠️ READ WHAT THE OPERATOR RULED OUT, not just what they asked for. They explicitly did NOT ask that entire MILESTONES be finished before a handoff: 'it just means that for each thread of workflow, we need to decide what the last PR for each manager is gonna be before we move on, and that needs to be documented clearly so that we can make sure that we're sticking to that.' So the unit is a DECLARED TERMINAL PR PER THREAD, documented in advance and held to -- not milestone completion, which would block every handoff indefinitely.
items.what_this_needs_built: Not yet designed, and deliberately not designed here: where the per-thread terminal PR is DECLARED (OPEN-PRS.json rows already carry a thread via checklist_item, so this may be a field rather than a new register); how the morning brief is GENERATED from the overnight record rather than written by hand; and whether the night session's scope is bounded by a stated deadline it can read. Operator also raised timers/pings for start-and-finish awareness -- worth a design pass, not a guess.
items.⚠️_honest_precondition: The operator's own read: 'it sounds like we still have a lot of [work] here to get [addressed] so that we're able to do an actual reliable handoff.' This item does NOT claim the cadence is achievable today. handoff_check.py still reads not_ready more often than ready on a busy repo.
items.⚠️_CORRECTION_THE_MANAGER_MADE_TO_ITSELF: THE NIGHT HOP NEEDS NO NEW MECHANISM, and the first version of this row said it did. It read: 'the night-manager hop depends on a fresh-session-per-fire routine gated on the lease, which does not exist.' That is FALSE for the flow the operator actually described, which has the MANAGER setting the night session off directly -- 'set off the night manager session yourself' -- and `create_session` is proven to do exactly that (MI-73 was spawned with it on 2026-09-02). Overstating a blocker is not a safe error: it invites a session to build a routine nobody needs and to treat tonight's handoff as impossible when it is not.
items.what_ACTUALLY_needs_a_mechanism: ⚠️ DECIDED 2026-09-02 — THE MORNING WAKE IS MANUAL, AND THIS IS AN ANSWER, NOT A GAP. Operator, verbatim: 'There's [no] new need for a timer or a trigger for the morning manager. I will do that manually. I will get the daily brief. I will read it, and then I will use it as the beginning of a prompt, which I'll also add my notes to, to set off the manager session for that day. So that doesn't need to be set off automatically. I wanna be there at the beginning.' So: NO cron routine, NO create_new_session_on_fire, NO lease-gated auto-spawn. Do not build one, and do not re-open this as an oversight -- the operator being present at the start of the day is a DELIBERATE choice, and automating it would remove the point.
items.⚠️_the_self_bound_sweep_limit_is_still_r: Unchanged by the correction above: the manager sweep re-armed 2026-09-02T15:20Z is SELF-BOUND and dies with its session. That is a genuine gap for a manager that DIES mid-day -- it is simply not the gap the night handoff has, because the night handoff is deliberate and the manager is alive to perform it.
items.⚠️_what_the_manual_wake_does_NOT_remove: THE BRIEF ITSELF IS STILL A DELIVERABLE AND IS STILL UNBUILT. The operator says 'I will GET the daily brief' -- they are the trigger, not the author. Something must PRODUCE a brief that carries what happened overnight, and that is precisely the half their stated reason depends on: 'so that I know where I'm starting off from.' Separating these two matters, because the wake being settled makes it easy to read the whole morning end as settled. The wake is decided; the brief is open. Most likely the NIGHT session's closing output is the brief, which would make it a night-session deliverable rather than a new mechanism -- but that is a proposal, not a decision, and nobody has built it.

items.title: A notifications menu per bot: choose WHICH notifications, and a CADENCE for the periodic ones
items.tier: 2 (Telegram bridge + a stored per-chat preference; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY for the backlog: 'a further idea, though, that I do want us to backlog as well ... so that we eventually get to it.'
items.observed: Operator: 'in the menu for each of the bots for there to be an option for notifications, which would then pull up a list of the notifications, and I could choose which ones. And for the ones that are periodic, there should be some choices for cadence -- hourly, daily, weekly, maybe once, twice, three times daily, depending on what kind of thing it is.' Raised alongside making the work digest hourly, which is the manual version of exactly this control.
items.⚠️_HALF_OF_THIS_ALREADY_EXISTS_AND_LOST_: DO NOT BUILD THE 'WHICH' HALF FROM SCRATCH -- measure it first. A per-kind subscription model is already shipped and has been since M12: `GET /api/bot/devices/event-kinds` serves the canonical taxonomy from `src.runtime.mobile_push.event_kinds` (kind/label/description/in_flight) precisely so a client need not mirror the list, and `PATCH /api/bot/devices/{id}/subscriptions` stores a per-device choice as `null|[kinds]|{kind:bool}`. It was built for the Android app's Notifications screen -- and the Android app was RETIRED from the live feed on 2026-09-01, with `device_tokens` measured EMPTY (0 registered devices). So this is a mechanism that is written, works, and now has no reader: the `provenance-consumer-guard` shape one level up, the same shape MI-70 found with the `Claude-Session:` commit trailer. The honest framing of this item is RE-POINT AN EXISTING TAXONOMY AT TELEGRAM, plus build the genuinely new half.

what_is_genuinely_new.cadence_per_kind: The existing model is a BOOLEAN per kind (on/off). Cadence is a third value and the taxonomy has no field for it. Note the operator's own distinction -- 'depending on what kind of thing it is' -- so cadence is not universal: an EVENT (a decision ready, an incident) is immediate-or-nothing and a cadence choice on it is meaningless, while a DIGEST (the work digest, the daily roll-up) is exactly where cadence belongs. The taxonomy therefore needs to say which kinds are cadence-BEARING, or the menu will offer 'weekly' on an alert.
what_is_genuinely_new.per_CHAT_not_per_DEVICE: `device_tokens` is keyed on an FCM token. Telegram has no such token; the natural key is the chat/bot pair. Whether that is a new table or a widened one is the first design question, and it is the one that decides how much of the existing model is reusable.
what_is_genuinely_new.a_menu_is_stateful: Same constraint as MI-71: one inline press submits one value, so a multi-select preferences screen is a TOGGLE keyboard plus an explicit Save, which means holding partial unsubmitted state. The two items share this problem and should probably share its solution -- do not solve it twice, differently.

items.⚠️_what_must_not_become_switchable: A preferences menu that can silence anything is a way to turn off an alarm and forget. The severity-band rule stands: a P0 (money at risk) page is NOT a preference. Whatever this ships with, the CRITICAL/unprotected-position class must remain unmutable, or this feature becomes the desensitized-alarm P1 with a UI in front of it.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability, P2 the overhaul implementation. The operator asked for it to be backlogged, not built, and the immediate need it came with -- an hourly work digest -- was satisfied directly by a cron change.

items.title: The manager watcher is BLIND by construction — give it a sensor that can actually see
items.observed: Of the three mechanisms MI-68 built to watch the manager (merged #10808), TWO WORK and the third cannot. `spawn_gate.py` was verified by the manager on BOTH controls -- out-of-priority object exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But `queue_latency.py`, the one aimed at the manager sitting on a blocked queue, reports `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live `list_sessions` read, that is an mcp__* tool, and CI holds no MCP tools. It refuses to substitute SESSIONS.json's stale `last_observed`, which is correct -- that register has been measured incomplete twice.
items.why_it_matters: This is the failure that cost the most on 2026-09-02: four sub-sessions sat IDLE and BLOCKED on the manager for up to 142 minutes while the manager asserted they held work. It is also the operator's core ask -- 'actual guards and mechanisms in the repo/vm themselves that watch the manager and enforce the rules on him.' A permanently-`unknown` watcher is honest but is not yet that guard.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST_not_assume: The same failure has an MCP-FREE PROXY that GitHub Actions can see with nothing but its own GITHUB_TOKEN: a PR green/mergeable/unmerged and ageing; a `needs_action` posted with nothing since; a board `▶️ START` with no `✅ DONE`, ageing; an `in_flight` checklist item whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours. ⚠️ THE MANAGER BELIEVES THIS AND HAS NOT PROVEN IT. If the proxy is weaker than it looks, a STATED BOUNDARY is the better deliverable -- which is exactly what MI-68 delivered on queue_latency and why its work merged.
items.what_must_not_regress: (a) Do NOT delete or weaken the `unknown` path -- `quiet`/`escalate`/`unknown` must never collapse, because 'we could not look' and 'nothing is waiting' are opposite facts. (b) It must NOT be invokable by the manager: MI-68's own measurement is that every mechanism the manager had to choose to run went unused, and every mechanism that stood in the way worked. (c) Never page on activity, only on a state that is actually stuck, rate-limited per class -- 202 of 376 CRITICAL rows in one measured window here were a single un-latched alarm.
items.⚠️_a_cron_is_not_evidence_of_a_run: work-digest.yml's own header records a scheduled workflow in this repo firing ~4h50m LATE and once instead of daily. Whatever carries this must make its own liveness checkable.
items.⚠️_outcome: DIED BLOCKED, WORK LOST. post_turn_summary: 'blocked on permission classifier; auto-mode denied add_repo x2 and git push x3'. It never pushed a branch, so ~$10 of work is unrecoverable -- exactly the loss MI-70 demonstrated by killing a session. Two manager wake attempts did not clear it: the denial is its session's permission classifier, which the manager cannot change from outside. SUPERSEDED BY MI-77, respawned with an explicit source_url (which this session's context lacked) and instructed to push within its first minutes. [!] THE MANAGER'S FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: it told MI-73 the cause was an omitted source_url, then found MI-75 had a source it never passed and MI-76 acquired one late -- sources attach ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so 'no sources' reads as a defect when it is often just a timing artifact.

items.title: Phase E: prove no work is lost by actually killing a session mid-work
items.landed_unproven_because: #10812 and #10820 both MERGED 2026-09-02. ⚠️ THE REAPER HAS STILL NEVER BEEN OBSERVED RUNNING TO COMPLETION, and #10820 is why that matters: the version merged in #10812 pushed straight to PROTECTED main (GH006), so every scheduled run would have reaped correctly and RECORDED NOTHING -- a frozen ledger reading exactly like a quiet week. The owner found that itself, after merge, and fixed it via .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged: true.
items.the_ruling_it_carries: ⚠️ PHASE E DOES NOT CLOSE ON THIS. The kill was RUN and demonstrated a PARTIAL loss -- 'killing a session loses everything it had not pushed, and nothing it had' -- which CONTRADICTS the object's done-condition ('loses nothing'). Manager ruled 2026-09-02: do NOT amend the condition to match the result (that fits the bar to the outcome) and do NOT leave 'loses nothing' standing (unachievable -- the loss is in a dead container no reaper can reach). BOUND it instead, and keep Phase E open until a successor object exists for PUSH CADENCE, which is the only lever that moves the number.
items.⚠️_do_not_merge: `claude/mi70-kill-subject` must NEVER be merged. It is the EVIDENCE for the kill demonstration and holds a throwaway notes file.

items.title: The HANDOFF BRIEF — what a successor manager and the operator are handed, generated not written
items.why_this_is_the_last_P1_gap: The operator set the daily cadence and then decided BOTH hops are MANUAL -- the manager spawns the night session (create_session, proven), and the operator starts the morning one because 'I wanna be there at the beginning.' That CLOSED the wake question and left exactly one thing open: they say they will GET the daily brief. They are the TRIGGER, not the author, and NOTHING PRODUCES ONE.
items.acceptance_is_the_operators_own_words: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, SO THAT I KNOW WHERE I'M STARTING OFF FROM.' A brief that renders but does not answer that fails, however well-formed it is.
items.two_consumers_and_it_is_an_open_question: (1) THE OPERATOR IN THE MORNING -- readable prose they paste as the opening of the next manager's prompt, carrying what happened overnight. (2) A SUCCESSOR MANAGER MID-DAY -- live state: checklist, in-flight sessions, open PRs with their operator decisions AND conditions, loud open-items, the lease, what is blocked and on what. The owner was told to ARGUE the choice rather than assume it.
items.⚠️_the_real_constraint_it_must_not_fake_: What MERGED is readable from git and the registers are readable, but WHAT A NIGHT SESSION CONCLUDED lives in get_session's post_turn_summary -- and mcp__* tools are unavailable to CI and to routine-fired turns. So the brief is probably a CLOSE-OUT DELIVERABLE the night manager runs before it ends, not a cron. The owner must decide that honestly and say which.
items.what_must_not_regress: GENERATED never hand-written (a hand-written brief dies with its session, which is the failure Phase E exists for); it must DECLARE what it could not read rather than silently omitting a register; and it must not flatten `landed_unproven` into `done` -- saying an item is finished when its effect was never observed actively misinforms the person starting the day.
items.adjudicated_2026_09_06: BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION, not a verdict on the work. State read `in_flight` with owner `session_017CSW7fZsqsbgGSDN6Atijj`, which a LIVE list_sessions read on 2026-09-06T08:0xZ graded IDLE (population: 180 sessions enumerated back to 2026-08-02; exactly ONE was RUNNING and it was the manager). So the register asserted this was being worked while no worker existed. Re-graded in_flight -> queued, owner -> unassigned. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE WORK IS UNDONE, and NOT a claim that it is done — nobody looked at the artifact. items.tier: 1 (trainer read; trainer VM is autonomous territory)

items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: The two halves are DIFFERENT FACTS and must not be collapsed. (1) OBSERVE -- what is the disk headroom, is the capture still writing, how stale is its newest data. (2) ALARM -- keyed on the DATA's freshness at the named path, NEVER on the unit's ActiveState, because a systemd unit can be `active` while writing nothing and a unit-state alarm would be green straight through the failure this watches. The row's own clears_when requires the alarm be SHOWN to fire against PLANTED staleness, not merely deployed.
items.done_when: The row's observation carries what was SEEN (verbatim, with the command) and verified_at is re-dated. The row clears only if the freshness alarm exists AND was shown to fire against planted staleness; otherwise it stays open with the reason. Disk headroom recovering on its own does NOT clear it -- the gap is the missing alarm, not the free space.

items.title: #10398 has been RED and stalled for 113 hours — the queue watcher's first real catch
items.priority: P2 — DIAGNOSED. The disposition is a judgement call, deliberately not taken.
items.note: DIAGNOSED AGAINST FRESH MAIN — and the diagnosis INVERTS the obvious call. Do not close this PR as stale. (1) THE RED WAS NEVER THE BLOCKER. `mergeable_state` is **dirty** — #10398 has a MERGE CONFLICT, which is also why it shows the total_count-0 check signature. Probed locally by merging fresh origin/main into the PR head: conflicts in exactly 2 files, comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl and comms/macro/econ_calendar_upcoming.json. Both are DERIVED files that main has regenerated 4 times since (most recently #10711 on 2026-09-02), so main's copies are newer and correct. (2) THE LIVE-PATH CLAIM IS TRUE — verified against the diff rather than the description, as this row asked. `git diff --name-status origin/main...pr10398`, COMPLETE changed-file set n=3: A comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260829T034952Z.fxstreet.json, M econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl, M econ_calendar_upcoming.json. NO path under config/ is touched; config/economic_calendar.yaml is absent from the diff. Data-only under comms/macro/. (3) ⚠️ THE REASON NOT TO CLOSE IT: the capture it carries is a GAP-FILLER, not superseded data. main holds 36 captures running 08-27, 08-28, then 08-30, 08-31, 09-01, 09-02 — 2026-08-29 IS MISSING, and #10398 holds the only copy. main's snapshots.jsonl contains 0 rows mentioning 20260829. So the naive reading ('4-day-old PIT data, close it') would PERMANENTLY LOSE a day from the point-in-time series. (4) THE DISPOSITION IS A JUDGEMENT CALL AND THE NIGHT MANAGER DELIBERATELY DID NOT TAKE IT, per this row's own instruction. The shape of a correct fix is: keep the capture file (new, unique, additive, unconflicted), take MAIN's side of both derived files, then RE-RUN THE PRODUCER so the 08-29 capture is reflected in the series — scripts/macro/econ_calendar_snapshot_backfill.py exists for exactly this. ⚠️ Hand-resolving a conflict in generated point-in-time data would FABRICATE a snapshot no capture produced, which is the one thing PIT data must never contain. That is why this is a decision and not a merge. NOT DONE: CI was not re-run against fresh main, because the branch does not merge cleanly and pushing a hand-made resolution is the very thing being avoided.
items.blocked_on_basis: MEASURED 2026-09-02T22:00Z against a FRESHLY FETCHED origin/main, not inferred, and not from the PR's 4.7-day-old CI. This is a real blocker with a dated observation behind it, not a bare-string claim.

items.title: The routine_scope_correction did not reach the spawn prompt it was correcting — the night manager acted on the uncorrected text
items.priority: P1 — a correction that does not reach the artifact carrying the error has not been made
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-02T22:10Z, and this is the FIFTH instance of the over-generalisation, observed live. docs/claude/CYCLE-PRIORITY.json::routine_scope_correction records the operator correcting the day manager at 21:50Z, verbatim: "when I said no cloud routines that wasn't 'don't use that tool', it was don't use that as a Band-Aid for something that needs to be an actual routine. You CAN spawn off cloud routines, especially if that's gonna give you better control over the session. That was for that specific thing, not a general rule. I don't want it written into the rules as a general rule." That row itself names the four places the hardened version was written — 'a spawn prompt, a checklist row, a work object and a merged PR body'. ⚠️ THE SPAWN PROMPT IT NAMES IS THE NIGHT MANAGER'S, AND THE NIGHT MANAGER WAS SPAWNED AT 21:37:58Z CARRYING THE UNCORRECTED TEXT: 'NO CLAUDE ROUTINE, in any form.' The correction was written at 21:50Z — 12 minutes AFTER the prompt was issued — and nothing propagated it into the prompt, because a prompt is a frozen copy, not a reference. WHAT IT COST, MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the night manager concluded and stated that it could not schedule the operator's 05:00Z brief because Routines were prohibited. That conclusion was FALSE, and the brief — the operator's own stated 08:00-Israel deliverable and this shift's done_condition — was nearly not delivered because of it. It was caught only because the rendered brief happened to surface routine_scope_correction by name and the session followed the reference instead of trusting its prompt. That is luck, not a mechanism. RESOLVED IN-SESSION once caught: Routine trig_01EWqusjwUZtGEZAjz8tekyW created for 2026-09-03T05:00Z. ⚠️ AND IT IS NOT CLEAN — the trigger stores NO MCP connectors, so the fired session may have no list_sessions, no GitHub tools and no add_repo, which means it may be unable to supply live observations OR to push. Its prompt was rewritten to declare a DEGRADED LANE that reports `not_observed` honestly and prints the brief inline rather than faking `all_observed`. TREAT THE 05:00Z BRIEF AS AT RISK, NOT ASSURED. THE GENERAL DEFECT: a correction landed in a register while the error stayed live in a frozen prompt already in flight. Same shape as MI-86 one level up — MI-86 is a stale READ of a store, this is a stale COPY of an instruction, and neither has a mechanism that closes it. A prompt cannot be corrected after issue, so the fix belongs at spawn time: a spawn-time check that reads the live corrections register, or prompts that REFERENCE the register rather than restating it.

items.title: An unpushed RELEASE strands the successor — the lease handover is most fragile exactly when it happens
items.priority: P2 — cost is bounded and measured (16 min), but it recurs at EVERY handover
items.note:
⚠️ RE-HOMED FROM MI-86 BY THE MANAGER, 2026-09-03, BECAUSE THE ID WAS ALREADY TAKEN. The night manager filed this finding as MI-86 while MI-86 already existed on main as the night-shift handoff row -- so merging the branch as written would have SILENTLY DELETED that row, along with the finding main had since added to it (that a session-bound Routine fire reaches a RUNNING session, not only an IDLE one). Both rows survive: the handoff stays MI-86, this finding becomes MI-91. Nothing in the repo enforces id uniqueness across concurrent branches, and git cannot see the collision because to git it is just a changed value at the same key -- filed as its own defect.

FOUND BY LIVING IT, 2026-09-02. The night manager was spawned at 21:37:58Z and refused to manage for 16 minutes because origin said the lease was held. It was not: the day manager released it at 21:38:05Z, deliberately, with a note naming the incoming session. THE RELEASE REACHED origin ONLY AT 21:41:54Z (f19fd014, #10869). The successor fetched at 21:39:37Z — 2m17s inside that window — read 14f101eb, the last commit still showing state=held, and correctly stood down. ⚠️ THE GUARD WAS RIGHT AND SHOULD NOT BE WEAKENED. manager_preflight.py graded exactly what origin showed; a session must not manage on a lease it observes as held. The bug is the FRESHNESS OF THE FILE, never the strictness of the check. WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL, not bad luck: MANAGER-LEASE.json's own _doc warns about the unpushed window in the CLAIM direction ('a claim you never pushed protects nothing'). This is the SAME window in the RELEASE direction, where the cost is different — an unpushed release STRANDS THE SUCCESSOR. And it lands in the worst possible place: the outgoing manager releases and spawns its successor in the same breath, so the successor's very first read falls inside the window BY CONSTRUCTION. MEASURED COST: 16 minutes of night shift, plus a false accusation ('the spawn prompt lied') published to board #6927 and PR #10871 before the session re-read at 21:54Z and retracted it. The secondary lesson is the session's own: a NEGATIVE EXISTENCE CLAIM ('no release commit exists') from a single read of a store with a known unpushed window is not a measurement. CANDIDATE FIXES, NOT BUILT: (a) make `release --commit` push, or push the release BEFORE spawning the successor — the ordering is the whole bug and this is the cheap sufficient fix; (b) have manager_preflight.py re-fetch once on a held_fresh refusal and report 'held on origin as of <sha> at <time>' instead of bare 'held', so a stale read is VISIBLY stale — it currently reports state with no provenance for the read. NOT A FIX: telling sessions to trust the spawn prompt over the file. ⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT WAY TO MISREAD THE SAME FILE, contributed by the outgoing day manager at 21:56Z and worth as much as the first: `manager_lease.py status` READS THE WORKING TREE, so running it while checked out on a FEATURE BRANCH reports that branch's copy of MANAGER-LEASE.json, not main's. The day manager reports this made IT briefly misreport the lease as HELD too. So there are now TWO distinct stale-read paths into the same wrong answer — a stale FETCH (this session's, the 2m17s window) and a stale CHECKOUT (any session standing on a branch). Both produce a confident, unqualified `held`. That strengthens fix (b) rather than replacing it: the tool should report WHERE and WHEN it read — 'held per <ref> at <sha>, read <time>' — because a reading with no provenance cannot be checked by the person it misleads. ⚠️ ALSO MEASURED: the day manager's correction was queued at 21:56:42Z and DELIVERED to this session at ~22:17Z — a ~20 MINUTE LAG, during which this session had already independently re-read the lease, claimed it, created the 05:00Z Routine and diagnosed MI-85. Cross-session correction is therefore NOT a reliable channel for unblocking a live session; the repo was the faster and more trustworthy one. That is an argument for putting corrections in the REGISTERS, which is where this session actually found them, rather than in messages.

items.note: AGREED IN WRITING 2026-09-03 -- the done-condition was an agreement, not a build, and it is met. OPERATOR'S FOUR ANSWERS: (1) INTENT IS SUB-THREAD, one intent per thread at a time unless a specific exception -- one taxonomy, not two, and enforceable with the spawn gate that already exists. (2) PRIORITY IS A MATRIX: a priority per thread AND between threads, cap stays at 3, OPS HOLDS A STANDING SLOT and TWO FLOAT; a blocker outranks a non-blocker across threads, which is the 'put research on hold for an engineering blocker' case. ADMIN IS PRECEDENCE, NOT A STANDING SLOT. items.title: The standing close-wedge ledger does not exist, and the digest reads a non-canonical path for it -- downgraded wedges are in NEITHER channel
items.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 via /api/diag/log_file?name=close_wedge_standing: present:false at /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/close_wedge_standing.json. TWO DEFECTS, NOT ONE. (1) THE DIGEST READS THE WRONG PATH -- it reported the ledger absent at /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/..., a repo-relative path, while diag resolves it under $DATA_DIR; that is the CWD-relative-fallback class canonical-db-resolver forbids for the journal DB, reappearing for a runtime_logs artifact, so even a working writer would keep reading NOT EXAMINED. (2) THE LEDGER IS ABSENT AT THE CANONICAL PATH TOO, so the writer has never written it. ⚠️ WHY IT MATTERS: on 2026-09-02 (MI-34) the operator DELIBERATELY downgraded broker_cancel_wedged close failures OUT of the pager and INTO this digest. That downgrade is only safe if the digest carries them -- and with no ledger and a mis-pathed reader, such a failure is in NEITHER channel, on a real-money close path. The digest says so in its own words. ⚠️ present:false ALSO COLLAPSES TWO OPPOSITE FACTS -- 'no wedge since the writer shipped' and 'the writer is not running' -- so the fix must emit an empty-but-present ledger with a timestamp, making wedges:[] mean WE LOOKED. ⚠️ AND CHECK WHETHER ANY broker_cancel_wedged failure HAS occurred since MI-34 shipped: if one has, it was silently in neither channel, and that is an INCIDENT rather than a gap. Surfaced only because the operator pasted the digest in -- the digest's NOT EXAMINED warning did its job. Filed as BL-20260903-CLOSE-WEDGE-LEDGER-IS-ABSENT-SO-DOWNGRADED-WEDGES-ARE-IN-NEITHER-CHANNEL. LIVE-SYSTEM/Ops, so it is NOT gated by the workflow-build sequencing per the operator's own carve-out. ⚠️ MANAGER RULING 2026-09-03T13:2xZ on the question MI-101 went idle asking — 'land the two-part staleness fix, or file it as a separate finding?' RULING: LAND IT AS PART OF THIS FIX, not as a separate row. Reason, and it is not a scope call: done_condition (b) already commits the writer to emitting an EMPTY-BUT-PRESENT ledger WITH A TIMESTAMP. A timestamp exists only to be graded — ship it with nothing reading it and this becomes the written-and-never-read defect the repo has paid for repeatedly (provenance-consumer-guard exists for exactly that shape). Staleness is not a third discovery bolted on; it is what makes (b) mean anything, because a ledger that is present but unrefreshed reads as current and re-collapses 'we looked' into 'we did not look' one level up — the same failure at a different layer. Splitting it would ship half a state machine. ⚠️ SCOPE IS STILL BOUNDED, so this is not a licence to widen: it means the path fix (a), the present-vs-absent fix (b) and a freshness grade ON THE SAME ARTIFACT. items.title: CANONIZE the manager's base duties -- runs the merge queue, holds a check-in cadence -- plus the meta-rule that turns operator feedback into canon
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-03, verbatim: "that's one of the base functions of what a manager session is supposed to do. That needs to be canonized. It's not something you take upon yourself in the session... We need to make sure that these types of feedbacks are turning into actual rules when applicable. Some comments are obviously one-offs, but in general here, this is a deeper problem that other sessions need to be prevented from getting to." ⚠️ THE POINT IS NOT THIS SESSION'S BEHAVIOUR -- this manager did build a queue and did tighten its cadence, but only after being told twice, and a fix living in one session's context DIES WITH THAT SESSION. The next manager starts blank and re-derives the same jam. MEASURED HARM on 2026-09-03 with no queue and a 20-25min cadence: 26 merges to main, 19 (73%) touching a shared register, 5 authored by the manager and 2 of those BARE LEASE HEARTBEATS -- merges whose entire content is a timestamp. #10918 conflicted THREE times, #10923 conflicted the instant it went green, 20 PRs open with 12 machine-authored and stacked three deep per family, and several sessions each burned a ~16min pytest-run voided before it finished. THREE THINGS TO CANONIZE: (1) THE MANAGER RUNS THE QUEUE -- schedules, does not merely resolve conflicts; names ONE position 1, tells that owner to rebase, merges, PROMOTES and POKES the next. The load-bearing half is THE HOLD: only position 1 rebases. And a session does not poll, so promotion without a poke is not promotion. (2) THE CADENCE IS A DUTY, NOT A TUNING KNOB -- operator: 'it can't be that the manager session is idle for thirty minutes... that's reflective of the fact that you're not actively managing'. Measurable with no new instrument: MANAGER-LEASE.json's git history already holds every heartbeat. (3) THE META-RULE -- feedback is TRIAGED into one-off vs rule, and a rule lands as canon WITH A MECHANISM. This is the rule that would have prevented the other two being learned twice; a session that fixes its own behaviour and does not canonize it has turned a systemic finding into a private one. ⚠️ HOME IS scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py (MI-95's, lands with #10918) which ALREADY derives the manager from the LEASE -- do not build a second manager-identity notion. ⚠️ THRESHOLDS MEASURED WITH THEIR POPULATION, never chosen by feel. ⚠️ DUTY 3 MUST NOT BE FAKED: CI cannot read a conversation, so a marker asserting 'I triaged the feedback' would be cheaper to lie to than to satisfy. If the honest answer is that it belongs in the session-end doc-freshness discipline rather than in a check, SAY SO. Object: WO-20260903-CANONIZE-THE-MANAGER-DUTIES-QUEUE-CADENCE. BLOCKED ON #10918 (position 2) because the target file is not on main yet.

items.title: The reconcile-open-prs generator is jammed on ONE missing fact, and it emits a new PR on every merge
items.note: ⚠️ STATE CORRECTED 2026-09-05T15:00Z from `in_flight` to `queued`, because NOTHING IS WORKING IT. I set it in_flight earlier today when I recorded the recurrence, and no session was ever routed to it. An `in_flight` item with owner `unassigned` is the checklist-side form of the exact contradiction the operator's 2026-09-05 directive names (MI-134: no work in a working state without an owner) — it reads as covered and is not. Honest state: QUEUED, nobody on it. ⚠️ RECURRED 2026-09-05, and the recurrence is the finding — this row was `landed_unproven` and is now PROVEN to regenerate. INSTANCE 2, measured 11:00Z: identical guard line, different PR — `#10921: terminal is 'closed_unmerged' and there is no disposition` — with FIVE reconcile PRs stacked unmergeable (#11041 07:40Z, #11046 08:20Z, #11051 09:00Z, #11056 09:31Z, #11058 10:37Z) over ~3h20m. Instance 1 (#10780, 2026-09-03) was closed by writing that one disposition (#10941) and CLOSING EIGHT stacked PRs. Instance 2 was closed the same way: write the disposition (#11062), close five. ⚠️ THAT WORKAROUND IS NOW THE ESTABLISHED NON-FIX. Twice is a mechanism, not bad luck: a reconciler CANNOT supply a disposition, because a disposition answers WHY a human closed a PR, and 'superseded' / 'the operator refused it' / 'the author gave up' are opposite next actions. So every PR closed without merging re-jams the generator, and each jammed run opens ANOTHER PR — unbounded in merges to main, not self-limiting. ⚠️ AND NOTHING SIGNALS THE REASON IS OWED until the stack has already formed and someone reads a failing guard log while draining the queue; both instances were found exactly that way. Do NOT fix by auto-generating a disposition (that manufactures a reason nobody gave) or by relaxing --strict (the guard is correct and is the only thing stopping a verdict being read without its condition). Candidates: the reconciler REFUSES to move a row it cannot disposition and says so loudly instead of emitting an unmergeable PR; it closes its own superseded predecessors; or a `disposition_owed` signal surfaces where a manager sees it first. || Full instance-2 write-up: BL-20260905-AN-UNDISPOSITIONED-CLOSED-PR-DEADLOCKS-EVERY-RECONCILE-PR-AND-THEY-STACK-UNBOUNDEDLY. ⚠️ THAT ROW WAS FILED AS IF NEW: backlog_append's duplicate probe searches the three BACKLOGS and not MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, so a manager can re-diagnose a live checklist item at full cost and the tool stays quiet. Filed separately. || PRIOR (instance 1) NOTE PRESERVED: MEASURED 2026-09-03T12:4xZ by running the failing guard against #10938's own OPEN-PRS.json: `open_pr_record.py --strict` -> settled=undispositioned, one finding — "#10780: `terminal` is 'closed_unmerged' and there is no `disposition`. The PR is not on `main` and nobody said why". THE GUARD IS DOING ITS JOB; the missing thing is knowledge, not machinery. ⚠️ IT IS A GENERATOR, NOT A BACKLOG: reconcile-open-prs fires on every merge to main, so the count grows with normal work — 7 open as of 12:34Z (#10901 #10907 #10913 #10924 #10928 #10934 #10938) and

items.title: pr-landing's hold vocabulary has no term for queue serialisation, so the manager branch must force-fit one
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-03T12:5xZ on this very branch. The manager branch deleted its own .github/pr-automerge-requests/ file (deliberately -- an armed manager branch merging on its own green is what jammed the queue: 26 merges, 19 touching a shared register, #10918 dirtied three times). pr-landing-guard R6 then correctly failed the branch for declaring `self` while unarmed. Demoting to `hold` needs a term from a CLOSED vocabulary of five: awaiting_evidence, changes_landing_machinery, depends_on_unmerged_pr, operator_asked_to_hold, tier_2_3_needs_approval. NONE of them is 'the manager is serialising its own queue'. ⚠️ `changes_landing_machinery` was tried and R8 REFUSED it, CORRECTLY -- the guard excludes a branch's own declaration file so the excuse cannot be free for everybody, and .github/pr-automerge-requests/* is not in its recognised list either. That refusal is the guard working, not a bug. Settled on `depends_on_unmerged_pr: #10920`, which is TRUE and checkable (this branch's MERGE-QUEUE/CHECKLIST rows describe #10920 as position 1 in flight, so landing them first commits a register stale on arrival) but is NARROWER than the real reason, and the imperfection is DISCLOSED in hold_text rather than hidden. ⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY WIDENING R8 TO ACCEPT A BRANCH'S OWN FILES. That is the exact presence-only weakness R8's own comment cites new-table-wiring-guard for. The question is whether a `queue_serialisation` term should exist, or whether the manager branch should simply arm and rely on hand-merging -- and that is a design call, not a patch. DONE = either a sixth term exists with its own plant + control in --self-test, or it is RULED that no such term should exist and the manager branch's correct declaration is recorded.

items.title: manager-scope-guard R6 goes permanently red on a long-lived manager branch, because a squash-merged commit never leaves the range
items.owner: MI-95 (session_017DxuurbMW5ex5Q1f7xATqW owns this guard; idle, review_ready)
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-03T13:0xZ on the manager branch. check_manager_scope.py --base origin/main grades every commit in origin/main...HEAD. This repo SQUASH-merges, so a manager branch's commits stay in that range after their content has landed on main -- the branch is currently 55 ahead while most of that content is already merged. R6 therefore re-grades HISTORICAL heartbeats forever: 7 findings today, 6 of them my own lease heartbeats from 08:0xZ-12:0xZ where SESSIONS.json was 129-479 minutes stale, and 1 R2 from the PREVIOUS manager (e84dcf03, session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, editing trainer-capture-watch.yml). ⚠️ THE FINDINGS ARE TRUE AND THE UNDERLYING CONDITION IS NOW REPAIRED -- SESSIONS.json was brought current at 13:0xZ from a live list_sessions read -- but a commit already made cannot be un-made, so NO amount of correct future conduct can clear the red. That is the defect: a guard whose verdict cannot be earned back stops being a control and becomes a thing to route around, which is the desensitised-alarm class this repo treats as P1. ⚠️ THE EXCEPTION FILE DOES NOT COVER IT. manager-scope-exception.yaml entries are `paths`-scoped (they excuse touching a named path, i.e. R2); R6 is about a STALE SUPERVISION RECORD, not a path, so there is nothing to name. Do not stretch the schema to fit -- that is the presence-only weakness the file's own header warns about. ⚠️ AND DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY GRADING ONLY THE NEWEST COMMIT: R6 exists precisely to catch a run of heartbeats made while supervision lapsed, and a last-commit-only rule would miss exactly that. The candidate shapes are (a) grade commits since the branch's last merge to main rather than since origin/main, or (b) let a REPAIR commit that brings SESSIONS.json current close out the earlier findings it repaired, recorded rather than silently forgiven. Both are design calls. DONE = a manager branch that has repaired its supervision record can go green on R6 WITHOUT the lapse being erased from the record, with a plant AND a control in --self-test.

items.title: manager-scope-guard derives authorship from a self-written trailer, so a MIS-stamped commit is a false violation — and the inverse is an open evasion
items.prs: #10895 is the live instance; the CLASS fix is on claude/mi106-manager-scope-authorship
items.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-03T14:0xZ while trying to land #10895. check_manager_scope grades it a VIOLATION: commit 5504200c touches scripts/notify_on_pull.py and tests/test_notify_merge_pings.py under a `Claude-Session:` trailer naming session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ — the PREVIOUS DAY'S MANAGER — so the guard reads it as a manager doing an item. ⚠️ THE EVIDENCE SAYS THE TRAILER IS WRONG, and I am stating that as a reading rather than a fact I can prove: the commit body is written in the MI-83 WORKER's voice ('a defect in what I shipped', 'The reason it could not be read is MINE') about #10857, which is MI-83's own PR; the PR body's footer names session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU (MI-83); and that session was alive at 06:13:07Z when the commit was authored. So the guard produced a TRUE finding about what it can see and a FALSE one about what happened. ⚠️ THE INVERSE IS THE DANGEROUS HALF AND IT IS UNGUARDED: authorship is taken from a trailer the author writes themselves, so a manager wanting to do an item can simply stamp a worker's session id and the guard vouches for it. The guard already discloses that UNTRAILERED commits are 'a gap in coverage, not evidence of compliance' — a MIS-trailered one is not covered by that caveat and reads as graded. A guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard, which is the lesson its own siblings cite new-table-wiring-guard for. ⚠️ I DID NOT FORCE #10895 THROUGH AND DID NOT WRITE AN EXCEPTION FOR IT. The exception file is for INCIDENTS by its own header, not for excusing a mis-stamp; rewriting the commit would mean rewriting history on another session's branch, which is forbidden; and merging past a failing required check to get a result I want is the thing the whole landing discipline exists to stop. #10895 therefore stays OPEN, which is a real cost: it is the PR that makes OI-20260902-PER-MERGE-PING verifiable at all. DONE = authorship is established from something the author does not solely control, or the trailer's limits are stated in the guard's own output so a mis-stamp reads as `unattributed` rather than as a graded verdict — with a plant AND a control in --self-test. Resolving #10895 specifically may just need its author session to re-commit with the right trailer.

=== 2026-09-04 MANAGER: ROUTED to session_01Bh89HtTcDzZqhfSCzZ2Lmp under a NEW object WO-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-AUTHORSHIP-SELF-DECLARED, which takes the 8th and last in_flight slot (ceiling 8, now exactly at it). Chosen over MI-108 for the slot because this is what unblocks #10895, and #10895 is what makes OI-20260902-PER-MERGE-PING verifiable at all. All three shortcuts stay forbidden in the prompt, and the cheaper instance-only fix is named AS instance-only so it cannot be reported as closing the class.

⚠️ 2026-09-04, by session_01Bh89HtTcDzZqhfSCzZ2Lmp — THE CLASS IS FIXED; #10895 IS NOT UNBLOCKED, AND THOSE ARE DIFFERENT SENTENCES. check_manager_scope now derives, from MANAGER-LEASE.json's own git history, the intervals in which each session actually HELD the lease, and grades every commit into three states that do not collapse: `attributed` (graded), `unattributed` (no trailer, OR a trailer the register CONTRADICTS — never graded, reported loudly, and it now DOMINATES `clean`), and `not_manager`. On #10895's range 5504200c now reads `⚠️ UNATTRIBUTED ... the register CONTRADICTS the trailer` instead of an R2 violation: session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ released the lease at 2026-09-02T21:38:05Z and session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd heartbeated at 06:06:14Z and 06:35:44Z either side of the commit's 06:13:07Z author time. Self-test 19 cases -> 23: a PLANT (mis-stamp -> `unattributed`, no finding) and a CONTROL (same diff, same trailer, authored INSIDE the window -> still `violation`), so the plant cannot be satisfied by a guard that has merely stopped enforcing R2.

⚠️ IT CONTRADICTS; IT NEVER CONFIRMS, and the guard says so on EVERY verdict including clean ones. The lease register is evidence the commit's author cannot reach back and change, but the author DATE it is joined against is ordinary git metadata and is author-settable. So this catches the CARELESS mis-stamp — the measured one, whose cause 7a93261f states outright: the spawn dispatch handed the sub-session the MANAGER's session URL to stamp — and NOT the deliberate one. A manager stamping a live worker's id inside that worker's own window remains undetected; closing that honestly needs a per-session credential this repo does not have. The evasion is NAMED in a standing disclosure rather than implied away.

⚠️ #10895 STAYS RED ON A SECOND, DIFFERENT DEFECT MEASURED WHILE DOING THIS, and it was never in this row: R7 fails 5244dafb — the MANAGER's own merge commit — for '223 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat'. That number is an artifact: `heartbeat_cadence_gap` reads the previous heartbeat from `sha~1`, which on a merge commit is the WORKER branch's stale lease blob. The register reachable from that same commit holds same-holder heartbeats at 08:32:50Z and 09:21:42Z — a 49-minute gap, inside the 90-minute TTL. The manager was on cadence. FILED as BL-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-R7-MEASURES-CADENCE-ALONG-THE-FIRST-PARENT-SO-A-MANAGER-MERGE-INTO-A-WORKER-BRANCH-READS-AS-A-LAPSE rather than folded into this PR: different rule (R7 not R2), different mechanism (parent traversal not authorship), and adjacent to MI-105 (R6/range membership) which already has an owner on this same guard. ⚠️ It is INVISIBLE from #10895's own tree — that tree's guard revision predates R7 entirely — and appears only under main's guard, which is what CI runs.

⚠️ THE CHEAPER INSTANCE-ONLY ROUTE WAS NOT TAKEN, and is now moot for R2: session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU re-committing 5504200c under its own trailer would have fixed the INSTANCE and left the evasion open. It would not clear R7 either.

⚠️ 2026-09-04, LANDING BLOCKED BY A THIRD DEFECT THAT IS NOT MINE AND NOT #10895's — AND IT IS BLOCKING THE WHOLE QUEUE. PR #10977 carries the MI-106 fix; `guards`, `pytest-collect`, `repo-inventory` and `open-and-automerge` are GREEN on 7773db2d, and `pytest-run` — a REQUIRED context — is RED. It is red on #10975 too (MI-109, another session, a disjoint diff), finishing at the same 08:38Z. Cause: three ceiling assertions in tests/test_work_digest.py, plus work_digest's own self-test 7, build their CONTROL from the LIVE repo (`wd.build_digest('HEAD','HEAD')`) and assert the repo is UNDER the WIP ceiling. It is not: 8 in_flight work objects against a ceiling of 8, which is LEGAL (check_wip_ceiling refuses the NINTH). The renderer is right; the tests' control is unsound. ⚠️ The 8th object is WO-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-AUTHORSHIP-SELF-DECLARED — this item's own — added to main by c17b4e7c (#10974), so spawning this session is what reddened the repo's required test check. Verified pre-existing: `scripts/ops/work_digest.py --self-test` prints 'self-test 7 ... FAIL' on an UNMODIFIED origin/main checkout. FILED as BL-20260904-WORK-DIGEST-CEILING-TESTS-READ-LIVE-REPO-STATE-SO-PYTEST-RUN-GOES-RED-REPO-WIDE-THE-MOMENT-WIP-LEGITIMATELY-HITS-THE-CEILING, AND FIXED IN #10977. ⚠️ I FIRST WROTE THAT IT COULD NOT BE FIXED HERE BECAUSE tests/** AND scripts/ops/** ARE NOT ON pr-landing-guard's TIER1_SURFACE. THAT WAS WRONG — I checked the list and BOTH ARE on it (only automation/**, which is what broke the self-land declaration earlier on this branch, is not). The mechanical objection did not exist, and with the whole queue jammed the fix is carried here: both arms of each ceiling assertion are now CONSTRUCTED (inFlight = WIP_CEILING - 1, ceilingHit = False) in tests/test_work_digest.py and in work_digest's self-test 7, so neither can pass or fail on repo state. Mutation-verified rather than assumed: with the renderer's `if wip['ceilingHit']:` branch disabled all three fail, and restored all three pass. tests/test_work_digest.py: 36 passed. The ceiling was NOT lowered and no in_flight object was dropped to get under it.
items.adjudicated_2026_09_06: BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION, not a verdict on the work. State read `in_flight` with owner `session_01Bh89HtTcDzZqhfSCzZ2Lmp`, which a LIVE list_sessions read on 2026-09-06T08:0xZ graded ARCHIVED (population: 180 sessions enumerated back to 2026-08-02; exactly ONE was RUNNING and it was the manager). So the register asserted this was being worked while no worker existed. items.title: Local LLM: neither size arm carries weight, and the path is NOT shelved — the next experiment must vary task framing, not parameter count
items.note:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-03, verbatim: 'We need to backlog this for further research - there's no point in wasting resources on a bad model, but we have to continue finding/building a production worthy llm.' ⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE `carries_no_weight` OPTION I OFFERED, which said shelve the path. The operator split it: STOP spending on these two arms, KEEP the goal. Recording it as shelved would have closed a direction they explicitly want continued — the more expensive of the two possible errors. SETTLED: neither the 1.5B nor the 3B carries weight; nothing is adopted; no further benchmarking of THESE arms is scheduled. STILL OPEN: whether a local LLM can do useful work here at all. ⚠️ THE OBVIOUS NEXT EXPERIMENT IS THE WRONG ONE. Both size arms have now been measured and both failed on ANSWER QUALITY, not throughput — the 1.5B fabricated a causal claim and misattributed a fault to venue liquidity when the defect was our own sizer; the 3B hedges instead of inventing and still never names the mechanism. A third parameter count varies the axis that has already been shown not to be the binding one. What has NEVER been varied is the TASK FRAMING and the RETRIEVAL: both arms were asked an open repo question with no grounded context, which is the setup most likely to produce invention. ROUTED TO THE ML-REVIEW BACKLOG, not health — that file owns AI experiment follow-ups and new-manifest ideas. DONE = a next experiment is proposed that varies framing/grounding rather than size, or the operator rules the path closed.

items.title: run_guards.py grades a MISSING test runner as FAIL, so 'we could not look' is unreadable as anything but 'this is broken'
items.note:

So 3 of the 5 red lines said nothing about the code. ⚠️ THIS IS THE COLLAPSED-STATES DEFECT IN THE TOOL WHOSE JOB IS TO SAY WHAT IS WRONG, and it misleads in BOTH directions: trust the count and you debug code that is fine; learn to discount those three and you stop reading them, which is the desensitized-alarm P1. ⚠️ AND IT IS THE MIRROR OF A HAZARD THIS MANAGER ALREADY PUTS IN EVERY SPAWN PROMPT — that run_guards can report FAIL 0 on an INCOMPLETE run. Same collapse, opposite side: silence where it did not look, and noise where it did not look. ⚠️ INSTALLING PYTEST IS NOT THE FIX and must not be recorded as one; the grader must carry a third state. Filed as BL-20260903-RUN-GUARDS-REPORTS-FAIL-WHERE-THE-TEST-RUNNER-IS-ABSENT-SO-COULD-NOT-LOOK-READS-AS-BROKEN.

=== 2026-09-04 MANAGER — THE ROW IS WIDER THAN ITS TITLE, and the wider half is the dangerous one. This row says run_guards.py grades a MISSING runner as FAIL. items.title: handoff_check's lease check passes ONLY on held_by_me, so releasing the lease — the correct final act — makes the readiness verdict go red
items.note: FOUND BY RUNNING THE WIND-DOWN PROTOCOL END TO END FOR THE FIRST TIME, 2026-09-03. check_lease PASSES only on `held_by_me` and FAILS everything else with 'A handover of something you do not hold is not a handover.' Correct for expired / unheld / held_by_other. WRONG FOR `released`, which is the state a correct handover ENDS in — manager_lease's own release output says 'The next session may claim' and warns that an unseen release locks the successor out for the full TTL. So the protocol can grade `ready` only in the state the manager is supposed to leave, and goes red the moment it does the right thing. ⚠️ A MANAGER FOLLOWING IT LITERALLY WOULD HAND OVER A LEASE IT STILL HELD — the exact outcome the check exists to prevent. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT `released` -> PASS UNCONDITIONALLY: a release by ANOTHER session says nothing about this manager and must stay a FAIL, so the check has to read who released it. OBSERVED DIRECTLY: with the lease held, `[PASS] lease`; after release, the same command grades the same manager FAIL with nothing else changed. Filed as BL-20260903-HANDOFF-CHECK-CANNOT-TELL-A-DELIBERATE-RELEASE-FROM-AN-EXPIRY-SO-A-CLEAN-HANDOVER-GRADES-FAIL.

items.title: handoff_check grades the OUTGOING manager as an unregistered LIVE session, so a clean takeover cannot reach `ready`
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04 on the takeover run. `live_registry` FAILED naming exactly one session — session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd — which is the PREVIOUS MANAGER, idle, and which released the lease at 2026-09-03T17:42:47Z. Population: 60 observed, excluded self 1 / terminal 9 / other-manager 49, graded 1. It is absent from SESSIONS.json because a manager registers its SUB-sessions, never itself, so the predecessor is structurally unregistrable and every takeover will reproduce this. ⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY REGISTERING THE PREDECESSOR AS A SUB-SESSION — that writes a false parentage into the one file a cold manager trusts, which is worse than the false alarm. The cheap true fix is an exclusion the lease already knows about: MANAGER-LEASE.json carries `previous_holder` and `released_by`, so a session named there is a predecessor manager and belongs in the existing `other-manager` exclusion bucket. SIBLING OF MI-111 and the same shape: both are cases where doing the correct thing at handover turns the readiness verdict red, which is how a check gets ignored rather than obeyed. ⚠️ THE CHECK IS NOT WRONG TO NOTICE IT — an idle predecessor holding context IS a real session — so the remedy is a named exclusion with a reason, never a blanket suppression.

items.title: the PR-queue watcher's escalation exits 1 into a workflow log and reaches no human, so a 17.4h-standing page was found only by a manager reading job logs by hand
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04 from the job log of scheduled run #8 (33839153592). ⚠️ FIRST READING WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED SO NOBODY REPEATS IT: 4 of the 6 scheduled runs conclude `failure` (#3 #5 #7 #8 fail; #4 #6 succeed) and I was about to file that as 'the watcher fails two-thirds of the time'. IT IS THE WATCHER WORKING. The job exits 1 DELIBERATELY to escalate — run #8's log reads `escalate: True -- the condition has stood 17.4h since the last page (floor 12.0h)`, `receipt : written`, and `##[error]PR-QUEUE ESCALATION -- open PRs are waiting on a merge decision past the threshold`. Reading `conclusion: failure` as 'this mechanism is broken' is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A, which this repo has a guard for. THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THE DELIVERY: the escalation's only surface is a red workflow run and a line in a job log. It writes no pending-pings row, sends no Telegram, and raises no notification — so the page had been standing 17.4h across at least two scheduled runs (#7 21:19Z, #8 05:04Z) and reached nobody until a manager opened the job log by hand on 2026-09-04. A red run in a repo whose automation PRs are routinely red is invisible; that is the desensitised-alarm shape CLAUDE.md names as a P1 in its own right. ⚠️ WHAT IT WAS PAGING ABOUT WAS TRUE AND ACTIONABLE: 14 PRs waiting on a merge decision, worst 145.3h. ⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MAKING THE RUN EXIT 0 — that removes the only signal there currently is. The fix is to give the escalation a surface a human actually reads, and the repo already has the pattern: a pending-pings row plus a durable receipt, the way work-digest does it. ⚠️ AND NOTE THE COUPLING TO MI-113: pending-pings.jsonl has no row-aware merge driver, so anything that appends to it from CI inherits that conflict problem. Establish that before choosing the surface. Manager filed, did not build — .github/workflows/ and scripts/ci/ are worker paths.

items.title: pr-landing's hold_reason vocabulary has no token for 'a human/manager merges this', so two independent authors invented `manager_merges` and both PRs went red
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04. HOLD_REASONS in scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py is a closed vocabulary of five: changes_landing_machinery, depends_on_unmerged_pr, awaiting_evidence, operator_asked_to_hold, tier_2_3_needs_approval. The repo's own working convention is 'DRAFT PR, the manager merges', and there is no token for it. TWO INDEPENDENT AUTHORS REACHED FOR THE SAME NON-EXISTENT TOKEN: .github/pr-landing/night-brief.json (#10877) and .github/pr-landing/mi81-capture-watch-observed.json, the latter already carrying a hand-written correction note from the session that hit it first. Two authors inventing the identical token is a vocabulary gap, not two mistakes. ⚠️ THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: hold_reason is graded by R7, a required check, so an invented token makes the PR RED and unmergeable -- #10877 sat red from 2026-09-03T07:31 until 2026-09-04T07:52 on this alone, while its content was strictly better than what main carries. A PR held for a good reason should be held; it should not be RED, because red is indistinguishable from broken and this repo already has an alarm-fatigue P1. ⚠️ DO NOT simply add `manager_merges` without deciding the question underneath it: is 'the manager merges' a HOLD at all, or is it the normal Tier-1 path with `landing: self` and the route left unarmed? Both PRs that hit this declared `hold`, and the second reading may be the correct one -- in which case the fix is documentation and a clearer error, not a sixth token. ⚠️ AND THE ERROR MESSAGE IS ALREADY GOOD (it names the closed vocabulary), so 'improve the message' is not the fix either; both authors read it and still had to pick a token that did not mean what they meant. Manager filed, did not build -- scripts/ci/ is a worker path.

items.title: MERGE-QUEUE.json has no row-aware merge driver either, so the one register a CI rule enforces conflicts on every concurrent edit
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04 while resolving #10977, which had gone `dirty`. With the row-aware driver ARMED, docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json auto-merged CLEANLY with zero hand editing; docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json CONFLICTED and had to be resolved by hand. Cause is identical to MI-113: .gitattributes maps merge=jsonregister onto exactly five registers (health-review-backlog, OPEN-ITEMS, MANAGER-CHECKLIST, SESSIONS, OPEN-PRS) and MERGE-QUEUE.json is not among them -- `grep -c MERGE-QUEUE .gitattributes` returns 0. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE OF THE CLASS, not just another one: MERGE-QUEUE.json is the register whose invariant check_manager_scope R8 actively enforces, and the one the MANAGER rewrites several times a day by the queue duty. So the file most likely to be edited concurrently is one of the two with no driver. ⚠️ AND THE CONFLICT IS UNRESOLVABLE BY ITS AUTHOR: GitHub does not run custom merge drivers and update_pull_request_branch refuses, so a sub-session whose PR touches this file cannot free itself however attentive it is -- it needs someone with an armed clone. That is a queue-wide serialisation cost, not a cosmetic one. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT OBVIOUSLY THE SAME AS MI-113's. pending-pings.jsonl is append-only JSONL where `merge=union` may fit; MERGE-QUEUE.json is a small JSON object whose `entries` list is REPLACED wholesale by the manager rather than appended to, so a row-aware union could silently resurrect a queue entry the manager deliberately removed. Establish the right semantics before wiring a driver; a wrong driver here is worse than the conflict. Manager filed, did not build -- .gitattributes and scripts/ops/ are worker paths.

items.title: test_work_digest builds its control from the LIVE work store, so the whole suite goes red whenever in_flight legitimately reaches the ceiling
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04, and it blocked the entire merge queue for ~90 minutes. tests/test_work_digest.py::test_ceiling_hit_is_loud_and_under_ceiling_is_not calls wd.build_digest('HEAD','HEAD') -- the REAL work store at the git ref -- and uses it as the NOT-HIT control: `assert 'WIP CEILING HIT' not in quiet`. So the control is only valid while production happens to be under the ceiling. The manager took in_flight to 8 of 8 at 07:43 by creating one work object -- a state scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py explicitly grades `OK` -- and three tests went red on EVERY PR that runs the suite. ⚠️ THE CODE UNDER TEST WAS CORRECT THROUGHOUT. The digest was right to say WIP CEILING HIT; the ceiling WAS hit. The test asserts that production is not in a state production is allowed to be in. That is the inverse of the usual failure: not a green that checked nothing, but a RED that indicts nothing. ⚠️ IT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL IT BITES, for two reasons worth knowing. (1) pytest-run appears to be path-filtered: docs-only PRs completed it in 12-19s while PRs touching comms/ or src/ took 17-25min, so several manager landings merged green while the defect was already live. (2) The digest reads at a GIT REF, not the working tree, so a local fix does not take effect until it is COMMITTED -- the manager re-ran the tests after correcting the lifecycle, saw them still fail, and briefly concluded the diagnosis was wrong. HOW IT WAS IDENTIFIED, since the same reasoning finds the next one: #10919 is a PURE DATA ADDITION whose pytest-run PASSED on 2026-09-03 and failed on 2026-09-04 with no test change in its diff. A pure-data PR going red is the signal that the BASE moved, not the PR. ⚠️ MAIN'S OWN pytest-run RUNS ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF A GREEN BASE: they complete in 18-77s against a 17-25min PR run, so they are not running the suite. Do not clear this by pointing at them. THE FIX IS A SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for the control -- construct a store known to be under the ceiling rather than reading the live one. ⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' it by keeping in_flight below the ceiling: that makes an operational limit into a test constraint and hands every future manager a CI failure for using a documented allowance. items.title: F6 is undischargeable on demand: both on-demand ping tools write to a gitignored dir, so a sandbox ping is lost and reports success

Same family as BL-20260902-PING-DELIVERY-IS-MARKED-ON-A-LOCAL-FILE-WRITE-SO-DELIVERED-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE, one hop earlier. ⚠️ SO A MANAGER CANNOT DISCHARGE F6 ON DEMAND: the two obvious tools are both wrong, and the one that works fires on work-object LIFECYCLE DIFFS rather than on a manager's action count -- so a manager with 10 actions and no lifecycle change has no available action that turns the check green.
