items.title: manager-scope R7 picks its 'previous heartbeat' from the wrong lease run — a CLAIM over an expired lease is graded as a late check-in, and a merge reads sha~1's stale worker blob
items.note: TWO measured instances, ONE root, and the root is that R7 never establishes that the blob it compares against belongs to the same lease RUN, reached along the right parent. (a) MEASURED tonight on this manager's own re-claim commit cc984fec: R7 fails it at '746 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat'. The 746 minutes are REAL and the failure is the point — the manager was idle twelve hours — but a CLAIM over an EXPIRED lease is a RECOVERY, not a late check-in, and R7's own docstring already exempts the sibling case: it compares only against 'a previous heartbeat by the SAME holder — a handover is not a lapse, and grading one would fail the incoming manager for the outgoing one's silence.' That reasoning transfers verbatim to a lease that DIED and was re-claimed. (b) The #10895 face, filed by MI-106's session rather than folded into its own PR (the correct disposition): R7 reads the previous blob from `sha~1`, which on a MERGE commit is the worker branch's stale lease, so merge 5244dafb reads as a lapse when the true same-holder gap was 49min, inside the 90min TTL — BL-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-R7-MEASURES-CADENCE-ALONG-THE-FIRST-PARENT-SO-A-MANAGER-MERGE-INTO-A-WORKER-BRANCH-READS-AS-A-LAPSE. ⚠️ THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS THE INCENTIVE, NOT THE RED: as written, the cheapest route to a green PR for a returning manager is to NOT PUSH THE LEASE — i.e. not record the lapse — while MANAGER-LEASE.json's own header says an unpushed claim protects nothing. A guard whose cheapest evasion is deleting the evidence is the new-table-wiring-guard shape this repo already names. ⚠️ OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, asked directly as a popup and answered 'Fix R7, route it to a session': fix the guard, do NOT write a manager-scope-exception entry, and accept that #10982 stays red until this lands. Recorded as a decision, not as a manager's own judgement. ⚠️ THE DEAD INTERVAL MUST STILL BE REPORTED. Reporting 746 minutes of no manager is the single most valuable thing the guard said tonight; what changes is where it is CHARGED, never whether it is SEEN — a silent pass here would be worse than tonight's false red. And R7's real case is untouched: a manager that is ALIVE and silent past one TTL must still fail. BLOCKS: #10982 (the manager register state, MI-118..MI-121, the session-cap resolution, and the record of the twelve-hour gap itself) and #10895. ⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-04T23:44:07Z: MERGED as a0b776fa. ⚠️ THE DEADLOCK IS BROKEN AND IT WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: the manager re-ran check_manager_scope.py --base origin/main on a fresh heartbeat commit under the corrected guard and got rc=0, verdict `unattributed` (one commit in range carries no Claude-Session trailer, which is the three-state grading MI-106 shipped and is not a violation). Before the fix the identical commit shape graded ✗R6 ✗R7. So the manager's lease heartbeat can now reach main, #10982 is unblocked, and #10895's own R7 face should clear too — that second half is NOT yet confirmed and must be checked against #10895 itself rather than inferred from this. ⚠️ CLOSED 2026-09-05T00:13:48Z: manager verified rc=0 directly on a fresh heartbeat commit; the identical shape graded ✗R6 ✗R7 before. Author self-test 28/28, session archived. TWO RESIDUES, both filed as MI-125 rather than folded into a closed row: (a) face (b) — #10895's sha~1-on-a-merge half — SHOULD clear under the same fix and that is an INFERENCE, unverified against #10895 itself; (b) the author's closing summary says 'R6 root unfixed' — R6 passes here only because SESSIONS.json is fresh, and the wrong-parent selection has not been shown absent from it.

items.title: a manager that stops acting is detected by nothing — bound idle with a durable wake
items.note: MEASURED, and the measurement is this manager: last act ~09:45Z, operator asked at 21:53Z. TWELVE HOURS against a standing directive of thirty minutes — twenty-four times the bar — and NOTHING NOTICED. Not a check, not a probe, not a Routine, not another session. ⚠️ THE MANAGER DID NOT DIE, and that is what makes this a different object from the reaper. It stayed alive and connected and simply stopped taking turns. Every mechanism here is aimed at DEATH (the lease's 90min TTL, time-based takeover, 'a session that dies cannot hand over') and death is the case already covered. ALIVE-AND-SILENT is covered by nothing. COST, measured: #10975 was GREEN at 15:02:46Z with the operator's Tier-2 approval ALREADY GIVEN and sat unmerged ~7h; all three sub-sessions were at need_input by 09:41Z each naming the ONE act it waited on, and MI-107's was a restart go-ahead already given; the lease sat expired 746 minutes, claimable by anyone and claimed by nobody; the manager branch went dirty against 28 commits. ⚠️ THE LEASE IS NOT A DETECTOR — it EXPIRES correctly, and nothing READS an expired lease and acts. ⚠️ NOR IS R7 — it grades a heartbeat only when a commit ADVANCES one, so a manager writing no commits is graded by nothing at all. Same distinction CLAUDE.md already draws for BL-20260903-THE-PR-QUEUE-WATCHER-CANNOT-SEE-A-TEN-MINUTE-STALL, where every gap was 15–35min while a green PR sat ten minutes and the operator noticed first. Tonight is that finding at 48x. ⚠️ OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, asked as a popup and answered 'A durable wake, so idle is bounded' — over a reaper and over building both. The reaper is real, complementary and DEFERRED, to be filed as its own row, not folded in. ⚠️ CREATING THE ROUTINE IS A DEPLOY, NOT THE DONE-CONDITION. The bar is an OBSERVED wake into a real session that then ACTS on something waiting — the same bar OI-20260902-DECISION-DRAIN-ROUTINE-DOES-NOT-EXIST sets for its own stage (4). CONSTRAINTS carried into the spawn: no minted credentials (operator, 2026-09-02, 'no minted tokens, ever'); no GitHub cron (work-digest fired 5x against 24 declared, probes ~4h50m late, #10845 already moved the digest off cron); and NO further reminder or checklist line — that instruction already exists, was read at session start, and produced the gap. ⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-04T23:44:07Z: MERGED as 5f397509. Its delivery half was OBSERVED before the merge: at 23:09:19Z the wake fired into the manager session as an out-of-band turn and reported the lease 901 minutes stale — a true reading of origin/main that the manager's own reflex disputed, and the reading that exposed the heartbeat-never-reaches-main deadlock. ⚠️ MERGED IS NOT ARMED. The scheduling half needs the operator to create the Routine from the claude.ai Routines UI with the Claude Code Remote connector attached (create_trigger via MCP yields sessions with no mcp__* tools, which the poke step requires; `connectors` is refused for this org). The prompt is now ON MAIN at docs/claude/work/manager-wake-routine-prompt.md. Until it exists, the manager's cadence is a hand-rolled send_later poke, which is scaffolding and not the mechanism. ⚠️ 2026-09-05T00:13:48Z: session ARCHIVED, complete. ⚠️ ITS OWN CLOSING SUMMARY SAYS 'PR #1234' — that number is GARBLED and must not be propagated; the real PR is #11014, merged as 5f397509, verified by the manager against origin/main. It also names a second operator-owed item the manager had not recorded: stop-hook-git-check.sh false-alarms on shallow clones. Filed under MI-125.

items.title: three residues from the MI-122/MI-123 pair: R6's root, #10895's unverified R7 face, and a stop-hook false alarm on shallow clones
items.note: Filed 2026-09-05 rather than folded into two closed rows — three separate facts, none of which was in either object's done_condition. (1) R6 ROOT UNFIXED (author's own closing summary, MI-122). R6 grades a lease heartbeat against SESSIONS.json staleness and passes on the manager branch ONLY because the registry is fresh; the wrong-parent selection that afflicted R7 has NOT been shown absent from R6. Measured tonight: a lease-only commit built on origin/main graded ✗R6 AND ✗R7, and only R7 was fixed. (2) #10895's R7 FACE IS UNVERIFIED. It SHOULD clear under a0b776fa and that is an INFERENCE. Check it against #10895 itself before cutting its blocked_on edge — the repo's own rule is that a guard passing elsewhere is not evidence about this PR. (3) stop-hook-git-check.sh FALSE-ALARMS ON SHALLOW CLONES (reported by MI-123). Every sub-session container is a shallow clone, so this fires on all of them; the manager hit the same shallow-clone class earlier today reading ping carriers and reported a false negative from it before `git fetch --unshallow`. NOT yet independently verified by the manager — recorded as the author's report, not as a manager measurement. || ⚠️ PART (1) NOW HAS A LIVE INCIDENT BEHIND IT, 2026-09-05, and it is no longer a suspicion. R6 KILLED PR #11031 OUTRIGHT — the manager's own 32-commit management record — and the guard was CORRECT: commit bfdf2fa3 advanced the lease heartbeat while SESSIONS.json was 154 min stale against a 90-min TTL, because the manager had been idle 143 minutes and the lease had expired. bfdf2fa3 was an ANCESTOR of the branch tip, so it sat permanently inside the graded range and the PR could NEVER go green however many later commits fixed the state. ⚠️ THAT IS THE ACTIONABLE SHAPE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: R6 grades HISTORICAL COMMITS in the range, so a lapse becomes UNMERGEABLE FOREVER rather than correctable — there is no "I have since fixed it" path. The only exits available were (a) manager-scope-exception.yaml, refused because it is for live INCIDENTS and spending it on a manager's own lapse is the cheaper-to-lie-to-than-to-satisfy failure, or (b) rebuild the branch from main, which is what the operator chose — and which SILENTLY DROPPED three filed backlog rows and rewound five generated registers, both caught only afterwards. So the guard being right about the lapse cost a rebuild that caused two further defects. A rule that can only be satisfied by discarding history is worth examining even when its finding is true. NOT a proposal to weaken R6 — the finding WAS true and the manager said so publicly — but the fixing session should read this incident before deciding what "R6's root" means. || ROUTED 2026-09-05T07:41Z. Its (2) half also unblocks #10895 in the queue. || ALL THREE RESIDUES SETTLED WITH EVIDENCE, verified by the manager against the DIFF rather than the session summary. PR #11044, auto-merge armed. (1) R6 ROOT — FIXED, NOT WEAKENED, which was the explicit constraint. "Advanced" now decides against EVERY PARENT rather than sha~1; sha~1 is the FIRST parent, which on a merge is the branch being merged INTO, so when a manager merges main into a worker branch the lease's prior state arrives on the SECOND parent and R6 graded a commit that ADVANCED NOTHING. That is R7's MI-122 root, left in R6 — exactly what MI-125 was filed to establish. And it was MEASURED before fixing: on the R6 face the merge was GRADED at gap=75min under a 90min TTL, and the same shape with a registry 160min stale FAILED, i.e. one arithmetic step from a false red, not latent. (2) #10895's R7 FACE — CLEARS when measured against #10895 ITSELF, so the carried inference was right and is now a measurement. ⚠️ BUT THE PR IS STILL BLOCKED, by a MERGE CONFLICT and an unresolved R2 that main's guard grades `unattributed` — NOT by R7. Filed as BL-20260905-PR-10895-IS-BLOCKED-BY-A-MERGE-CONFLICT-AND-AN-UNATTRIBUTED-R2-NOT-BY-R7. That is actionable and is the manager's next queue item. (3) THE STOP HOOK — REPRODUCED, and the reproduction OVERTURNED BOTH the report and the manager's dispatch. The cause is the SINGLE-BRANCH REFSPEC, not shallowness, so `git fetch --unshallow` does NOT fix it. MI-123 reported it as a shallow-clone false alarm and the manager repeated that framing verbatim. It was caught only because the dispatch required REPRODUCING before fixing — the instruction did the work, not the framing. It also filed the HISTORICAL-COMMIT TRAP separately (BL-20260905-R6-GRADES-HISTORICAL-COMMITS-SO-A-TRUE-LAPSE-IS-PERMANENTLY-UNMERGEABLE), correctly keeping it apart from the wrong-parent bug it fixed — two different defects in one rule.

items.title: sunset_pass.py defaults an ABSENT leg to a measured ZERO, and that zero produced retirement candidates
items.note: Routed 2026-09-05 off MI-124's merged diagnosis (371ceaa6). ONE LINE — sunset_pass.py:288, `life = lifetime.get(name, 0 if lifetime_state == 'read' else None)` — defended by a comment that is FALSE about its own source: it claims /api/bot/performance lists every strategy with ANY closed trade, while that route's SQL carries `AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL` and therefore lists PNL-BEARING closes. A leg whose every close has pnl NULL is ABSENT, and the default reads that absence as a measured 0. Chain: pnl NULL -> absent from the capture -> 0 -> basis `never_closed_lifetime` -> verdict `retire_candidate` -> note 'has never closed a single trade in its life'. POPULATION (live capture, 2026-09-05): 52 enabled legs, 46 present, ELEVEN absent and defaulted to 0; 9 of the 10 candidates are among them; 5 of the 10 had journal closes before the packet was generated. ⚠️ THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS, IN THE MACHINERY THAT PROPOSES RETIREMENTS — and sunset_pass.py already implements the three-state discipline correctly one level up, which is what makes it a slip in one default rather than a missing concept. ⚠️ IT VINDICATES AN OPERATOR DECISION MADE WITHOUT THIS EVIDENCE: the refusal to retire on this basis, twice. Had the batch retirement been taken, five legs would have gone on a manufactured zero. SCOPED TIGHT, and the exclusions are the point: do NOT change /api/bot/performance's SQL (correct for that route; the defect is the CALLER using it as an 'ever closed' oracle), and do NOT fix the pnl-stamping defects that CAUSE the nulls (alpaca reconciler closes; trade 4350 + 7 orphaned packages on mes_trend_long_1d, which has held a position 33 days and cannot re-enter) — real, different unit, still unrouted. ⚠️ CLOSED 2026-09-05T02:58:39Z: MERGED 5eb59917. items.title: OPERATOR-APPROVED TIER-2, FORWARD-ONLY: key the local-pnl sweep window on the CLOSE, not the OPEN
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-05, asked directly as a popup and answered 'Fix the predicate, forward-only'. VERDICT approved_with_conditions. CONDITION, and it is the load-bearing half: FORWARD-ONLY. The historical back-fill of the ~20 already-silent long-held rows was OFFERED AS AN OPTION AND NOT TAKEN — it remains a SEPARATE decision with its own evidence bar, because pricing a close that happened weeks ago without an anchor is FABRICATED by this repo's own definition. A successor reading 'approved' without this condition could back-fill values nobody measured into the money DB. SCOPE: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:10533 — the scan query ends `AND datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now','-14 days')`. created_at is the OPEN; the value the sweep recovers is a property of the CLOSE. Key it on COALESCE(closed_at, created_at). EVIDENCE (MI-127, on main): population = all 5,493 journal rows fetched complete by pagination against trader sha 5eb59917; non-backtest status=closed, intent_reduce excluded, hold computable = 1,373 rows. pnl-NULL share by hold bucket <1d 22/1103 (2.0%) | 1-7d 3/196 (1.5%) | 7-14d 12/47 (25.5%) | >14d 20/22 (90.9%). And 0 OF 20 long-held rows was ever DECLARED unmeasured — they never reach the no_anchor branch (order_monitor.py:10637-10655), so they are SILENT nulls with no provenance key at all, which is precisely what src/runtime/provenance.py exists to prevent. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN ROW: this is the HEAD of the chain whose tail is sunset_pass proposing real strategies for retirement — pnl NULL -> absent from /api/bot/performance (its SQL carries AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL) -> no lifetime measurement -> retirement basis. items.title: OPERATOR-APPROVED TIER-2: refuse an empty sizing map once instead of re-emitting it (mes_trend_long_1d minted 7 packages in 49 minutes)
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-05, asked as a popup and answered 'Route it now as a Tier-2 fix'. VERDICT approved. SCOPE: the sizing/retry path — an empty sizing map must be refused ONCE with a logged cause rather than re-emitted. EVIDENCE (MI-127, on main): mes_trend_long_1d minted SEVEN order packages in 49 minutes from ONE daily signal because sizing returned an empty map; all seven were orphaned unexecuted. STATED PLAINLY SO SEVERITY IS NOT INFLATED: nothing reached a venue and no money moved. The cost is a loop with no brake and seven phantom packages per occurrence — which pollute exactly the order-package data the M7 review packets grade strategies on, so it corrupts the evidence base rather than the book. ⚠️ THE OPERATOR WAS OFFERED 'investigate WHY sizing returned empty first' AND DID NOT TAKE IT — so the approved scope is THE BRAKE, not the root cause of the empty map. If the fixing session finds the empty map is itself an account/instrument resolution failure, FILE that separately rather than widening this item. Backlog row: BL-20260905-MES-TREND-LONG-1D-RE-EMITTED-ONE-DAILY-SIGNAL-SEVEN-TIMES-IN-49-MINUTES-WHEN-SIZING-RETURNED-EMPTY. BLOCKED ON A SLOT: sessions 3 of 3. || ROUTED 2026-09-05T06:22Z. || OPERATOR TIER-2 OK ON THE DIFF, 2026-09-05, given as a popup: "Merge it". ⚠️ AND THE MANAGER WAS WRONG ABOUT THIS SESSION — recorded because the error is the useful part. It was not drifting: renaming _eligible_for_dispatch to _dispatch_exclusion_reason IS the named-cause half of the approved brake, because a bare bool made every dropped account vanish without a recoverable reason — which is precisely WHY seven identical attempts said nothing about their own cause. Judging a session from a status string rather than its diff produced a false positive. It stayed in scope, declared Tier-2 hold as a draft rather than self-landing, filed THREE rows rather than widening (including the why-was-sizing-empty question the operator declined to fund, left explicitly unanswered), keyed the brake on the SIGNAL rather than a clock so the leg still trades the next bar, shipped a positive control, and verified its four residual guard failures as environmental against unmodified origin/main rather than asserting it. || ✅ MI-129b FIXED BOTH TESTS PROPERLY, verified by the manager against the diff rather than taken from its report. NO skip/xfail/quarantine anywhere (grepped the whole tests/ diff for + lines matching skip|xfail|pytest.mark — none introduced). (1) test_arbitration_fanout_apply.py: the source-scraping assertion was REPLACED with a real BEHAVIOURAL test built on actual accounts YAML and Coordinator (+117 lines). That is the correct verdict of the two offered — the test WAS pinning something it should not have, and it now asserts the property instead of the function name. (2) test_s030_pr1_order_packages_log.py: it kept the BUG-049 contract pinned exactly and replaced the exact-literal close_reason assertion with a PROPERTY assertion — the reason must NAME the excluded account and the strategy, never a bare count and never silence. items.deliverable_1_MEASURED_2026_09_06: THE R INSTRUMENT IS NOT MERELY NOISY -- IT IS SIGN-INVERTED, and this lands before any attribution rests on it. Population: trades where status='closed' AND NOT is_backtest AND pnl IS NOT NULL, n=1451, drawn from all 5516 rows (full table, not a page), read live 2026-09-06. R-provenance via src/runtime/r_provenance.py::classify_r (imported, not re-derived): contaminated 124 (8.5%), confirmed_initial 174 (12.0%), unverified 1132 (78.0%), no_basis 21 (1.4%). 8.5% OF ROWS CARRY 98.8% OF THE R. Contaminated: sumR +4020.27, meanR +32.42. Confirmed_initial: sumR -92.16, meanR -0.53. All R-measurable: +2.84 mean. THE SIGN FLIPS -- on rows whose risk basis is CONFIRMED to be the initial risk, expectancy is -0.53R; the published +2.84R is an artifact of the other 8.5%. POSITIVE CONTROL for the discriminator: |R|>10 occurs 35 times among the 124 contaminated and ZERO times among the 174 confirmed_initial, max contaminated R +3672.3 -- total separation, so the threshold was not chosen to fit. MECHANISM, read from code not inferred: _clean_trades.r_multiple computes pnl/(|entry-stop|*|qty|*contract_value); the abs() is load-bearing, so a stop on the WRONG SIDE of entry still yields a positive risk and a finite R instead of a refusal. trades.stop_loss holds the FINAL stop and order_monitor._apply_update writes trailing amends into it, so a trade that trailed through breakeven stores a stop beyond entry, |entry-stop| collapses toward zero, and R explodes. R is defined against ENTRY-TIME risk; the column holds EXIT-TIME stop. CONSEQUENCE: every promote/demote verdict computed from expectancyR over a population containing contaminated rows is UNSAFE. This supersedes MI-30's framing (which said 17.2% store a stop on the wrong side and expectancyR reaches +206.9) with a measured sign inversion and a named mechanism. Deliverable 2 (attribution) is in progress and rests on NO R.

But a wider stop buys a DEFERRAL, not a win -- none of these trades was ever meaningfully in profit, so the loss would have been taken later and larger. WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED -- THE MARKET STOPPED TRAVELLING. Max favourable excursion as a multiple of each trade's own stop distance (MFE/D), from Bybit candles: PRIOR 08-16..08-29 n=23 median 2.11, 14/23 reached >= +1R; POST 08-30..09-06 n=13 median 0.15, max 0.95, ZERO of 13 reached +1R. The single best trade of the losing week never matched the MEDIAN trade of the winning fortnight. In the prior window 14 trades reached +1R and there were exactly 14 wins -- the metric tracks the outcome. A stop is a floor under a loss and cannot create upside, so no stop setting wins a trade that never goes into profit. And e35 made stops NARROWER, which INFLATES MFE/D; the post window is 14x lower DESPITE that upward bias. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, measured without reference to any trade (Coinbase spot 15m): per-bar volatility essentially UNCHANGED (median |15m| move 0.093 -> 0.091) while directional efficiency fell 4-6x (BTC 0.098 -> 0.023, ETH 0.093 -> 0.014, XRP 0.060 -> 0.010). The market did not get quieter, it got DIRECTIONLESS -- which is why ict_scalp_5m lost on BOTH its longs and its shorts. !! IT CORRECTS A FACT THE MANAGER GAVE THE OPERATOR AND PUT IN THE DISPATCH: 'BTC fell 81k -> 77k in the window' is FALSE. BTC opened the post window at 78234 and closed at 79864, +2.08%, high 82283 low 76219. The competing explanation is real but it is LOSS OF DIRECTIONALITY, not a decline -- and a decline would not explain a book that lost on longs and shorts alike. IS 0-FOR-13 UNUSUAL? YES, and the session corrected its own first reading to establish it: it nearly reported two prior 13-14 trade streaks as precedent, then dated them -- the 14 IS THIS EVENT and the 13 was entirely orphan_adopt reconciler artifacts. The longest genuine prior losing streak on comparable legs is 6. So the run is ~2x anything this book had done, a real outlier, just not one whose timing or composition points at e35. HONEST LIMITS, stated by the session: it CANNOT clear e35 (n=2), so OI-20260830-E35-...-NOT-YET-LIVE-VERIFIED stays open on its own terms; and it CANNOT separate regime from a silent degradation in ENTRY quality, because MFE/D is a joint function of both -- the independent regime measurement is why confidence is MODERATE rather than low, and it says plainly that anyone claiming this week was purely regime is over-claiming. THE REAL ITEM IS ict_scalp_5m, NOT e35: 6 of 13 losses, 58.6% of the money, stop distances 0.15%-0.80% on BTC -- inside the noise of a directionless tape. Lifetime on bybit_2: 37 trades, 54.1% WINS, -12.65 USD. It wins more often than it loses AND STILL LOSES MONEY, which is a payoff-geometry problem, not a hit-rate one. items.note: FILED, DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN — a guard change is scripts/ci/, a worker path, and the manager does not execute items. MEASURED TWICE ON 2026-09-08. check_manager_scope's merge_slot_claim_only admits a manager commit touching docs/claude/session-board.json only when merge_slot is the sole top-level key changed, checked against EVERY parent — so on a merge commit whose two parents differ on ANY other key, or on merge_slot itself, no resolution can satisfy it. First hit: the parents differed on `updated_at`. Second hit: #11378 landed its own merge_slot change and `git merge-tree --write-tree` returned EXIT 1 on session-board.json. ⚠️ THE INTERACTION IS THE DEFECT, NOT EITHER RULE. pr-landing R13 REQUIRES an armed branch to hold merge_slot in that file; the carve-out then makes the file unmergeable. So the one file a manager register branch MUST touch is the one it can never resolve a conflict in. Force-push is prohibited and weakening the carve-out would re-open what #11357 closed, which leaves re-laying linearly off main as the ONLY honest route — and it must be re-done every time another branch lands a merge_slot change first, which under a working merge queue is often. ⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' this with a manager-scope-exception: that is the papering-over this repo has already ruled against.

It measures 15 instances across 5 distinct days and records that FILING TAUGHT NOTHING. A fourth row would be the accumulation this repo complains about, so none was filed. || THE 16TH INSTANCE IS MINE, 2026-09-08T22:11Z: I spawned MI-205 with source_url omitted and it attached the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot — a different OWNER, outside this session's allowed scope. It reached RUNNING, cloned that repo, read its docs and pushed a board START there before I interrupted it at 22:17Z and re-dispatched as MI-205b with the source pinned. || WHAT IS NEW AND IS WHY THIS ITEM EXISTS: I spawned THROUGH session_registry.py, and register + confirm BOTH SUCCEEDED. The registry records that a spawn happened and cannot see which repo the child was handed, so A REGISTERED SPAWN IS NOT A CORRECTLY-TARGETED ONE. The registry is also the one mechanism a manager reliably runs at spawn time and the one thing in this class the REPO ACTUALLY OWNS — CLAUDE.md states plainly that nothing here is on create_session's call path, so 'wrap create_session' (the third row's own clause 1) is not buildable from inside this repository. Refusing to register without an explicit --source-url, and printing it into the spawn prompt the registry already emits, is the strongest prevention the repo can actually implement. || ⚠️ THE TRAP IS IN THE TOOL'S OWN WORDING and should be quoted in whatever is built: create_session says it 'inherits the calling session's environment' when environment_id is omitted. An ENVIRONMENT IS NOT A SET OF SOURCES. Verified both directions this session: my own get_session carries the three benbaichmankass/* repos, while MI-205 — spawned from it, same environment — carried the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot. || ⚠️ THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT, NOT SAFE. The third row draws the distinction and it held here: a no-repo spawn fails safe (nothing to compute), a WRONG-repo spawn runs and produces confident, quotable output from the wrong codebase — MI-188 reported a trading number from the historical the-lizardking tree. MI-205's own task_summary read 'repo cloned, docs read, board START pushed' and looked entirely healthy. || DETECTION HALF, already available and cheap: get_session with NO argument returns the caller's own session_context.sources in one call — no git, no commit, no push. That row is about the CADENCE (an Actions cron measured firing 5x/day against 24 declared) and its fix is #10858, Tier-2, held on an operator OK. items.title: The strategy-review packet grades edge off live in-window n, which the binding promotion-evidence rule forbids
items.note: OPERATOR-DIRECTED 2026-09-09. ⚠️ THIS NOTE WAS REWRITTEN THE SAME DAY BECAUSE ITS FIRST VERSION WAS THE WRONG SHAPE. It read "DO NOT RE-ASK THE WINDOW/FLOOR QUESTION IN ANY FORM", and the operator rejected that framing outright: "you keep adding guards in the shape of forbidding questions from being asked - this is incorrect. the problem isn't the question, it's the underlying misunderstanding of infra and processes, and not asking questions isn't what fixes that - it just makes it more likely that you will f****** again in the future because you're not asking the right question... it's that you don't understand how the system works. that's what we need to fix here, not the question". THE PROHIBITION IS RETRACTED. Ask whatever you need to, window and floor included. Banning a question suppresses the symptom and leaves the misunderstanding intact, so the next session fails in a NEW way instead of asking a better question. THE THING TO CARRY IS THE MODEL, NOT A RULE: (1) EDGE is established OFFLINE — this repo has extensive backtesting infrastructure built for exactly that (purged walk-forward CV, replay_pregate_fleet, the point-in-time backfills), and that is where 'does this strategy work' is answered. (2) LIVE data establishes MECHANICS ONLY — that executions match the simulator — which canon says needs 1-2 executed trades, not calendar time. (3) SLOW LIVE ACCRUAL IS A FEATURE OF THE SYSTEM, NOT A BARRIER TO OVERCOME: a leg closing ~1.2 trades a week is not a problem to engineer around, and `none_gradeable` on a live window is not a defect. (4) Fewer legs does NOT raise trades-per-leg, and on paper accounts every leg runs regardless — the manager recommended that lever and the operator rejected it. WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY IS: the review/validation layer is built on a LIVE-ACCRUAL model of evidence while the system's real evidence engine is the BACKTEST infrastructure. MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION is a symptom of that mismatch, not the defect. The operator's own framing: "our overall operation is clearly not built to suit the system's structure." THE RULE THIS CONTRADICTS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS BINDING: docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Promotion evidence — offline edge, live mechanics' (2026-07-26), scope explicitly STRATEGY legs, clause 3 'No gate may require calendar-time accrual to prove edge', and it already names this as 'the recurring drift this rule kills'. THE GUARD HALF MUST ENFORCE THE RULE, NOT A PHRASE: a gate producing a STRATEGY verdict must source its edge from offline evidence. A guard that greps for forbidden words is the same wrong shape one level down. Keep the positive control — a guard silent because it scans nothing is indistinguishable from one silent because all is well. Tier-3 where it changes what a KILL/DEMOTE rests on: propose, do not enact. Retiring a strategy leg is Tier-3 and is not the answer here. Manager does not take this — it is ROUTED to session_01MrTjuoRpBb7spyQLydXmmT, which has been sent this correction directly.

items.title: Prop status-request pings on wall-clock age alone, so it asks about an account nothing has touched
items.note:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-09, verbatim: "This ping in the prop channel is unessacry, the account snapshot is updated when a trade closes, if there are no prop trades than the account state didn't change." The ping quoted was breakout_1, no open positions, snapshot 228h (9.5d) old. ⚠️ DO NOT SIMPLY REVERT TO THE PRE-2026-08-14 BEHAVIOUR — THAT IS A TIER-2 OPERATOR-APPROVED DECISION AND IT WAS MADE FOR A STATED REASON. src/prop/prop_status_request.py used to bail on `if not positions: return []`; it was changed BECAUSE the static DD floor (breakout.yaml drawdown_type: static, $4,700 on $5,000) is an ACCOUNT-level line that binds while FLAT, and flat is exactly when the next ticket gets sized against a cushion nobody has measured. Re-adding the flat bail re-opens that hole. The operator is not asking for that; they are saying the TRIGGER is wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: the trigger is WALL-CLOCK AGE of the last snapshot and nothing else, so a genuinely quiet account is indistinguishable from one that moved and was never reported. The operator's refinement — key on whether anything has HAPPENED since the last snapshot — preserves the 08-14 purpose while removing the noise, provided the ask still fires (a) on any fill since the last snapshot and (b) before a new ticket is sized. ⚠️ VERIFY THE PREMISE BEFORE BUILDING ON IT — DO NOT INHERIT IT. "The snapshot is updated when a trade closes" is a claim, not an established fact: the snapshot lands only when the OPERATOR reports numbers back. A close produces a FILL report; telegram_report_handler.account_status_nudge only APPENDS a balance nudge to the fill ack, and a screenshot may or may not yield an account_status alongside the fill. So a close PROMPTS a snapshot and does not guarantee one. Measure it: over the 228h window, count prop_fills rows against prop_account_status rows for breakout_1 and report BOTH numbers. If fills happened and no snapshot followed, the operator's premise is false in the dangerous direction and the ping was doing its job — say so plainly. ⚠️ AND NOTE FOUR CONSUMERS SHARE THIS THRESHOLD, so changing PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS is NOT a local edit: the ask, the folded balance nudge, prop_balance.max_age_hours() (the SIZING freshness gate) and the status_freshness verdict on /api/bot/prop/status. One definition of "too old to trust" is deliberate — sizing must never run off a balance the safety panel has written off. Change the TRIGGER, not the threshold. Tier-2 (src/ + prop bridge). Manager does not take this — ROUTE IT.  ⚠️ OPERATOR APPROVED 2026-09-09T10:44Z VIA POPUP — "Approve — ship it". #11530 is cleared to land. THE APPROVAL RESTS ON ONE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM, and the operator was shown it and offered the chance to reject it: prop_reconcile.reconstruct_equity is ASYMMETRIC by design — an unplaceable LOSS is always applied, an unplaceable GAIN is withheld — so a REPORTED fill can only ever make the cushion CONSERVATIVE, never optimistic. They were also offered "I disagree with the asymmetry claim — don't land it" and "Approve, but keep asking while flat" and chose neither. If that claim is ever falsified, this approval falls with it. SCOPE: #11530 only — the prop status-request TRIGGER in src/prop/. NOT a licence to raise PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS (four consumers share it, including the SIZING gate) and NOT a licence to restore the pre-2026-08-14 flat bail. ⚠️ THE LANE MEASURED THE OPERATOR'S PREMISE AND IT IS HALF FALSE — record this, because a later session will otherwise re-derive the wrong half: read 2026-09-09T09:54Z, breakout_1's newest prop_account_status is id 19 at 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z and its newest prop_fills row is id 41 at 2026-08-30T19:39:00Z, so THE LAST CLOSE IS 5.5 MINUTES NEWER THAN THE SNAPSHOT IT SUPPOSEDLY PRODUCED. A close PROMPTS a snapshot and never guarantees one. The operator's CONCLUSION held anyway for a stronger reason — 0 fills, 0 open positions and 0 unacted tickets in the 230h since, against a positive control of 41 fills lifetime (oldest 2026-06-22), so the zero is real and not a broken probe.

=== OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED 2026-09-09 (asked in-conversation, answered in-conversation; this is the operator-feedback-becomes-canon duty, which has NO CI check behind it) ===
(1) 15:52Z — MERGE #11560 APPROVED, Tier-2. The read-only Bybit closed-PnL diag route (account_bybit_raw_closed_pnl + /api/diag/bybit_raw_closed_pnl). Routed to the MI-221 lane as a one-line fix. Its three-state design GRADED that could_not_look rather than reporting an empty result, so nobody built a conclusion on a call that never ran.
(2) 15:58Z — MERGE #11546 APPROVED, Tier-2, AND THE ALERT FLOOR STAYS AT THE GLOBAL 5. Asked as two separate questions. items.title: Replace the model-promotion calendar gates with a COUNT OF OBSERVATIONS that the mechanics worked (operator-directed 2026-09-09)
items.operator_verbatim: "None of these are correct. It's not a matter of time. There should be no trade [floor] because again, that's not what we're looking for. What we're looking for is mechanics which means we need to decide if it should be one trade or three trades or five trades. But it's the number of observations that we see the system working correctly, not a specific amount of time that needs to be verified."
items.note: MI-218 (#11538, merged 13:22Z) found S2: ml/promotion/gates.py default GateThresholds requires BOTH require_shadow_soak=True @ 7d AND min_trades=200 LIVE. THE MANAGER PROPOSED KEEPING THE SOAK AND DROPPING ONLY THE TRADE FLOOR, AND THE OPERATOR REJECTED THAT: the soak is ALSO time-denominated, so it is wrong on the same axis. NEITHER a duration NOR a trade count is the right unit. The unit is THE NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS THAT THE MECHANICS WORKED CORRECTLY -- for a model head, that the head scores in live the way it scored in training (live/train parity). TWO PIECES OF WORK, and the second is not a licence to wait for the first: (1) redesign the gate to count parity observations rather than elapsed days or executed trades; (2) ESTABLISH N from evidence that already exists -- the shadow-prediction / live-parity record is already written per head (gate packets cite figures like live_parity 50/0), so how many observations are needed to detect a mechanics failure is MEASURABLE OFFLINE TODAY and must not become another accrual wait. N is expected to be small (the operator named 1, 3 or 5 as the shape of the answer). Canon's claim that this is 'mechanically guarded' is true only of the regime-classifier profile; the default profile every non-regime head uses is unguarded -- fix the guard's reach in the same change. The GATE CHANGE itself is Tier-3 (promotion path) and is operator-gated; establishing N is Tier-1 measurement.

items.title: The manager checklist has no schema — two competing status fields that disagree, 152 field names, 95 used once
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-10, verbatim: "The fact that it's not organized is also a workflow issue that needs to be resolved (as part of the workflow implementation lane)." Raised after asking for the whole checklist as a detailed table and receiving a summary instead — the summary happened BECAUSE the file cannot be tabulated: there is no column set to tabulate on. MEASURED 2026-09-10 over all 242 items at docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json (population = every element of items[]): 152 DISTINCT FIELD NAMES; 95 of them appear EXACTLY ONCE and 111 appear three times or fewer. Only `id` (242) is universal; `owner` 240, `title` 238, `note` 220. The one-off names are prose smuggled into keys — e.g. `⚠️_platform_state_20260909T042657Z`, `what_actually_prevents_it`, `the_honest_residual`, `⚠️_I_MARKED_THIS_OWNED_BEFORE_IT_WAS`. !! THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING IS NOT THE COUNT, IT IS A COLLAPSED STATUS. There are TWO competing status fields: `state` (177 rows) and `status` (83 rows). Every row has at least one, so nothing is stateless — an earlier reading of this as '65 items carry no state' was WRONG and must not be re-quoted, because it points at the wrong fix (backfilling a field rather than collapsing two). 18 rows carry BOTH, and 13 of those 18 DISAGREE. The disagreements are in the dangerous direction: MI-136 / MI-138 / MI-139 / MI-143 each read `state: in_flight` while `status: done`, and MI-144 / MI-145 read `state: queued` while `status: done`. A reader (human or script) that picks one field gets a different answer about what is running than one that picks the other. !! THIS IS NOT COSMETIC AND IT HAS ALREADY COST SOMETHING: this session found SIX rows sitting `in_flight` whose sessions were DEAD or ARCHIVED (MI-136 archived 2026-09-06, read `in_flight` for four days), and the two-field split is a sufficient explanation for at least four of them. `check_manager_scope.py` R6 and `session-registry-guard` both read `items[].state`/`owner`, so a row that records its truth in `status` is INVISIBLE to the guards that exist to catch a lost sub-session. !! AND THE VOCABULARIES ARE NOT THE SAME SET: `status` carries values `state` never uses — `superseded` (5), `operator_approved` (2), `filed_not_taken` (2), `unassigned` (2), `filed`, `failed`, and one literal `duplicate_of_MI-180`. So this is not a rename; some of those are real distinctions that a collapse must preserve or deliberately drop, and `duplicate_of_MI-180` is a POINTER wearing a status field's clothes.
items.what_this_item_is_not: NOT a request to prune the checklist, and NOT a rendering problem for a reader to work around. A session that 'fixes' this by writing a nicer renderer has not touched the defect — the file is the state of record a COLD manager reads, and the renderer is downstream of it. !! AND IT IS NOT A LICENCE TO DELETE THE ONE-OFF FIELDS WHOLESALE: several carry real evidence (`what_actually_prevents_it`, `the_honest_residual`) that exists nowhere else, so they must be moved into a declared field, not dropped. Deleting knowledge to satisfy a schema is the exact failure the OPEN-ITEMS cap produced on 2026-08-26.
items.resolution_criteria: THREE PARTS, and they are different facts — say WHICH you did. (1) A DECLARED SCHEMA exists for items[] — a required core (id, title, owner, ONE status field, lane, tier, added, updated) with a CLOSED status vocabulary that accounts for every value currently in BOTH `state` and `status`, including the ones only `status` has; free prose goes in a declared free-text field, never in a new key. (2) The 242 existing rows are MIGRATED onto it with the 13 known disagreements RESOLVED INDIVIDUALLY against the session registry and the PR record — never by a rule like 'status wins', which would mark four dead lanes done without anyone looking. (3) A CI guard refuses a row carrying an undeclared key or a status outside the vocabulary, so the drift cannot re-accumulate silently — a one-time cleanup with no guard is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for on MI-15 twice. !! A GREEN GUARD ON A MIGRATED FILE CLEARS (3) AND NOT (2): the guard proves the shape, not that anyone established which of `in_flight` and `done` was true for MI-136.

items.title: Build the live Workflow page: the manager checklist with collapsible rows + the decisions waiting on the operator
items.note: OPERATOR-DIRECTED 2026-09-10, and the directive has FOUR parts, all load-bearing: (a) the full-detail checklist rendering becomes a PAGE ON THE UI; (b) every time the operator asks for a status update, THE PAGE is updated too, so the detail lives there instead of being pulled into chat each time; (c) COLLAPSIBLE ROWS -- the operator wants to see every item at a glance and expand only the ones they care about, not read every field always; (d) the page ALSO lists the OPEN DECISIONS WAITING ON THE OPERATOR. Operator's own framing: "that will be the live workflow page that all the manager sessions are supposed to use so that we can stay organized about how we're working, and I can track the progress of the sessions as you're going", and it must be "the same as the document in the repo that you're working on so that we know that we're working in an organized fashion." !! DO NOT BUILD THIS FROM SCRATCH -- MOST OF IT EXISTS AND WAS MEASURED BEFORE FILING. src/runtime/manager_status.py ALREADY reads the checklist (CHECKLIST_RELPATH) and already owns the grading the readout needs: grade_owner(), build_sections(), build_status(), StatusReadout, Omission. It is what serves the Telegram /status command. And src/web/api/routers/work.py ALREADY serves GET /api/bot/work, /api/bot/work/object/{id} and -- this is part (d) in full -- GET /api/bot/work/decisions, the decision inbox, complete with a write gate reading. So the DECISIONS HALF NEEDS NO NEW BOT ROUTE AT ALL. Building either from scratch would be RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED.
items.the_three_halves: (1) BOT ROUTE -- add a read route (GET /api/bot/work/checklist) to the EXISTING work router that serves docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json THROUGH manager_status's existing grading, rather than re-deriving it. (2) SPA PAGE -- a Workflow page in benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard under webapp/, collapsed by default: one summary line per item (status pill, id, title, owner, lane, tier) expanding to every remaining field. A section above it for the open decisions off /api/bot/work/decisions. Follow that repo's own CLAUDE.md -- the Svelte SPA is the ONLY live consumer since 2026-09-01, it calls the API browser-direct from GitHub Pages through Caddy, so CORS IS LOAD-BEARING and a new route needs the origin to keep working. (3) THE DUTY BECOMES CANON -- the operator said every manager session is supposed to USE this page. Name it in CLAUDE.md's manager-duty bullet (the status-update contract is already checklist -> recently done -> next; this adds: and the page is pushed before you answer) and in the role packs that check_role_pack_operating_layer.py keeps pointed at the operating layer. NOTE this half touches CLAUDE.md canon OUTSIDE the generated SESSION-BRIEF block and role packs, which are WORKER paths for manager-scope-guard -- which is exactly why this whole item is routed to a session and cannot be done by a manager.
items.the_one_owner_rule_that_decides_the_desi: !! THE SPA MUST NOT MERGE `state` AND `status` ITSELF. MI-237 measured two competing status fields on this same file -- `state` (177 rows) and `status` (83), 18 rows carrying both and 13 of those DISAGREEING. A renderer that picks one, or merges them in TypeScript, becomes a SECOND definition of an item's status, free to drift from the one check_manager_scope.py R6 and session-registry-guard read -- the exact class this repo has a guard family for. The merge belongs in ONE place on the BOT side (manager_status, which already owns grading), and MI-237's schema work then makes that merge a no-op rather than requiring a second edit. So MI-237 is NOT a blocker on this item and no blocked_on edge is written for it -- an invented edge is read by the constraint computation as a real blocker and a false blocker is worse than a missing one. The two are ORDER-INDEPENDENT if and only if the merge has one owner.
items.the_freshness_constraint_state_it_rather: The operator's ask (b) -- "every time I ask for a status update, the status is updated on that page" -- is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION and only under one condition, which must be stated to them rather than quietly assumed. The route reads the repo working tree ON THE LIVE VM, which ict-git-sync pulls roughly every 5 minutes. So the page is exactly as fresh as the last PUSH of MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, plus up to ~5 minutes. There is no separate 'update the page' step to forget -- which is the point, and is strictly better than a second artifact a manager must remember to regenerate. What it means in practice: A MANAGER MUST PUSH THE CHECKLIST BEFORE ANSWERING A STATUS REQUEST, not after. That is already the standing duty (the checklist lives in the repo precisely so it survives its holder's death); this makes it observable, because a stale page is now visible to the operator instead of only to a guard. !! AND THE PAGE MUST SHOW ITS OWN AS-OF STAMP -- the file's git commit time and the sync state -- so a page serving a checklist from three hours ago cannot read identically to a live one. A frozen board reading byte-identically to a live one is the exact failure the coordination board hit on 2026-09-07.
items.resolution_criteria: FOUR PARTS, and they are different facts -- say WHICH you did. (1) The route serves the checklist and is OBSERVED returning it from the live API, not from a local run. (2) The SPA page RENDERS on the deployed GitHub Pages site with rows collapsed by default and expanding to full detail, and the decisions section shows the real inbox -- observed in a browser, which a session cannot do alone, so this half needs the operator to confirm they can see it. (3) The page carries an as-of stamp that distinguishes fresh from stale. (4) The duty is written into CLAUDE.md and the role packs. !! A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NONE OF THESE: a harness cannot render a page or reach the live API. !! MERGING CLEARS NOTHING -- a merge is not a deploy, and for the SPA half a deploy is not a render; the same distinction that keeps WO-20260901-PHASE-B's edge open. !! AND THE PAGE EXISTING IS NOT THE PAGE BEING USED: the operator's stated purpose is that manager sessions work from it, so the item is not done until a status update has actually been given against it.
items.why_it_is_tier_1: A read-only GET route on the existing work router, a new SPA page, and canon prose. It touches no order path, no strategy config, no risk cap, and adds no write surface -- the decision inbox's write route already exists and is token-gated and fail-closed; this item does not widen it.
items.blocked_on_basis: ASSESSED — nothing blocks it. The two things it plausibly depends on were checked and neither is a blocker: the decision-inbox route already exists (so part (d) has no dependency), and MI-237's schema work is order-independent PROVIDED the state/status merge has a single bot-side owner, which this item's design requires anyway.
items.source: operator (conversational), 2026-09-10
items.operator_clarification_20260910T0800Z: VERBATIM, and it changes the SCOPE of this item rather than merely emphasising it: "just to be clear the organized workflow isn't a backstop - it's the way we need to work in general, and part of that is making the work page on the UI clear so that I can keep track of the work sessions without needing to ask for ad hoc updates all the time." !! TWO CONSEQUENCES, AND THE FIRST IS A REAL GAP IN WHAT WAS FILED. (1) THE PAGE NEEDS A THIRD PANEL: LIVE WORK SESSIONS. As originally filed this item covered the CHECKLIST and the DECISION inbox only. The operator's stated purpose is tracking the work SESSIONS, and that is a different source: docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json (the sub-session registry). The panel must show, per live lane: which item it owns, its session id, its state, WHEN IT WAS LAST OBSERVED, and what it is blocked on. Without that the operator still has to ask, which is the exact cost this item exists to remove. (2) IT IS NOT A STOPGAP FOR A MISSING PAGE. The page reflects the discipline; it does not create it. So the CLAUDE.md/role-pack half (half 3) is not optional polish — working from the page IS the workflow, and the page is only as good as the registers behind it.
items.the_sessions_panel_and_the_trap_it_must_: ⚠️ `state` IN SESSIONS.json DECAYS AND NOTHING DECAYS IT. Measured 2026-09-10T07:47Z: MI-232 and LANE4-RECOVERY both read `working` on main while both were IDLE and COMPLETED — false BY TIME PASSING, not by anyone being wrong when they wrote it. 17 rows were false the same way on 2026-09-08, one of them 42 minutes after it was written. So a panel that renders `state` verbatim will confidently show dead lanes as running, which is WORSE than no panel: the operator would stop asking precisely because it looks live. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT TO GUESS. Render the row's own `updated_at` BESIDE its state and make staleness visible — a `working` row last observed 90 minutes ago is not the same fact as one observed 2 minutes ago, and the page must not collapse them. MI-236 already carries the underlying defect (nothing decays a stale in_flight row); this panel must not silently depend on that being fixed first, and must not paper over it either. ⚠️ AND THE PAGE CANNOT READ list_sessions: that is an mcp__* tool no route holds, so the live session state is only ever as good as the last MANAGER OBSERVATION written into the registry. Say so on the page rather than implying a live feed.

Bot half #11651 -> 4875f407a (09:27:59Z), DEPLOYED and READ OFF THE LIVE HOST: GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/work/checklist -> 200 at 09:29:42Z, 253 items, byBasis state_only 172 / status_only 64 / agree 5 / DISAGREE 12 summing to 253, freshness warnings []. items.title: A monitoring workflow: follow monitored items cleanly instead of adjudicating loud rows one at a time
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-10, verbatim, IN PLACE OF ANSWERING a decision request: "We should have a workflow for monitoring that allows us to follow mo itores items in a clean wya that doesn't generate noise, if we don't then we need to understand how that fits into the workflow lane. The problem here is not correctly framed for a structurally sound workflow." !! THE OPERATOR REJECTED THE UNIT OF DECISION, NOT THE PARTICULAR ROW. They were asked whether ONE loud OPEN-ITEMS row should be removed given a deviation from its written clause (1). Answering that question either way would have reproduced per-row adjudication, which is the thing that does not scale: OPEN-ITEMS.json carries 26 monitoring items DUE in the CLAUDE.md session brief today, each with a multi-paragraph clears_when, and every one of them is a candidate for exactly this argument. !! THE MEASURED SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM, so the lane does not start from prose: the brief's monitoring block is the single largest thing a session reads before acting, several rows have carried `verified_at: never` since they were opened (the closed-flat invariant and the rollback registry both do today), and the register has NO CAP by deliberate operator decision (2026-08-26: check_open_items.py sets MAX_ITEMS = None, because "we don't want to cap the number of bugs we can track, we want to ensure that they are actually being tracked, fixed, and learned from"). So the answer is NOT to prune and is NOT to cap — both were already tried and the cap was reversed as a bandaid that "bounded the LIST rather than making anything get read or fixed". The answer is a way to FOLLOW them.
items.what_this_is_not: NOT a licence to delete monitoring rows, shorten clears_when, or reintroduce a cap — all three are the failure the operator already ruled out. NOT a renderer: MI-238's page will DISPLAY monitored items, and displaying them is not following them. And NOT a per-row triage pass: doing 26 adjudications by hand is the very thing being rejected, one order of magnitude larger.
items.the_question_to_answer_first: What makes a monitored item NOISE rather than signal? Candidate distinctions worth measuring before designing anything: an item whose clears_when nobody can act on today vs one that is genuinely due; one waiting on an OBSERVATION nobody has scheduled vs one waiting on a decision; one whose cadence has elapsed vs one re-affirmed. `verified_at: never` with no owner and no scheduled observer is a different state from `verified_at: <recent>` and the brief renders them alike. Establish the population first — how many of the 26 are in each state — rather than designing against an assumed shape.
items.resolution_criteria: A workflow EXISTS and has been USED, and those are different facts — say which. (1) A stated policy for what a monitored item owes and who owes it, covering the case the loud-row request exposed: an item whose written clause was deviated from by work that nonetheless delivered the capability. (2) It is MECHANISED, not a reminder — this repo has paid twice for restating a rule as prose (MI-15) — so something refuses or surfaces rather than relying on a session choosing to look. (3) A session is OBSERVED following it and the brief's monitoring block is measurably smaller or better targeted afterwards, with the before/after counts stated. !! A GREEN GUARD CLEARS (2) AND NOT (3): a pointer existing is a deploy, not a reading. !! AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the current handling is acceptable, this does NOT clear — it CHANGES, and must be recorded as that decision with the consequence stated.

items.title: Sweep the 623 dormant work objects — close or queue each, and add a lifecycle value for work that is genuinely waiting on a soak or observation
items.note: OPERATOR-DIRECTED 2026-09-10, from READING THE LIVE SPA WORK PAGE — not from a report. Their words: "there are over 600 dormant work items - we need a specific session in the ops lane (when opens ups) to work through the list and update it - these things either need to closed or qued (for future sessions, it just doesn't make sense that our workflow has this many dormant items) - if some of them are stuck on soaks/observations, then we need a status the describes that". MEASURED BY THE OPERATOR OFF THE DEPLOYED PAGE: 708 work objects — 6 in flight, 18 ready, 24 waiting, **623 dormant**, 37 done, 0 accepted. 2 intents, 0 steps. !! THE SECOND HALF IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED FOR THE FIRST. `dormant` is doing the work of at least three different facts: (a) genuinely parked, nobody intends to start it; (b) QUEUED for a future session; and (c) ACCRUING — a soak is running, an observation is pending, and the work is progressing without a session attached. Calling (c) dormant is a COLLAPSED STATE in precisely the sense this repo already has a guard family for: it makes "nothing is happening" and "something is happening that nobody is watching" render identically, which is the worse direction. !! CONTEXT THAT BOUNDS THE SWEEP: ~572 of these migrated in bulk in Phase C on 2026-09-01, and the CLAUDE.md brief already states they are "carried, not started, and NOT queued". So the 623 is not 623 forgotten decisions — it is mostly one migration that was never triaged. That makes the sweep tractable and it also means a per-row essay is the wrong instrument.
items.what_this_is_not: NOT a licence to bulk-close. The store's own README records a bulk pass on 2026-09-01 doing real harm, and CLAUDE.md states in terms that an invented blocked_on edge is read by the constraint computation as a real blocker and that a FALSE blocker is worse than a missing one. The same applies to a false `done`. NOT a licence to bulk-QUEUE either: moving 623 rows to `ready` would make the ready list unreadable and would assert an intent nobody formed. AND NOT a renderer change: MI-238 makes this list visible; visibility is not triage.
items.how_to_do_it_without_repeating_the_bulk-: Sweep by COHORT, not row by row, and state the cohort rule before applying it. The 572 Phase-C migrants share a provenance and can be graded as a group against a stated test; the ~50 that are NOT migrants deserve individual reads. For every cohort decision, record WHAT THE RULE WAS and how many rows it moved, so a later session can audit the sweep rather than inheriting an unexplained state change. Any row you cannot grade stays where it is — `we did not look` is a legitimate outcome and must not be laundered into `closed`.
items.the_new_lifecycle_value: Propose it, do not just add it. `lifecycle` is currently the six-value vocabulary dormant/ready/in_flight/waiting/done/accepted, and CLAUDE.md says it is NEVER collapsed — so widening it is a schema change that touches scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py, check_wip_ceiling.py, the work router and the SPA. ⚠️ CHECK `waiting` FIRST: 24 rows already use it, and if it already means "waiting on an external event" then the answer may be to RE-POINT rows at it rather than invent a seventh value. Establish what `waiting` means today from its actual rows before proposing anything. If a new value IS warranted, it must be distinguishable in the constraint computation — a soak-bound row is NOT blocked on a person and must not be counted as if it were.
items.resolution_criteria: THREE PARTS, different facts — say which. (1) Every one of the 623 has been graded into closed / queued / accruing / explicitly-still-dormant, with the COHORT RULES recorded and the counts per rule stated. (2) Work genuinely waiting on a soak or observation carries a status that SAYS SO, either an existing value re-pointed or a new one, and the constraint computation treats it as not-blocked-on-a-person. (3) The dormant count on the SPA Work page is materially lower AND the operator can tell from the page which of the remainder are parked versus accruing. !! A LOWER NUMBER ALONE CLEARS NOTHING — it is trivially achievable by closing rows nobody read, which is the harm. Report the counts per rule, not the delta.
items.blocked_on_basis: ASSESSED — nothing blocks the sweep itself. It is deliberately NOT blocked on MI-238: the page makes the list visible and visibility is not triage.
items.source: operator (conversational), 2026-09-10, reading the deployed SPA Work page

items.title: Restore the three-lane model — ops / engineering / research, each with a ROLE, not three fungible slots
items.note: OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-09-10, and it is a correction of THE MANAGER'S MODEL, not a new feature. Their words: "we built out a good work plan for how we were gonna work in organized fashions that we could have multiple lanes running and have the manager session everything, and then we pause that in the middle, and we didn't execute on it properly. And now we're paying the price for that... there's supposed to be three lanes, ops, engineering, and research". !! WHAT THE MANAGER HAD WRONG: it treated the cap of 3 as THREE FUNGIBLE SLOTS and filled them by priority order, so which KIND of work was running at any moment was an accident. The model is THREE NAMED LANES WITH ROLES, and a slot is not interchangeable with another lane's slot. THE THREE ROLES, as the operator states them: (1) ENGINEERING — DEDICATED TO IMPLEMENTING THE WORK PLAN. Their words: "everything that we're discussing here about the UI and the... all the manager... manager bugs, that's what that lane is for for fixing that so that we can keep going and not keep on getting stuck on the same problems over and over again." So MI-235/236/237/238/239/242/243 are not competing miscellany — they ARE the engineering lane's queue. (2) OPS — the system review, the audit, trade grading, monitoring what is soaking. AND, PRIORITISED ABOVE its own backlog: "that lane should be prioritized for unsticking things that are stuck. Right? That's what it's there for... we can pause other work going on there. That's, like, backlog work, if we need to unstick things also." **Ops backlog work is PAUSABLE to unstick.** That is a standing priority rule, not a judgement call per incident. (3) RESEARCH — the trading/strategy work (roster proposals, backtests, ML). !! THIS SESSION IS THE EVIDENCE FOR WHY IT MATTERS, which is the operator's actual point: today three lanes sat blocked on manager actions whose blockers had ALREADY cleared (MI-140 ~63h, MI-139 3.5 days, MI-222 13h), two registry rows read `working` while dead, MI-201 sat unrouted for two days while being the answer to a question the operator then had to ask, and an operator-answered audit decision was dropped entirely (see MI-245). Every one of those is a thing an ops lane prioritised for unsticking would have caught. The manager did not have such a lane because it was not running the model.
items.what_this_is_not: NOT a request to raise the cap — the operator explicitly noted "we also seem to be having a hard time correctly managing 3 lanes as it is", and the manager recommended against more lanes on measured grounds. This is about giving the THREE their roles, not adding a fourth. NOT a re-design either: the operator says the work plan already EXISTS and was paused mid-execution. FIND IT AND READ IT before proposing anything — docs/design/operating-model-DESIGN.md and its three siblings, plus the build plan's phase order. Re-deriving a model that is already written down is the built-a-mechanism-that-already-existed class.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The three lanes and their ROLES are written into CLAUDE.md's manager-duty section and the role packs, including the standing rule that OPS BACKLOG IS PAUSABLE TO UNSTICK. ⚠️ That half is a WORKER path for manager-scope-guard, which is why this is routed to a session and cannot be done by a manager. (2) Every checklist row carries a `lane` of ops/engineering/research — which is MI-237's schema migration, so do it THERE rather than as a second pass. (3) A manager is OBSERVED spawning by lane role rather than by priority order, and says which lane each spawn fills. !! A GREEN GUARD CLEARS (1) AND NOT (3): prose existing is a deploy, not a reading — the same distinction that keeps OI-20260902-ROLE-PACKS-NOW-REACH-THE-OPERATING-LAYER open.
items.blocked_on_basis: ASSESSED — the design documents already exist; nothing blocks reading them and writing the roles into canon.

items.title: REAL ROUTING DEFECT, operator-answered and unrouted: the unlisted-strategy arbitration fallback WINS instead of losing
items.note: FOUND 2026-09-10 while answering the operator's question "I still haven't heard back [on the audit]". THE AUDIT DID DELIVER: MI-225's /full-system-audit landed 2026-09-09 as 566c0ff4c (#11571) — 68 findings, 19 backlog rows, SIX operator decisions, at docs/audits/full-system-audit-2026-09-09.md. FIVE of the six were answered AND routed, becoming MI-227 / MI-228 / MI-229 / MI-230 / MI-231, all of which have merged code. !! THE SIXTH WAS ANSWERED AND DROPPED. WO-20260909-DECISION-UNKNOWN-STRATEGY-PRIORITY-IS-INVERTED's TITLE reads 'operator answered: fix the constant AND map the five legs' — but its decision_request carries `chosen: None` and `answered_at: None`, it appears on NO checklist row, and it has NO owner. The answer was recorded in PROSE, in a title, where no register and no guard reads it. It has sat `ready` since 2026-09-09. THE FINDING ITSELF IS LIVE AND IS TIER-3 ROUTING: `_UNKNOWN_STRATEGY_PRIORITY = 10` is DOCUMENTED as 'deliberately below the in-scope strategies', and 45 of 50 mapped legs now sit BELOW 10 — so an UNLISTED strategy WINS arbitration instead of losing it, which is the inversion of the documented intent. FIVE declared-live legs are absent from the map, with LIVE SLV CONTENTION ON THREE ACCOUNTS. !! DO NOT RE-ASK THE OPERATOR FOR THE DECISION — it is given ('fix the constant AND map the five legs'). What is owed is TYPING it into the object and doing the work. ⚠️ AND VERIFY THE ANSWER AGAINST THE ORIGINAL WORDING BEFORE ACTING: a verdict surviving only in a title is exactly the 'a row recording a verdict without its condition is WORSE than a missing row' hazard CLAUDE.md names for OPEN-PRS. Read the audit section and the object history; if the conditions cannot be recovered, ask for the CONDITIONS, not for the decision.
items.why_this_is_the_ops_lane: It is a STUCK THING — operator-answered, unrouted, live. Under the operator's 2026-09-10 direction the ops lane is prioritised for unsticking, above its own backlog. This is the first test of that rule.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The answer is TYPED into the object (`chosen` + `answered_at` + scope/condition) so a register reads it rather than a title. (2) The constant is fixed and the five unmapped legs are mapped — Tier-3, so propose the exact diff and land it by the normal Tier-3 route, not self-landing. (3) OBSERVED on the fleet: an arbitration tick where an unlisted strategy LOSES to a mapped one, read off the live audit surface. !! A GREEN TEST CLEARS (3) NOT AT ALL — a harness cannot reach an arbitration contest. !! AND THE SLV CONTENTION MUST BE RE-READ LIVE before proposing: it was measured 2026-09-09.

items.title: THE THIRD DROP CLASS: a row filed and never routed has no age, no owner and no alarm — filing is not routing
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-10, stating the manager's core mandate: "your job as a manager session or part of it at least is to ensure that things don't get dropped in the middle and that we actually finish things and execute them. And if not, then things are documented correctly so we know where to pick them up in a new session and things don't just fall between the cracks. That's the main thing that you need to be focused on... the main impetus for moving to a new system with the manager session was to prevent these kinds of things from happening." !! THIS IS THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY AND THE ONLY ONE NOT YET FILED. MI-235 covers a session BLOCKED on a manager action never being told when it clears. MI-236 covers an `in_flight` row going stale because nothing decays it. NEITHER covers a row that was FILED, correctly, with a real owner-shaped gap — and then simply never routed to anyone. Such a row sits at `ready` / `owner: unassigned` indefinitely: it has no age, nothing computes how long it has been unrouted, and no surface reports it. FILING IS NOT ROUTING, and today the register made those two indistinguishable. MEASURED ON THIS SESSION, and every instance was found only because the operator asked a question that happened to touch it: (1) MI-201-ALPACA-LIVE-ROSTER-EXPANSION — `ready`/`unassigned` from 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-10T08:14Z, TWO DAYS, while being the actual answer to 'why am I still not seeing any live trades'. The operator had to ask before it moved. (2) WO-20260909-DECISION-UNKNOWN-STRATEGY-PRIORITY-IS-INVERTED — the operator ANSWERED it on 2026-09-09 ('fix the constant AND map the five legs'), the answer was written into the object's TITLE while `chosen`/`answered_at` stayed None, and it reached no checklist row and no owner. Found 2026-09-10 only because the operator said 'I still haven't heard back'. Now MI-245. (3) MI-140-ALPACA-LIVE-CANNOT-PLACE — its verdict MERGED 2026-09-07 as #11271 and its row read `state: queued` / `status: in_flight` for three days after. Different proximate cause (MI-237's two status fields) and the SAME outcome: a settled thing that no surface reported as settled. !! AND A FOURTH, ON THE FILE ITSELF: this checklist's `cycle` field declared CY-20260903-MANAGER-CONTROL, superseded 2026-09-06 — so the manager's own state of record carried the wrong named priority for four days and nothing noticed.
items.what_this_is_not: NOT another reminder, and NOT more documentation. The operator's point is EXECUTION: "we actually finish things and execute them". A row saying 'the manager should route filed rows promptly' is precisely the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for twice on MI-15. Whatever is built must SURFACE or REFUSE without anyone choosing to look. NOT a licence to auto-route either: spawning against an unread row is worse than leaving it, and the operator's cap of 3 is deliberate.
items.the_shape_that_would_have_caught_all_fou: They differ in proximate cause and share one property: a row whose STATE stopped matching reality, with no elapsed-time term anywhere. So the candidate mechanism is an AGE on the state transition — `state_since` — plus a surface that reports rows whose state has held longer than that state should last. `ready` for two days is a finding; `in_flight` owned by a dead session is a finding (MI-236); `blocked` past its blocker's clearance is a finding (MI-235). ⚠️ ESTABLISH THE THRESHOLDS FROM THE DATA, not by choosing round numbers — measure how long rows ACTUALLY hold each state before they move, and state the population. ⚠️ AND IT MUST DISTINGUISH `we did not look` FROM `nothing is stale`: a surface that cannot say which is which reproduces the collapsed-state class this repo has a guard family for.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) A row that has held `ready`/`unassigned` past a measured threshold is SURFACED somewhere a manager reads before it plans — not in a 5.1 MB backlog, and not behind a command someone must choose to run. (2) It is OBSERVED catching one: a real unrouted row is reported before the operator asks about it. !! (2) IS THE WHOLE POINT AND (1) DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE — every mechanism in this family has shipped and then not been read; that is what OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION and OI-20260902-ROLE-PACKS-... both still record. !! A GREEN GUARD CLEARS (1) ONLY. !! AND IF THE ANSWER IS THAT MI-235/MI-236/MI-237 SUBSUME THIS ONCE BUILT, that is a legitimate finding — say so and CLOSE this row explicitly rather than leaving a fourth near-duplicate accruing, which is itself the class.
items.blocked_on_basis: ASSESSED — nothing blocks it. It is deliberately NOT blocked on MI-237: the schema migration would give the field a home, but the missing thing is an elapsed-time term and a surface, which do not depend on it.

All three packages since the roster was armed 2026-08-31 were SHORT and are unexecutable AT THE VENUE, before side_filter is consulted — so the manager's earlier relay (that the operator-directed side_filter: long gate was the suppressor) was true but pointed at the wrong remedy: DROPPING THE GATE WOULD BUY ZERO TRADES. And the incumbent's LONG side fired 18x in June, 2x in July, 13x in August and 0x in September — it went quiet the day before the account was armed. ⚠️ THE ORDER PATH REMAINS UNTESTED, NOT PROVEN WORKING: zero long signals have ever reached it, so this change may be what first exercises it.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The four legs are on config/accounts.yaml::alpaca_live.strategies and the PR is MERGED — Tier-3, so R4 bars self-landing whatever the approval state; a human clicks merge and the approval must NOT be re-sought. (2) DEPLOYED — /api/diag/version shows the merge commit as git_sha and git_sha_on_disk with restart_pending false. (3) OBSERVED — a LONG order package from one of the four reaches the venue. ⚠️ (3) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS and may take weeks: these are 1d legs and the incumbent produced zero longs in September. Do NOT report the roster change as working on the strength of (1) or (2); a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a placed order.

MI-201 diagnosed it — SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP='alpaca_live' on the running process, and BOTH loops that could clear the latch continue on the same skip condition, so a skipped account's latch is IMMORTAL and silent_accounts() has handed every review skill a 20-day-old alerting:true. THE SKIP IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED. The fix is Tier-2 and ships separately; folding it into a Tier-3 roster PR would widen a real-money diff.

items.title: The Workflow page's decisions inbox grades on `answer` alone, so a decision answered IN CONVERSATION renders identically to one nobody answered
items.source: OPERATOR, 2026-09-10, reading the live Work page: 'i do want to point out that the page doesn't seem to be very up to date - at least an hour old and I don't think all these decisions are still waiting for me'. BOTH HALVES WERE RIGHT AND NEITHER WAS THE PAGE'S FAULT. The staleness half was the MANAGER's — MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json did not change between 84d8e2d49 (09:24:19Z) and d5fe81aed (~10:22Z) and a status update was given inside that gap, i.e. answered-before-pushing, the exact order the operator canonized. The '59m ago' banner measured that lateness accurately and this is the FIRST time the freshness contract has caught anything.
items.scope: MEASURED over every *.yaml in docs/claude/work/objects/ — 21 objects carrying 26 decision_requests. The page's 'Waiting on you' shows exactly 3 as NOT SUBMITTED and ALL THREE ARE ANSWERED: DR-20260908-SHOULD-SCRIPTS-BACKTEST-STAR-BE-IN-THE-TIER1-SURFACE (verdict approved / chosen add_it), DEC-20260910-EXIT-EVAL-60S-REMEDY (approved / r2_only), and DR-20260908-CLEAR-THE-LOUD-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-ROW (reframed_not_answered) — all answered_at 2026-09-10T07:52:00Z, and `answer` is None on all three. TWO RECORDING SHAPES FOR ONE FACT: an answer given through the SPA/Telegram POST route writes an `answer` block; an answer given IN CONVERSATION is recorded by hand as verdict + chosen + answered_at + answered_by. The inbox knows only the first, so 'nobody answered' and 'answered through the other channel' render IDENTICALLY. That is a collapsed state on the surface built to prevent collapsed states, and its cost is the panel's credibility, which is the entire point of the panel.
items.resolution_criteria: The page distinguishes AT LEAST answered_via_route / answered_in_conversation / reframed_not_answered / genuinely_unanswered / unknown, names WHICH channel carried each answer, and the three rows above no longer read NOT SUBMITTED — verified by the OPERATOR on the deployed page, not by a local harness. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT BE FIXED BY TREATING ANY `verdict` AS ANSWERED: reframed_not_answered is a real verdict meaning the question was NOT answered, and collapsing it into 'answered' would hide a genuinely open decision — worse than the bug. ⚠️ THE STALENESS BANNER MUST NOT BE SOFTENED as part of this; it was correct.
items.status_note: In flight with MI-238 since 11:33Z. The operator re-confirmed the symptom at ~11:40Z with a screenshot of the deployed page: three NOT SUBMITTED / ROUTINE rows, all three already answered, plus a 'BLOCKING YOU, WITH NO ANSWERABLE REQUEST ATTACHED (3)' list. #11683 (merged 11:42:39Z) cleared TWO of those three blocking rows and this branch clears the THIRD, so that list should go to zero. The three NOT SUBMITTED rows are MI-254's own subject and remain until it lands.
