items.title: 12 checklist items have `state` and `status` disagreeing, and 38 carry values outside the declared vocabulary — on the page the operator reads
items.owner: unassigned — route when a lane frees; the 3-lane cap is holding
items.source: MEASURED by the manager 2026-09-10T12:0xZ, from the LIVE operator-facing route GET /api/bot/work/checklist (which is what the Workflow page renders) and re-derived directly against the file. Population: all 260 items. The route's own summary reports byBasis {state_only: 179, status_only: 64, agree: 5, disagree: 12}, offDeclaredVocabulary 38, unsectioned 18. This is MI-237's two-competing-status-fields defect, still live at ITEM level after being fixed at HEADER level.
items.scope: TWELVE items where `state` and `status` contradict each other. NINE read state=in_flight or state=queued while status=done — i.e. nine items that render as OPEN on the operator's page and are finished (MI-135, MI-136, MI-138, MI-139, MI-143, MI-144, MI-145, MI-146, MI-147). ⚠️ ONE READ THE OTHER WAY AND THAT IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: MI-179-TLT-5414-REARM-56-NAKED-SHARES carried state=done / status=blocked — a PROTECTION row reading FINISHED while another field said BLOCKED. The manager resolved that one in this same commit against a live venue read; the other eleven are NOT resolved and must not be guessed. ELEVEN OFF-VOCABULARY VALUES across 38 items, against a declared vocabulary of exactly {blocked, done, dropped, in_flight, landed_unproven, queued, triage}: `ready` x20, `superseded` x5, `deferred` x2, `waiting` x2, `unassigned` x2, `operator_approved` x2, `filed_not_taken` x2, `filed`, `failed`, `duplicate_of_MI-180`, `needs_redispatch_premise_is_wrong`. The last two are FREE PROSE IN A TYPED FIELD — a status that is a sentence cannot be counted, filtered or rendered.
items.resolution_criteria: ONE status field per item, on ONE declared vocabulary, with the page's `disagree` count at 0 and `offDeclaredVocabulary` at 0 — read off GET /api/bot/work/checklist, not off a local harness. ⚠️ EACH OF THE ELEVEN REMAINING DISAGREEMENTS MUST BE RESOLVED AGAINST EVIDENCE, ONE AT A TIME, NEVER BY PREFERRING ONE FIELD WHOLESALE. Nine happen to point the same way, which is exactly the reasoning that would have got MI-179 wrong — it points the other way. ⚠️ AND A VALUE BEING OFF-VOCABULARY IS NOT LICENCE TO DELETE THE DISTINCTION IT CARRIES: `ready`, `waiting` and `deferred` are three different facts and collapsing them into `queued` would destroy information to satisfy a schema. Either widen the declared vocabulary deliberately or map each value with its reason recorded.

items.title: A decision request keeps rendering as 'waiting on you' after the thing it asks about no longer exists — measured at >24h on a `done` object
items.owner: unassigned — belongs with MI-238/MI-254 (same surface, different defect)
items.source: MEASURED 2026-09-10T12:5xZ by the manager, after putting the question to the operator and only THEN discovering it was moot. DR-20260908-CLEAR-THE-LOUD-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-ROW asks whether to remove OI-20260831-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-IS-LIVE-BUT-UNPROVEN-AND-ITS-AB-HARNESS-DOES-NOT-EXIST. That row was removed from docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json on 2026-09-09T10:34:23+0300 by ba5fccc1a (#11509). Established by `git log -S` over the file, and by confirming the row is absent at 001b842bb and every head since — not by reading the PR title. The request kept rendering on the operator's Workflow page as work waiting on them for MORE THAN A DAY.
items.scope: THIS IS NOT MI-254 AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. MI-254 fixed HOW an answer state is GRADED — it taught the inbox that a conversationally-recorded verdict is an answer. This is a different defect one level up: NOTHING CHECKS WHETHER THE REQUEST'S SUBJECT STILL EXISTS. A perfectly graded question about a deleted row is still a question that should not be on the operator's screen. ⚠️ AND THE OBJECT'S OWN LIFECYCLE ALREADY READ `done` — so the surface is not even consulting the one field that was already telling it the truth. WO-20260908-BUILD-THE-N-BOOK-RANKING-KEY-HARNESS is `lifecycle: done` and its request still rendered as open. That is the cheapest possible check and it is not being made. ⚠️ THE POPULATION IS UNKNOWN AND MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT: this is one confirmed instance out of 26 requests across 21 objects. How many of the other 25 ask about a row, PR, file or branch that no longer exists is NOT established, and 1-of-26 is not a rate.
items.resolution_criteria: The page distinguishes a request whose SUBJECT is gone from one genuinely awaiting an answer, and the operator is not shown the former as work. ⚠️ THREE STATES AT MINIMUM, NEVER COLLAPSED: `subject_live` · `subject_gone` · **`subject_unknown` — we could not check**. The third is the one that matters: a subject reference the grader cannot resolve must NOT default to `gone` (that silently hides a real question) nor to `live` (that reproduces this bug). ⚠️ AND `lifecycle: done` ON THE PARENT OBJECT IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN to suppress a request — an object can be done while a decision it raised is genuinely still open, and suppressing on that alone would hide real questions. It is EVIDENCE, not the test. ⚠️ A SUPPRESSED REQUEST MUST STILL BE READABLE somewhere — moving it out of 'waiting on you' is not deleting it; a question that was asked and became moot is a record, and the reason it became moot is the useful part.

items.title: Operator decision: salvage the three unrecoverable automation artifacts, close the nine superseded ones
items.owner: manager — a merge-queue disposition, which is management; no build follows
items.source: OPERATOR ANSWERED ~2026-09-10T13:20Z on a pop-up: 'Rescue the 3, close the 9', over 'close all twelve and accept the loss' and over 'fix #11519 first, then let it drain'. Put to them after the manager discovered it had reported the merge queue EMPTY while 20 PRs were open.
items.scope: MEASURED over all 12 stuck automation PRs. ONE COMMON CAUSE: every one touches docs/claude/session-board.json, which — unlike the five append-only registers — carries NO merge driver at all in .gitattributes, so it is a BARE conflict. R13 forces every armed branch to claim merge_slot there, so each automation PR conflicts with every other the moment one lands, and nothing re-drives them once the producing run exits. That is #11519's diagnosis with a population. NINE ARE SUPERSEDED and merging them would REGRESS data: main's WORK-DIGEST generated_at is 2026-09-10T11:17:59Z against the oldest PR's 2026-09-09T07:40:34Z, and both gld-compat runs are already covered (main 77 rows; the two PRs 77 and 66). THREE CARRY ARTIFACTS ABSENT FROM MAIN THAT CANNOT BE REGENERATED: comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-09/INDEX.json and .../2026-09-10/INDEX.json (dated packets — the next run writes a later date, never these), and comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260910T002941Z.fxstreet.json plus its 435 rows in comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl — a POINT-IN-TIME capture, where a later re-fetch returns REVISED consensus, i.e. exactly the lookahead the macro discipline forbids.
items.resolution_criteria: The three artifacts are on main byte-identical to what their producing runs wrote, and the nine superseded PRs are CLOSED with the reason recorded on each. ⚠️ THE RESCUE IS BY VALUE, NOT BY MERGE, and its provenance must stay honest: these files arrive in a manager commit rather than from their producing run. Byte-identity was ASSERTED against `git rev-parse <branch>:<path>` for all three rather than assumed, and the snapshots.jsonl append was resolved as a VERIFIED UNION (main 17540 unique / PR 17975 unique / 0 rows only on main / 435 only in the PR / union 17975 with no duplicates), so nothing of main's was overwritten. ⚠️ CLOSING THE NINE DOES NOT FIX THE CLASS. #11519 is still stuck and is still the mechanism; this clears the pile it was supposed to prevent, and does not prevent the next one.
items.⚠️_the_population_was_43_NOT_12_correcte: ⚠️ THIS ROW SAID 'all 12 stuck automation PRs' AND THAT NUMBER IS WRONG. DO NOT RE-QUOTE IT. MEASURED 2026-09-10T13:2xZ with an explicit perPage=100: there are 48 OPEN PRs, of which 43 are AUTOMATION, oldest 2026-09-08. The '12' was the first PAGE of a default-20 listing minus this session's own lane PRs — a number I reported as a population without checking for a second page. That is the SECOND time in one session I stated a queue size I had not measured (the first was 'the merge queue is empty' while 20 were open). The merge-driver finding explains the CONFLICT mechanism; it does not explain either of these, which were unmeasured assertions. THE OPERATOR'S DECISION STILL GOVERNS AND WAS NOT RE-SOUGHT: rescue what cannot be regenerated, close what is superseded. It simply applies to a larger population than it was put on. BY PRODUCER: reconcile-open-prs 13 · session-reaper 8 · work-digest 7 · error-feed-digest 6 · data-commit receipts 4 · econ-calendar(PIT) 1 · m28-valuation(PIT) 1 · strategy-reviews(DATED) 1 · constraint-readout 1 · due-list 1 · probe-results 1. ⚠️ THE MOST-STUCK PRODUCER IS THE ONE THAT RECONCILES THE OPEN-PR LIST. Every merge to main fires it, it opens a PR, that PR conflicts on session-board.json, and the next merge fires another — it has been generating its own backlog for two and a half days, and OPEN-PRS.json is the file that carries operator decisions WITH THEIR CONDITIONS. The register meant to track the queue is the single biggest thing stuck in it. DONE SO FAR: 9 closed with an individually measured reason (#11684 #11672 #11525 #11620 #11664 #11662 #11595 #11541 #11654 #11536 #11518 #11512 — the four work-digest and two gld-compat checked row-by-row rather than swept). 3 artifacts rescued in #11697. STILL OWED: 34 automation PRs undispositioned, and THREE MORE UNRECOVERABLE ARTIFACTS found in the wider population and NOT yet rescued — a second PIT econ capture (US-20260909T002929Z), the m28 valuation snapshots, and the 2026-09-08 strategy-review packet. ⚠️ NOT TAKEN BY THE MANAGER, DELIBERATELY: 34 per-PR content checks is an ITEM. It needs a fresh OPS session, which would be a FOURTH lane against the operator's cap of 3, so it is QUEUED and documented rather than started. The disposition rule is written above and is reusable: rescue PIT/dated artifacts by value with byte-identity asserted, resolve append-only files as a verified union, close regenerated snapshots and receipts.

items.title: Operator approved ARMING the stale-automation sweeper (#11519). Rebase dispatched; the manager merges by hand.
items.source: operator decision, 2026-09-10 ~13:5xZ, verbatim: "Yes — rebase it and I'll merge." Put as a pop-up with three options; the chosen one was the recommendation.
items.scope: REBASE ONLY, then a hand merge. #11519 registers itself in LANDING_MACHINERY, so R12 holds it for a human and R4 bars it from self-landing whatever its approval state. hold_reason 'changes_landing_machinery' is HONEST and stays exactly as it is — do not rewrite it to get past the guard.
items.⚠️_what_merging_this_ARMS: A 2-hourly cron (.github/workflows/stale-automation-sweep.yml) that force-pushes automation branches with a PAT and lands them on green. THE MECHANISM HAS NEVER RUN UNATTENDED. The PR's own body states it: 'Every run was hand-run. The workflow is not on main, so it has no cron: the SCRIPT is proven, the MECHANISM is not.' The operator was told this risk in the pop-up and approved anyway. Merging is the arming; running a pass is a SEPARATE act and is NOT covered by this approval.
items.⚠️_why_it_is_worth_the_risk: It is the root fix for the class, not the pile. Measured 2026-09-10T13:36Z with an explicit perPage=100: 43 of 48 open PRs are stranded automation branches (I first said TWELVE — that was the first page of a default-20 list minus my own lane PRs, and the correction is recorded on MI-259). One common cause: docs/claude/session-board.json carries NO merge driver, so every armed branch's R13 merge_slot claim conflicts bare with every other. THAT DEFECT HIT THIS MANAGER'S OWN PR #11697 AT 13:5xZ WHILE ITS CI WAS GREEN — the seventh takeover today — which is the strongest available evidence the class is real and recurring.
items.resolution_criteria: THREE PARTS, different facts — say which you cleared. (1) The rebase lands: the corrected merge check `git -c merge.jsonregister.driver=false merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` exits 0, and the union of docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json is VERIFIED (base 1426 / main 1433 / PR 1431; target 1438 if no ids overlap — measure, do not assume; 0 rows lost from either side, no duplicate ids). (2) The manager MERGES it by hand — not auto-merge, not the lane. (3) A SCHEDULED run of stale-automation-sweep.yml is OBSERVED completing and its effect verified as EFFECT (merge-base equal to main's tip on a branch it refreshed), never from the sweeper's own report. ⚠️ (3) MAY NOT BE CLEARABLE FOR HOURS — the cron is 2-hourly and this repo's scheduled workflows fire LATE and ERRATICALLY (probes.yml ~4h50m late; work-digest 5 firings against 24 declared). Read the run history, NEVER the cron expression. ⚠️ A workflow_dispatch run clears (3) NOT AT ALL: dispatch is what is already proven and a cron that does not fire is the failure class. ⚠️ A GREEN CI RUN CLEARS NOTHING — 21 tests pass in a harness and a harness cannot reach a cron. ⚠️ AND MERGING CLEARS ONLY (2): a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a run.
items.⚠️_what_this_does_NOT_fix: A FIFTH strand mode the sweeper does not cover, stated in its own body: when the producing run exhausts the shared user API quota, `gh pr create` fails and the branch is pushed with NO PR at all. The sweeper enumerates OPEN PRs, so such a branch is invisible to it — the premise is right and the INPUT SET is wrong. Also unfixed: 34 automation PRs remain undispositioned, and three more unrecoverable artifacts are NOT yet rescued (the US-20260909T002929Z econ capture, the m28 valuation snapshots, the 2026-09-08 strategy-review packet).

items.title: #11648 (MI-139) looks green, has never run CI, and carries three conflicts including CLAUDE.md
items.owner: unassigned — needs a lane; NOT the manager (it touches CLAUDE.md, a worker path)
items.source: manager merge-queue sweep, 2026-09-10T14:0xZ
items.scope: Open since 2026-09-10T07:08:09Z. MEASURED: get_check_runs returns total_count 1 and the ONE run is `open-and-automerge`, conclusion success. That is the documented GITHUB_TOKEN trap -- claude-pr-automerge OPENED the PR itself, so no `pull_request` event ever fired and the four real checks never will. ⚠️ IT READS AS GREEN AT A GLANCE, which is why it sat seven hours. Remedy is one ORDINARY commit pushed by a session (never an empty commit -- prohibited).

items.⚠️_do_not_read_this_as_a_bug_in_the_bann: The mechanism works and its own reported age was accurate to the minute. ⚠️ AND A MANAGER ERROR IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN DROPPED: I first read the payload for `ageHours`, got None from a missing key, and was about to file 'the banner cannot compute an age'. The field is `commitAgeHours`. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A committed by the READER -- the label I looked for named a quantity the accessor did not return -- and it was caught only by dumping the raw block instead of trusting the parse.
items.resolution_criteria: The banner is OBSERVED warning on a checklist older than 15 minutes and NOT warning on a fresher one — read off the deployed page, not off the constant. ⚠️ A green test clears nothing here: the question is whether the operator can see lateness, and only the rendered page answers it. The separate treeState defect (synced / treeBehindCommits: 0 while the VM is a commit behind) is part of this row and needs its own observation — a tree that is behind must not read `synced`.
items.⚠️_a_SECOND_freshness_signal_has_the_sam: MEASURED 2026-09-10T15:0xZ on the live route: freshness read treeState 'synced' with treeBehindCommits 0 WHILE the VM was genuinely one commit behind main (treeHeadSha c69b1b4ac against main 158effe7aa). Its own treeNote is honest -- 'level with the local origin/main ref (this never fetches)' -- so nothing is hidden, but the STATE NAME and the COUNT both read as up-to-date while meaning 'up to date with whatever we last pulled'. A VM that stopped fetching entirely would read synced / 0 behind indefinitely. Same subject as this row (what the page's freshness signalling tells the operator), so folded in rather than filed separately. ⚠️ NOT ITSELF EVIDENCE OF A FAULT: on this occasion ict-git-sync caught up within ~6 minutes, CONFIRMED by polling the live page to 266 items at 15:08:02Z. The finding is what the signal COULD hide, not what it did.

items.⚠️_OPERATOR_DECIDED_2026_09_10_FIFTEEN_M: DEC-20260910-WORKFLOW-PAGE-STALENESS-THRESHOLD. Asked as a pop-up by manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj offering ~1h (recommended), leave it at 3.0h, or a number of their own. THE OPERATOR CHOSE NEITHER OFFERED OPTION AND TYPED '15 min' — TIGHTER THAN THE OPTION I RECOMMENDED, which is worth recording as such rather than rounding to the nearest thing I proposed. So the Workflow page's freshness banner warns at 15 MINUTES, not 3.0 hours and not 1 hour. ⚠️ READ WHAT THAT IMPLIES BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: the page is exactly as fresh as the manager's last PUSH plus ict-git-sync's ~5-minute pull, so at a 15-minute threshold the banner will show whenever a manager goes two sync cycles without pushing. THAT IS THE OPERATOR'S POINT, not an argument against the number — it makes manager lateness visible to THEM rather than only to a guard, which is the enforcement CLAUDE.md names. Do NOT quietly widen it back because it fires often. ⚠️ AND THE FIELD IS `commitAgeHours`, NOT `ageHours` — the manager read the wrong key on 2026-09-10 and nearly filed 'the banner cannot compute an age' as a defect; the field read 0.954 correctly. That is the unprovenanced-diagnostic trap committed by the READER, and it is recorded so the implementer does not repeat it. The second observation in this row still stands and is a SEPARATE defect: treeState read `synced` with treeBehindCommits: 0 while the VM was genuinely one commit behind main.
items.⚠️_DELIVERED_AS_11716_AND_THE_LANE_CORRE: #11716 opened 17:23Z, 25 minutes after dispatch. tier 1 / landing hold / hold_reason unvouchable_paths — R5 correctly refuses self-landing because the diff touches src/runtime/manager_status.py and src/web/api/routers/work.py, outside TIER1_SURFACE. 498 insertions over 5 files, 17 new tests all three mutation-tested, 329 passing, guards PASS 72 FAIL 0. ⚠️ I TOLD IT THE treeState DEFECT WAS PROBABLY THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS AND IT ESTABLISHED THAT IT IS NOT. All three tree states ARE emitted and branched on, and the behind==0 && head!=main case already grades `unknown`. The real defect is PROVENANCE ON THE COMPARISON BASE: behind_commits counts against the LOCAL origin/main ref, and scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh does `git fetch` then `git reset --hard origin/main`, so on the live VM that equality holds BY CONSTRUCTION — the zero is guaranteed, not measured, and TREE_BEHIND is close to unreachable in production. Its fix carries main_ref_age_hours from FETCH_HEAD's mtime (a rev-parse plus a stat, NO network call, because fetching on an API request path is the wedge class this repo has paid for twice), returning None — never 0.0 — when it cannot establish when we last fetched. Reaching for the repo's named failure class because it was nearby would have been the wrong diagnosis, and it said so rather than agreeing with the manager.
items.⚠️_criterion_2_is_NOT_met_and_the_lane_s: 'A tree that is behind reads as behind' CANNOT be met by this change: establishing that the VM is behind GITHUB requires a fetch, and the code deliberately performs none. What it delivers instead is that `synced` now states WHEN IT LAST LOOKED and warns when that is too old to justify itself. The lane declined to declare the criterion met. Criterion (1) is also NOT observed — a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a render. So this row stays open past the merge.

It is NOT this PR's problem (here the paths are genuinely unvouchable, so the honest declaration exists and is used), and it needs its own row and its own session. A manager is expected to push it before answering a status request, so this page is 25m behind whatever they are actually working on.'] — 25 minutes against a 15-minute threshold, on the DEPLOYED page, under the NEW code. items.⚠️_criterion_1_is_HALF_observed_and_the_: ⚠️ DO NOT CLOSE THIS ROW ON THE POSITIVE ALONE. The earlier clean read (2026-09-10T17:04Z, commitAgeHours 0.061, warnings []) was taken under the OLD 3.0h code, so it is NOT a valid negative control for the NEW threshold — a probe that only ever sees the stale case cannot distinguish 'correctly reported' from 'reports everything', which is the lane's own stated discipline turned on the observation rather than on the tests. What is owed is ONE read on the deployed page, under this code, with commitAgeHours < 0.25 and warnings []. Pushing this very commit and reading the route within 15 minutes produces it. ⚠️ AND CRITERION (2) IS STILL NOT MET BY THIS CHANGE AT ALL — establishing the VM is behind GITHUB needs a fetch the code deliberately does not perform. It needs its own disposition: a follow-up that establishes behind-ness, or a RECORDED operator decision that `synced` stating when it last looked is sufficient and the criterion is retired. Routed to the lane as a proposal, not decided.
items.⚠️_the_manager_own_probe_gave_a_FALSE_PO: The first deploy probe grepped the WHOLE API payload for `main_ref_age` and reported 'DEPLOYED+RENDERED' at 17:53:57Z. It was WRONG: the freshness block it printed in the same output still carried the OLD treeNote and commitSha fddf491f3, i.e. the VM had not yet pulled the merge. THE PROBE MATCHED THE MANAGER'S OWN CHECKLIST PROSE — this very row describes `main_ref_age_hours`, and the checklist text is served in that payload. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class C (an unasserted denominator) committed by the READER, and it is the SECOND time in one day a manager read this route with the wrong accessor (the first was `ageHours` vs `commitAgeHours`). The lesson is specific and reusable: ASSERT ON THE FRESHNESS BLOCK'S KEYS, never on a substring of a payload that contains our own writing about those keys. Re-armed correctly; the 17:58:55Z reading above is from the corrected probe. Nothing false was reported to the operator or the lane — the poke said 'deployed-or-will-shortly'.
items.⚠️_CRITERION_1_IS_NOW_MET_BOTH_HALVES_OB: The negative control was captured and criterion (1) is COMPLETE. Both readings are off /api/bot/work/checklist on the DEPLOYED page, under the NEW code, and they are a matched pair rather than two convenient facts: POSITIVE 2026-09-10T17:58:55Z — commitSha fddf491f3b15, commitAgeHours 0.423 (25 minutes), warnings carried 'The checklist was last COMMITTED 25m ago ... this page is 25m behind whatever they are actually working on.' NEGATIVE 2026-09-10T18:10:23Z — commitSha 27d576237d17 (#11720's own squash, verified on main by `git log origin/main`, not inferred), commitAgeHours 0.059 (3.5 minutes), mainRefAgeHours 0.017, treeState synced, warnings []. ⚠️ THE PAIRING IS THE EVIDENCE, NOT EITHER READ ALONE: a staleness banner that only ever fires cannot be distinguished from one that fires on everything, and 'reports everything' is precisely how an operator learns to walk past it. That discipline is the LANE's, stated in #11716's own body about its tests, and it is applied here to the live observation. ⚠️ THE 17:04Z CLEAN READ IS STILL NOT PART OF THIS PAIR — it predates the deploy and was taken under the OLD 3.0h threshold; using it would have looked like a control and proved nothing about the 15-minute code.

So (2) needs a DISPOSITION rather than an implementation: either a follow-up that establishes behind-ness against GitHub off the request path, or a RECORDED decision that `synced` stating when it last looked is sufficient and the criterion is retired. _merge_queue.⚠️_my_merges_clean_check_was_measuring_t: MANAGER ERROR, corrected 2026-09-10T13:1xZ by measurement. All day I asserted 'merges clean into main' from `git merge-tree --write-tree`, and for the append-only registers that measured THE WRONG THING. .gitattributes maps health-review-backlog.json, OPEN-ITEMS.json, MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, SESSIONS.json and OPEN-PRS.json to a CUSTOM merge driver (merge=jsonregister), which IS armed in this clone — and GITHUB NEVER RUNS CUSTOM MERGE DRIVERS. So the local check auto-merged via the driver and reported clean while GitHub conflicted. .gitattributes says so in terms: 'CLIENT-SIDE ONLY ... this does not make a `dirty` PR auto-mergeable on GitHub'. I did not read it before asserting. THE CORRECTED CHECK, which reproduces GitHub's view: `git -c merge.jsonregister.driver=false merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>`. Verified both ways on #11691: driver armed -> exit 0; driver disabled -> exit 1, matching GitHub's `dirty`. ⚠️ AND session-board.json IS NOT IN THAT LIST AT ALL — it has no driver, so it conflicts bare. That is the single common cause behind all 12 stuck automation PRs and behind the six merge-slot takeovers this session.
